A businessman was left fighting for his life after corrosive liquid was thrown in his face outside his home in Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings in East Sussex, has been charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30.
A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route is warning pilgrims and other visitors to stop defecating along the famous path.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze took place at a building located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. Only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The site was not a vacant facility, the officials also said. The fire reportedly started at about 1pm, and thick clouds of smoke and large, brightly burning flames were seen sweeping the building. Local resident Terry Rauh told MLive a fire took place at the building once before. An investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf, the American Civil Liberties Union said Tuesday. The federal government will give Shoshana Hebshi $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search and held her for hours.

An Asiana Airlines flight crashed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people and skidding off the runway. The plane had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, and overran the runway at 8pm local time. Local media reported that the plane had a tailstrike and spun 180 degrees before skidding off the runway. The plane had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, and overran the runway at 8pm local time. Local media reported that the plane had a tailstrike and spun 180 degrees before skidding off the runway.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old reality TV star, has a collection of 16 expensive watches, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them in an interview with the newspaper.

Actor Robert Hardy, 89, is selling his collection of antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow, and a portrait of him holding the bow, in a £100,000 auction. The collection, which he has built up thanks to his interest in classic literature and military history, is being sold by Dominic Winter auctioneers at its saleroom in South Cerney, Gloucestershire.

A Brazilian commuter took a photo of a man standing on the yellow line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, where it quickly went viral. The image was shared more than 100, 000 times in 24 hours. The man in the photo was breaking a public transport safety regulation, but the commuter was actually observing a safety rule. The post was interpreted as homophobic, but the commuter was actually warning against homophobia. The post received thousands of comments, with users praising the witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan who wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket great, almost 20 years ago, has shared the Australian cricket legend's response in the wake of his death. The letter, dated September 27, 1996, included a full sheet of notes about spin bowling for left-hand bowlers and tips on different deliveries. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler and middle-order batsman, was the first player to score 2,000 Test runs and take 200 Test wickets.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg believes that virtual reality will play a key role in the future of travel, allowing users to experience new environments and locations without the need for physical travel. Zuckerberg's views on the future of virtual travel are supported by Facebook's recent purchase of virtual reality headset maker Oculus and the company's plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed.

A couple who had planned to get married this month in Sichuan, southwest China, had to postpone the ceremony because their girlfriend Dong Hui, 22, was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to hospital. Despite her condition, Dong wanted to have wedding photographs taken for her birthday, so her boyfriend Guo Kai arranged for professional photographers to come to the hospital to take pictures. Dong chose a wedding dress with embroidered flowers and had her make-up done before posing with her husband-to-be. The couple met a year ago after a mutual friend introduced them and quickly fell in love. Guo arranged for 24 alarms on his phone to make sure he does not forget to attend to Dong's every need. The wedding and photo shoot is a dream for them all, and Dong Hui and Guo Kai both experienced the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake and understand the value of life.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions that took place within three hours in Houston.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company. The positions will be based at its Redmond campus in Washington and the program will be run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that helps train people with autism for careers in IT.

Two Tulsa deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned because of threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The shooting has been the subject of criticism, and the sheriff's office has suspended operations of the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting of Harris. The shooting has also been the subject of allegations of forgery of training records and unqualified training.

Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, is in desperate need of a lung transplant but her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Her husband, Dalton, pleaded for help, saying that his wife is struggling to negotiate her healthcare options from her hospital bed at the University of Kentucky.

The Sleep Cycle app has gathered data from over two million users in 47 countries to discover the best and worst days of the week for sleep quality. Mondays are the earliest wake-up times, with South Africa rising first at 6:09 am. Americans are in the worst mood on Tuesdays, while Wednesday nights are the best sleep quality. The US sleeps in the latest on Fridays, with an average of 8:24 am.

Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, which were written in Spanish and saved by Jose until his death in 1995, were passed down through different generations of his family until they reached the current owner.

The article discusses the controversial political stance of Unite union leader Len McCluskey, who is known for his militant tactics and socialist ideology. Despite his popularity among activists, McCluskey is seen as a threat to British politics due to his desire to impose socialist policies on the government. The article highlights the close relationship between Unite and the Labour Party, which has led to concerns about the potential for a socialist revolution within the country.

A zookeeper captured footage of animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera. The footage shows a range of drinking methods, from a rhino that almost kisses the surface of the water to a lemur that delicately licks it. The zookeeper placed the camera in the animals' water troughs and filmed them for a total of 30 hours. The footage offers a unique perspective on how different animals drink and is a humorous and educational experience for the zookeepers.
A YouGov poll suggests that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, while 43% believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight.
A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed more than 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, had been searching for him for 22 hours after the house collapsed. Sonit's face was coated in dust from the debris, but he was found uninjured and was taken to Bhaktapur Hospital.
A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a bizarre land use battle over its plans to turn a patch of secluded in woods near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center.

The article describes the transformation of Kabul, Afghanistan, into a city that is both swollen in size and shrunken in scope, with the legacy of America's longest war still present. The city's population has increased five times since NATO arrived, but the violence in the provinces has forced people to flee, leaving the city empty and deserted. The article also highlights the isolation and fear of reprisals faced by those who lost their jobs due to the decline of English-speaking skills.

Two Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, a Navy spokesman said. The two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. NBC host Rebecca Lowe, a former BBC and ESPN journalist, is helping to enhance coverage of the Premier League in America. The move has resulted in more people watching Premier League matches live in the USA than in Britain.
The Labour leader Ed Miliband has been accused of being a 'monkey' by Boris Johnson, the London Mayor, who claimed that Labour could not take power without the support of the SNP.
A prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing.

Jenson Button believes McLaren's pace has improved significantly since their Australian Grand Prix, with Fernando Alonso and he both retiring. Button is now hoping for further steps in the team's improvement, with the team still needing to work on downforce and power units.

A hospital in Western Australia was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitised medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider and fined. The hospital has been found to be continuing to operate with poorly sanitised instruments, raising concerns about patient safety.

A couple who chose to sacrifice their dream wedding in order to pay for one final shot at IVF are celebrating giving birth to twins and even found a way to say their 'I do's' Becca Litchfield, 29, and partner Dale, 30, from Gotham, Nottingham, were heart-broken when they discovered their savings would only be enough to cover the cost of a wedding, or fertility treatment.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, was hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours and caused confusion for the staff and customers, who were locked out of the page and had to wait until Facebook was contacted to regain control. The incident is believed to have occurred after an employee clicked on a link in an email that purported to be from Facebook.

A Shibu Inu puppy was filmed barking at a husky dog at an American Kennel Club centre. The video shows the two dogs barking, whining, and squeaking at one another. The puppy's vocalizations were so loud that it caused the husky to respond. The video ends with the husky losing interest and chewing on its handler's sleeve.

Liam Plunkett, a 29-year-old England seamer, is back in Test contention against the West Indies after a comeback last summer was cut short by injury. He has set his sights on using his pace to lead England to victory in the Test series. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with conditions in the West Indies.
Paul Smith, the younger brother of Liverpool's boxing greats, is set to face reigning world super-middleweight champion Andre Ward in a rematch in the UK.

Parma, Missouri, has seen a significant turnover in its police force, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor after the election of the first African American mayor. The outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, claims that the employees cited "safety concerns" in their resignations, while the new mayor, Tyrus Byrd, insists that the election of an African American mayor should be celebrated instead of focusing on the departures of city employees. The town has suffered a surge in crime, and residents believe that the departure of the police force has not negatively impacted the community.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the club are set to make the Ivorian available this summer. The Ivorian has played a major role during City's recent trophy-laden period and is in no rush to leave. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, are interested but given his huge wages there are some doubts. City, meanwhile, will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, but instead may have other psychiatric disorders. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of people taking SSRIs did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a 28-year-old woman who killed herself last month, has revealed how her daughter's mental illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death, and said her daughter was "the bravest person I have ever known." Fuller's daughter, Natalie, had a close relationship with her mother and collaborated on a parenting guide based on her honesty. However, Natalie's mental illness worsened over years, and she eventually decided to stop taking her medication, which brought her troubles back, even more acute than before.

A 10-year-old boy nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. Koby Hodder's heart stopped for a staggering 12 minutes after he collapsed while running around with friends during the morning break. He was playing British Bulldog, a game in which children run from one side of a playing field to another without being caught by one of the 'bulldogs', who often employ forceful tactics to trap runners, including rugby tackling opponents to the ground.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, wants to see the bitterness taken out of most matrimonial disputes by removing the need for allegations of adultery and blame in divorce laws. She also wants couples to be made to sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce, with a one-year 'cooling off period' after declaring that their marriage has permanently broken down.

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could enable them to become the home of a new NFL London franchise. The stadium, due to be completed for the start of the 2018-19 season, could involve a 'slide-out' grass football pitch with an NFL-style synthetic surface housed underneath. The NFL is said to be within five years of having a permanent franchise in London, and teams are looking at how quickly they can have their players back in the USA and ready to play again.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA president Sepp Blatter, calling for Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup because of its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including Republican John McCain, are urging FIFA to move the global competition.

Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on Feb. 10, 2017, and the third film in the series will debut Feb. 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, who is married and has two sons with the British author, will write the script for the second film. James, whose real name is Erika Leonard, has been credited with keeping a strong amount of creative control when it comes to Universal's adaptations of her books.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace on Saturday but in the midst of yet another relegation battle for the 57-year-old, he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League. Pulis has never finished higher than 11th, achieved in 2009/10 with Stoke and 20013/14 with Palace. Pulis took Stoke into the Premier League and turned them into an established team. Pulis has a top-five finish at Newcastle United on his cv.

The Turkish Super Lig championship has been suspended following a gun attack on Fenerbahce's team bus on Saturday night. The bus driver was wounded and taken to the hospital, but no other injuries were reported. The club has called for the suspension of the championship until the attackers are caught and punished.

A massive avalanche struck the Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The avalanche struck at the height of the climbing season, when many climbers were in the area. The avalanche was caused by aftershocks from the Nepal earthquake, which killed more than 4,300 people. The climbers who were higher up Everest appeared to have avoided the deadly avalanche that struck Base Camp, but many -- estimated to be in the hundreds -- could not descend on their own. The climbers can't head down because the dangerous Khumbu Icefall has been ravaged by a series of aftershocks.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit who fought in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, found himself again surrounded by war in Ukraine. Margolin, who survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house on February 10. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews has brought 600 Jews to Israel since December, including Margolin.

John Carver, who was assistant to Ruud Gullit in 1999, is relishing the chance to take charge of Newcastle United against Sunderland on Sunday. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer in the 1999 derby led to Newcastle's defeat and Gullit's downfall. Carver believes a positive result could help him win the head coach position beyond the end of the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning. He preached at the Charity Missionary Baptist Church and addressed the Scott case and the need for reform around national policing legislation during his sermon. Sharpton wrote on Facebook: 'Joining us this morning is Mayor Keith Summey, Sheriff Al Cannon, Senator Marlon Kimpson, SCLC Leader Michael Steele, North Charleston Police [Chief] Eddie Driggers, and Assistant Police Chief Reggie Burgess.'

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversies, including his alleged use of nitrous oxide and shisha pipe, after the forward scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Rodgers said that Sterling's behaviour would be dealt with internally and that he would be speaking to him. Sterling could have had more goals and at one point shot wide with the goal gaping. Rodgers said that lack of a second goal for Sterling would have left his player disappointed at Anfield. Sterling is a valuable player who wants to learn and improve himself, and he will learn from the last six to 12 months at Liverpool.

Union donations to Labour have swelled the party's election war chest, with the party receiving more than £1 every second from trades unions in the second week of the election campaign. Labour received £1.1 million in donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservative party, which received just £492,512.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight were stranded at Manchester Airport for five hours after their plane was diverted to Birmingham due to strong winds. The flight was unable to land at Manchester due to the operating crew exceeding their legal flying hours. Passengers were eventually allowed off the aircraft and bused to Manchester, where they were left waiting for transport.
Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300million Las Vegas mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

For-profit colleges are being shut down by the U.S. Department of Education, which has curtailed their access to federal student aid. Corinthian Colleges Inc., which once enrolled more than 70,000 students, is one of the worst of the "predator colleges" that offer dubious degrees, saddle students with high amounts of debt, and gobble up tens of billions of dollars in federal money every year. The closure of Corinthian is a positive development in a long struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable.

Bayern Munich boss Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola played down the feud, saying it was his decision and injuries are part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years and was a world leader in his field.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top on the eve of his world title defence against undefeated Bryant Jennings. The 39-year-old Ukrainian superstar will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years when he takes on the slick Philadelphian at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. Klitschko, who has been reminiscing about how it all started for him when he won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, believes age has no bearing on how long he can go on for.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has admitted he will miss fronting the BBC2 show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said it would be 'great' if she were invited back to front Top Gear. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract.

Celta Vigo striker Fabian Orellana was given a straight red card for throwing a lump of grass at Barcelona midfielder Sergio Busquets during the closing stages of the match. The incident led to Busquets grabbing his eye, and the referee gave Orellana his marching orders. Despite the incident, Barcelona earned a crucial three points against Celta Vigo.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the finish line of the Boston Marathon. In 2015, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was convicted of using weapons of mass destruction, bombing a place of public use, conspiracy, and aiding and abetting. The sentencing phase of his trial began on April 21, and the judge warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events or gatherings related to the anniversary or the current running of the Boston Marathon.

The annual Qingming Festival, also known as Tomb Sweeping Day, is a three-day holiday in China that marks the start of spring and the beauty of nature. The festival is celebrated by millions of Chinese people who travel home to their ancestral villages to clean their tombs, burn fake paper money, and leave food and drink for their loved ones in the afterlife. The festival also includes parades, outdoor celebrations, and traditional dances. The festival is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and is believed to have originated in the Tang Dynasty.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from Simon's 50-year career, including hits from his days with Simon & Garfunkel, has outsold more youthful musicians such as Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping to propel him to the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas insists he will stay at Real Madrid even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper at the Bernabeu. The 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking in to the side as a 16-year-old in 1996 - before becoming the youngest Champions League keeper in 2000.
Britain has created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU put together, according to the International Monetary Fund, which praised Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy.

SsangYong, a Korean car manufacturer, is launching a new sports utility vehicle called the Tivoli SUV in the UK. The Tivoli SUV is priced from £12,950 and comes in three trim levels, with a choice of front-wheel drive or 'intelligent' 4x4. It is powered by 1.6 litre Euro 6 petrol and diesel engines with six speed manual and automatic transmissions. The Tivoli SUV is expected to double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 a year.

A chef has created a 10in-tall, half-kilogram burger piled with six forms of three different meats and containing a whopping 2,000 calories. The Whole Damn Farm, which costs £13. 50, is the creation of Sam Longhurst, head chef of Splendid Kitchen, Manchester.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, which serves meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef, has opened its doors to the public. The canteen, which serves only organic and locally sourced produce, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now feeling much better and is back home with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille.

New York's Fifth Avenue was a sea of bizarre hats on Sunday as people celebrated Easter, with some wearing outlandish headgear and others sporting more conservative attire. The parade featured a variety of headpieces, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets, as well as more traditional Easter attire.

Emergency crews in Essex were called to a call about a person being run over by a car in Epping Forest, but the caller revealed the 'victim' was actually a squirrel. The East of England ambulance service has received 1,248 inappropriate calls in the last two years, with front-line crews attending almost half of them.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake teamed up with Loic Remy and Willian to take part in Audi's football challenge. The players took on each other in a series of challenges, including shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range and sinking balls into convertible Audi's from long range. Hazard and Ake won the first two rounds, but Willian and Remy won the final round. Willian's long-range effort smashed the wing mirror of one of the Audi's, causing damage to the car.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers has criticised Raheem Sterling's agent, Aidy Ward, for allegedly trying to manipulate the player's decision to leave the club. Rodgers has sat down with Sterling since the player gave an interview last week, in which he admitted he was flattered by Arsenal's interest in him. Sterling has rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season. Rodgers believes that Liverpool Football Club is the best place for Sterling to develop his football career and financially.

Rachel Riley, Countdown co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode of the show when contestants offered up a rather rude eight-letter word as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as a blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word 'erection'.
A 16-year-old boy who was seized in an anti-terror operation after he tried to buy deadly poison on the internet has been spared jail after the court heard he wanted to commit suicide.

Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four who died three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy, was taken to North Manchester General Hospital by ambulance after suffering two previous stillbirths and three premature pregnancies. The hospital called in independent experts to review its maternity units after the spate of 10 deaths in the eight-month period from December 2013 to July last year. Ms Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, has called for action to prevent further tragedies at the hospital.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, who gave birth to her second child just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant, has been congratulated by the official Australian Olympic team's Twitter and her former agency PACE Sports Management. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while she was pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said that Pittman trained every second day and was careful to monitor her core temperature throughout her training program.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing people. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused damage to boats and people, and the race was canceled.

Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. The combination of the two is terrible, as macular degeneration takes away her central vision, and glaucoma is taking away her peripheral vision. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.
A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of an Australian college baseball player who was killed while out for a jog.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his team's poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their chances of beating Chelsea on Sunday. Wenger has lost seven of his 12 games against Mourinho, but he believes the result will be determined by the performance on the day. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces, and Wenger expects his team to nullify these. Chelsea is currently 10 points behind Arsenal in the Premier League, but Wenger believes they have a chance to catch up.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in the world of sports after a series of major fights and another one scheduled for Saturday night against Floyd Mayweather at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before being given his chance on the big stage in 2001. He left home at the age of 14 to pursue his boxing career in Manila, where he trained at the LM Gym and won his first 10 professional bouts in 1995.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has warned young footballers that they have a duty to look after their bodies. The Arsenal manager said alcohol was described as poison and that players should eat what's required to refuel, not for pleasure. Wenger said that when he sees Jack Grealish play, he's no surprise that he is full of confidence.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery to look like reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men who pelted him with eggs on Easter Monday. The attack was believed to be targeted because he had checked in at a pub on Facebook minutes earlier. Sam had also been subjected to online abuse about his appearance.

A university in Indiana was on lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. The university issued a warning to students to shelter in place and continued to repost the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message. The person was possibly armed with explosives, according to the university.

Edinson Cavani, a player known as El Matador, prepares for Paris Saint-Germain's quarter-final clash with Barcelona. If PSG are to progress beyond the Champions League's last eight, Cavani must torment the stars from Catalonia.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight at Echo Arena in Liverpool. Mathews, who saw Richar Abril and Ismael Barroso both pull out of a fight due to illness, was given a unanimous points decision of 114-112, 114-112, 115-112. Mathews, known for his relentless style, kept Luis contained behind the jab while landing a decent uppercut at the end of the second round. Luis, who was drafted in at the last minute, showed aggression in the closing rounds but was unable to overcome Mathews' superior performance.

Hull, who were in the wars against Wigan last week, recorded a shock 28-20 victory over St Helens at Langtree Park. Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, and Hull's Jordan Rankin added the extras. The win was Hull's first since the Good Friday derby defeat to Hull KR.

The U.S. Census Bureau has projected that the undocumented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, and 82% of the population by 2060. The report from the Center for Immigration Studies (CIS) said that the undocumented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, and 82% of the population by 2060.

Arsenal's Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury in the Under 21s match against Reading, but the Gunners were unable to prevent a 1-0 defeat. Wilshere was joined by other injured first team players, including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby, who managed to last 56 minutes. The match was won by Reading's Martin Keown's son, Niall, who scored the eventual winner with a header in the opening minutes.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has been struggling with his game recently, but he has been working hard on the practice ground. He has been hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and has signed for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose is optimistic that his decline will prove temporary and that he is going in the right direction again.

A Mayfair mansion that was once a milking parlour has gone on the market for £25million. The property, which is decorated with modern furnishings and features a private lift and guest cloakroom, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank. The mansion, which is on the market for £25million, is being sold for £25million by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is stronger for their recent injury troubles, according to Thomas Muller, who believes the team will be able to build a strong unit on the pitch with the players who are there. Muller and Robert Lewandowski will rely heavily on their scoring prowess in the absence of Arjen Robben and Franck Ribery as they look to become the first team to beat Porto in the Champions League this season.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base on Thursday to discuss a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that he was worried by Sebastian Vettel's Malaysian Grand Prix victory, which was won by 8. 5 seconds. Mercedes had previously dominated the season-opening race in Australia, but Vettel's victory in Malaysia suggests that the team may not be as dominant as they had hoped.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable. The bill, which was signed on Friday, is the first time nitrogen gas has been used in an execution in the United States. The process is said to cause a quick loss of consciousness and death from lack of oxygen. The bill, which was authored by Rep. Mike Christian, has been met with criticism from the Death Penalty Information Center, which argues that the same "painless" argument has been used to advance the use of lethal injections.

Bafetimbi Gomis, the French striker for Swansea, tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after scoring twice in the club's 3-1 victory over Hull. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9. The EA Sports PPI measures a player's contribution to the success of his team and removes any opinion bias.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and leaving 13 missing. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. More than 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. The drug, called olaparib, works by blocking the cancer cell's ability to repair damage, targeting only cells with genetic defects. The study found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, stopping prostate cancer growth and improving responses in medical scans. The drug could extend the length of time that a prostate cancer patient lives with the disease without it getting worse.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, Taylor has built relationships with hotels and PR companies over the past seven years, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and hotels and write reviews. She has photographed and reviewed hotels in countries such as Indonesia, the US, and Mexico, and has generated further income by featuring products from companies that sell travel products on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death after getting caught up in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water in the nature reserve.

The Football Association is investigating the incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. QPR are unlikely to face disciplinary action, but the FA will seek observations from each club and ensure that QPR and the police are taking the necessary steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and for them to face a banning order.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Saskatchewan, Canada. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not say how he died, they did say that it was not a homicide. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the family as 'very quiet' and 'hard working.' The family is now trying to raise money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, lost her frontbench job after tweeting a picture of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, while renting out a property she bought from a housing association. She has come out against David Cameron's pledge to extend the right to buy policy from council tenants to those in housing association homes.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was attacked by protesters armed with iron bars during a hunt, despite the police having evidence of the attackers. The police have dropped the investigation, angering the victim and his supporters.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. The 21-year-old has been linked with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea but he says remaining at the Mestalla is his preferred option. Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table.

An Australian teenager was raped twice by a man she met on a Christmas Eve holiday in Bali, according to Channel 9's A Current Affair. The alleged attacker, Henry Alafu, lured the teenager to his remote home and then assaulted her in a taxi as she tried to flee. The family believed Alafu had attacked their daughter, but the teenager claimed he had lured her to his home and raped her twice. CCTV footage captured Alafu waiting in the lobby for the teenager before the alleged attack took place.

The former Made in Chelsea star Ashley James has joined forces with animal rights crusaders PETA on a hard-hitting anti-fur campaign directed at Harvey Nichols after the national department store abandoned its ten-year anti-fur policy. Harvey Nichols, which has 12 locations around the world and previously stood against the fur industry, backtracked last year when it quietly re-introduced it.

Chile has joined several of its South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples, such as not being allowed to visit partners in hospital, make medical decisions on their behalf or decide what to do with their remains.
Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history as they prepare to break the record of most days at the summit of the table in a single season.

Cape Verde, a small country off the coast of West Africa, is known for its rich musical heritage, which has been a key part of its economy for decades. The country has been seeking to tap into the potential of its music industry to help its development, despite being resource-poor. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which celebrated its seventh edition in 2019, has been a success, bringing people from all over the world to share in the country's musical culture.

A video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney's Opera House has gone viral for the second time, with some users referencing the heavy storms that hit Sydney overnight as the trigger for the strange phenomenon. The video was originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson in June 2012, but was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters who pointed out inaccuracies in the video.

Reading were beaten 1-0 by Birmingham City in a Championship game at the Madejski Stadium on Wednesday night. Reading dominated the match but wasted several chances in the closing stages. Birmingham's Clayton Donaldson scored the winner in the 78th minute.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, has been ruled out of the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury. The Brazilian defender, who has been a mainstay for the club, will miss at least four weeks of action, potentially impacting PSG's chances of securing the Ligue One title.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. Leicester host West Ham in the Premier League on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an achilles problem, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring injury.

A statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian and actress, has become a source of controversy in Celoron, New York. The statue, which was unveiled in 2009, has attracted more than 600 likes on a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue." The anonymous creator of the page, who describes himself as a "big fan of Lucy's," argues that the statue should be more like the statues created for other popular TV shows. The statue, which would cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, has been criticized for its unflattering depiction of Ball.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st has shed nearly half her body weight after she was forced to stand during an 11-hour flight - because she feared she was crushing the woman in the seat next to her.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice with other new mothers. She wrote a post called "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" that went viral, highlighting the challenges of being a new mother and the pressure to conform to societal expectations.

Two teenage boys from West Yorkshire, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, have been reported missing after allegedly traveling to Syria to join ISIS. The families of the boys are in shock and deeply worried about their safety. The boys, who are believed to be related to a 15-year-old who was arrested for joining ISIS, have not been in contact with their families for several days and cannot be reached on their mobile phones.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, New South Wales, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding to Aaron Leeson-Woolley. The 24-year-old's life was cut short when her body was found in nearby bushland, and her grieving father, Robert, has opened up about the pain of losing his daughter. Stephanie was a bubbly and thoughtful person who had planned a perfect wedding, but the day before her remains were discovered, her fiancé was inconsolable at the memorial ceremony. The high school where she worked turned into a memorial site, and the couple's wedding ceremony was postponed. Robert Scott has been contemplating the afterlife since his daughter's shocking death, but he remains confident that his beautiful, sweet daughter will be with him.

Southampton are monitoring the transfer of Dutch winger Tonny Vilhena, who is ready to make the move to the Premier League now. The Saints are also monitoring their team-mate, the £10m-rated midfielder Jordy Clasie, and are looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent ahead of possible qualification for European competition next season.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags at one of its historic homes in an experiment which has enraged heritage experts. The move was designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere' in the room but it provoked fury from heritage experts who branded the move 'misguided'. The National Trust has replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music in the heart of the city as his driver got down on his knees to jack up the flash car.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" when he claimed that West Brom's players "s*** themselves" during their defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes that Barton's comments were justified given the circumstances. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, which he believes is relevant to the current situation. Pulis praised the performances of West Brom and hopes that they will continue to do so.

A new species of monkey has been discovered after researchers learned to distinguish it by the appearance of its penis. The white-cheeked macaque was discovered in the remote highland forests of south-east Tibet after researchers set up camera traps.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia, a country in the South Caucasus region, for an eight-day stay. The family is staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is on Republic Square, a tourist attraction in the capital Yerevan. The city is known for its rich history and cultural landmarks, including the Opera House and the Zvartnots International Airport.

A British couple who are locked in a legal battle with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain are attempting to sell the property but are facing the possibility of losing it to demolition.

Apple's iPhone sales have surpassed analysts' expectations for the first three months of the year, with the company reporting a 40% increase in iPhone sales from the previous quarter. The company's revenue and profit have also increased, with the iPhone accounting for more than two-thirds of its revenue and the lion's share of its profit.

A 3-year-old girl who survived a 2016 SUV crash with her mother has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van, which her father believes may have something to do with the crash. The toddler, Elisa Tyler, has been having nightmares and daytime visions about the accident, and her father, Craig Tyler, believes that the white van in her dreams 'hurt' her and her car. The toddler's father has come across several Facebook posts from nearby communities of Foxcroft and Magnolia Green about a series of hit-and-run accidents involving a white box truck.

Researchers have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening tumour, has put her psychology studies on hold in order to care for her long-term boyfriend, Jackson Byrnes, who was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour four weeks ago. The 18-year-olds from northern NSW have raised over $80,000 from community generosity for his life-saving surgery to be performed on Wednesday by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. Jackson's girlfriend Jahnae Jackson (right) noticed he had developed a lump three weeks ago and prompted him to visit a doctor who requested an MRI. For the past week, Jahnae and her girlfriend have been desperately raising the sum needed to pay the hospital.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. The 28-year-old has 15 months left on his contract and has played regularly under Chris Ramsey. Onuoha was in the starting eleven for QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that shows the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US. The map allows users to click on a location and see common phrases for a region, as well as its source. The overall pattern was clear; In the South people found that sentence to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. The traveler, Kalman Kallai, used the chair to enjoy the scenery and interact with the landscape. He wore a green hoody, blue jacket, and hat throughout the journey, which included posing precariously on a river bed, dancing and jumping around in front of rapids, and teasing large statues. The trip was a bonding experience for the traveler and his father, as they shared stories about the father's youth.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed his 'win bonus' to young fan Charlie Pye during a press conference, offering him sweets and chocolate as a consolation for not being selected for the club. Sherwood also revealed a Twix multi-pack as his 'win bonus' for a previous win at Tottenham.

Kell Brook, the world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10 to move onto 17 points in second place, was introduced to the crowd at the Motorpoint Arena. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson.

Marco Verratti of Paris Saint-Germain has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club's Ligue 1 goals, saying he is always on hand to help his team-mates and exerts confidence in the team. Ibrahimovic was suspended for the club's Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona but will be available for selection ahead of the return fixture.

The RAF's main base on the Falklands Islands was accidentally published on the MoD's website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The Aerodrome Manual, which contains vital details of the base, was accidentally uploaded onto a public section of the MoD's website and could have been downloaded by Argentine intelligence agents. The RAF is defending the islands with modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, but the manual could provide valuable intelligence to any Argentine bombers sent to attack the islands.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to kick-start his side's misfiring attack to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have plummeted from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter holiday period. Anderson says there is no hiding when facing Catalans Dragons, who have the league's best defensive record. Huddersfield can climb to a season-high fourth if they make it three wins in a row against Castleford.
Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa cafes less than 500 yards apart, sparking controversy among residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the shooting of free-running badgers in controversial pilot culls, saying that the first two years of culling had not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' of free-running badgers could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow has accused streaming services of giving music away, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite their songs being played 34million times. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, told The Times that younger artists are getting a poor deal and that record companies have been quick to upload their music on to these platforms to prop up the collapse in CD sales after music moved online.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. The first four episodes had been downloaded more than 550,000 times as of early Sunday morning.
A best man left guests at his brother's wedding in tears after composing an emotional song to use as his best man's speech.

Zara Phillips, the Duchess of York, has revealed how she has been working hard to get back into shape after giving birth to her daughter Mia. The 33-year-old has been hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up, and has also been spending time with horses at her mother's stables. She hopes to qualify for Team GB in the 2016 Olympics.

Raheem Sterling's interview on Wednesday, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has caused a stir among fans and the club. Some fans believe that Sterling should be allowed to leave the club, while others are of the opinion that he should stay. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and the club's fans have a popular mantra that no player is bigger than the club.

The article discusses how the Barcelona XI that won the Spanish Super Cup under Bobby Robson in 1996 is breeding managers, with players from that team including Luis Enrique, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho, and Julen Lopetegui currently managing different clubs.

Former Manchester United striker Eric Cantona has claimed that Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore is the best player in the world, saying that he is the most creative player in the world. Pastore has three goals and five assists this season compared with Messi’s 45 goals for Barcelona and Ronaldo’s 51 for Real Madrid.

Campaigners are calling for local councils to draw up maps of the areas where residents are most likely to suffer from social isolation. The maps are being used to target vulnerable people and help them get the help they need.

Judy Eddingfield, a dedicated waitress at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, celebrated her 50th anniversary of working there last week. She has been employed at the restaurant for half a century and considers it her home away from home. Eddingfield remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents at the restaurant she started working at in 1965. She has been married to her true love, Jerry Mathers, for 18 months after meeting him at Winstead's.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Gatting believes that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, there might not be a place for Pietersen in the team. Gatting also believes that if Pietersen does get runs, it is not the end of it and that if people are playing well in the team, why should he just get straight in?

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to the popular photo-sharing app directly from their computer rather than using only their smartphone. The app has been making $1,000 a day, and Instagram is now suing Benn over the hackings its API.

Korean drinking culture is a significant aspect of Korean society, with most companies holding hoesik (dinner with co-workers) at least once a month. The pressure to participate in drinking etiquette is intense, and drinking is considered a way to get to know someone. Koreans always identify the "higher" person in the relationship and defer to them accordingly. It's considered rude for anyone to have an empty glass, and after all glasses are full, everyone says "Gunbae!" and chugs, usually "one-shotting" the entire glass in one go.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during a trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was discharged today after being successfully treated for the injury. The Duke, who is the son of Prince George, has enjoyed a long military career and is the country's top Freemason. He is also the President of the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club and presents the Wimbledon trophies each summer.

The controversial Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called outdated and no longer providing a service due to advancements in parking meter technology. Local business owners have labeled the group as irrelevant and a business, while the Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president believes they are violating anti-touting laws.
Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the websites refused to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a letter to George Lucas asking him to change the rule that bans Jedi Knights from marrying. Lucasfilm responded with a letter addressing his question, saying that being a Jedi is about knowing the value of friendship, compassion, and loyalty, and that a marriage with someone who can connect to you in a selfless way will lead to the light side of the Force.
The Wisconsin Badgers defeated Kentucky in the semi-finals of the NCAA Tournament, ending Kentucky's unbeaten season and advancing to the Final Four.

A video of a violent altercation between brothers in Sydney has been released for the first time, showing a single punch from Barry Lyttle to his brother Patrick, who was left in a coma. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and could face up to two years in jail.

The family of conjoined twin sisters who died 19 days after they were born have been left mortified after they arrived at their gravesite to find cemetery staff had cleared the baby section of all mementos and tossed them in the rubbish.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, has suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court. He believes that judges and courtrooms should allow women to wear the traditional dress as a sign of respect towards different customs. Lord Neuberger also stated that judges should be sensitive to the fact that they usually come from a more privileged sector of society and have an understanding of the different cultural and social habits of those facing them.

An alleged fraudster has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, executives from her TV network, former Obama aide Reggie Love and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food and jewelry worth $2.4million. Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been carrying out the bizarre schemes in the hope of cashing in on the freebies, or winning himself a job in luxurious hotels, according to court documents.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has slapped a €50million (£36m) price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the 'new Lionel Messi'. Dybala is wanted by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain.
Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff is facing protests and a bribery scandal as she struggles with an economic downturn and a massive corruption scandal at the state-run oil company Petrobras.

Eric Cantona, a former Manchester United midfielder, has refuted claims that he starred in a soft porn film, insisting that You and the Night is a "piece of art" and not pornography. The film, which includes a scene of Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, has been both praised and criticized.

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study by behavioral psychologist Charles Spence. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding.

Liverpool's Raheem Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain, but the 20-year-old England player has insisted he is not a 'money grabber' and has postponed contract negotiations until the end of the season. Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers described the £100,000-a-week contract offer as an 'incredible offer', but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Sterling has admitted in a TV interview that he is not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool. Taylor, chief executive of the Professional Footballers' Association, believes waiting until the season is over before resuming talks could be a wise move. A woman named La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, who was adopted, discovered that her biological mother worked at the same company as her and lived only six minutes away. After connecting the dots, she found out her mother was Francine Simmons, who worked at the same call-center operation company as Mitchell-Clark. The two women eventually met and found out they both worked at the same company and lived close to one another.
Oscar Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun smuggler for Aaron Hernandez, was sentenced to one year and one day in prison for transporting firearms across state lines.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning. He is also never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating he plans to keep the striker beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed his desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be away with Gareth Southgate's England under 21 side in the Czech Republic until late June. Pulis has not spoken about any other matters with Berahino.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a 53-year-old Italian who had worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding there, was killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012.
