Zeus, an 11-year-old retired K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession held by the Ridgefield Police Department in Connecticut on Wednesday before he was put down because of a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute for the police dog, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, began around 4. 45pm and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital.

The number of child sex abuse reports has risen by more than 60% since Operation Yewtree, which was sparked by Jimmy Savile's assaults on dozens of children. However, the number of arrests fell by nine percent, prompting critics to accuse the government of failing victims of abuse.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Svinafellsjokull, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajokull, Dettifoss, and Jokullsarlon lake being some of the most favoured filming locations.
A 100-year-old mechanic’s garage in Sydney and a 1850’s goal in Victoria have sold for a combined $3.46 million.

A 40-year-old woman from Morecambe, England, suffered a rare brain disorder that caused her to lose control of her body and crash her car. She was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder, an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that doctors cannot explain. The condition is rare and debilitating, causing symptoms such as uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and cognitive issues. The woman, who lost her job and is unable to walk or drive, is now confined to her home and takes 32 different drugs each day to manage her symptoms.

The statue of Lucille Ball, which depicts her intoxicated pitch for the Vitameatavegamin health tonic, has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has admitted to being "disappointed" in his work and offered to fix it for free. Poulin pledged to make a new one, but the statue is still on display.
Bayern Munich's David Alaba, who was ruled out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament, will be out for the closing stages of the season.

A 21-year-old woman, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, has been charged with running an upmarket prostitution ring in London. Beatrice Nokes, who is accused of grooming three young women to sell their bodies for sex, faces charges of 'causing or inciting' prostitution 'in the expectation of gain' in September and October last year. The two suspects, who are both on bail, will return to court in the coming weeks.

A firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data has offered details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, plastic surgery, credit cards, and health insurance for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on people suffering from 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, migraines, and sensitive teeth. The data is a goldmine for unscrupulous firms and criminals, who can use it to target vulnerable individuals and scam them over the phone.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2016 Masters tournament, expressed his thoughts on his autistic sister Ellie, who was not able to attend the tournament. Spieth said that he misses his sister and wishes she could have been there to witness his victory. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and has helped him understand the bigger picture of life.

Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat insists he will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, despite his previous underestimation of the rivalry in 1998. Advocaat, who has won just twice at home this season, believes that the home crowd will provide an extra weapon for the team.

A young woman and a butcher in Sydney's eastern suburbs have been in a bitter war of words over a chicken purchase dispute. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused at a Bondi butcher shop when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher denies the claims, saying she was the one being rude.

Cadbury has cut the size of its Freddo Frogs chocolate amphibians by 20 percent, from 15 grams to 12 grams, while keeping the price the same. The change was made due to manufacturing cost increases that the company can no longer absorb. The Freddo Frogs were previously 20 grams, and the change is just the latest in a decline in the confectionery industry.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met on Saturday in its Brooklyn headquarters, a day before the former secretary of state officially announces her campaign for president, according to a Democrat who attended the meeting. The campaign's purpose is to give every family, every small business, and every American a path to lasting prosperity by electing Hillary Clinton the next President of the United States. The campaign will try to avoid mistakes that plagued Clinton's failed 2008 run, and maintain that the campaign must remain humble, disciplined, and united.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. The disease, which affects less than 0. 1% of people, worsened over time, leading to a 20-pound weight loss and a need for a feeding tube. Kyli, who was initially misdiagnosed with acute pancreatitis, found solace in a support group for people with the condition.
The five party leaders who took part in the debate were put in the places of the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers in another image - although Mr Farage was hidden behind the Black Ranger, Zack Taylor.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather refused the Fight of the Century. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now looking forward to a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could be a dream come true for Khan, who has been looking forward to fighting in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, north London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide in its maximum width. The home, which is sandwiched between two other properties, has a narrow 'galley kitchen' and a garden, and is described as 'well proportioned' by the estate agency. The home has two bedrooms, a tiny study, a reception room, a shower room, a cloakroom, a kitchen, and a garden. The property was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, almost double the price it sold for in 2001.

The SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon is launching an extraordinary bid to lead the UK, unveiling a manifesto including policies reportedly tailor-made for a power-sharing deal with Labour. Several of her election pledges overlap with Labour policy, including slashing tuition fees in England from a maximum of £9,000 a year to £6,000, and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for people 'right across the UK' and aims to increase public spending on infrastructure in northern England and Wales. The SNP's manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, which could trigger constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election.
Celtic U17s beat Rangers 2-0 in the Glasgow Cup final at Hampden Park, with Josh Kerr scoring twice to give the Hoops a deserved victory.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis insists he will never change his traditional playing style, including wearing a cap and track suit on the sidelines, despite his former club Crystal Palace winning 2-0 against him. Pulis, who led West Brom to a 2-0 victory, says he wants to be close to the action during games and will continue to wear his cap and suit after the match. Pulis has worked wonders at West Brom and has virtually assured their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after she was diagnosed with high levels of mercury in her blood. The fillings, which she had as a child, were believed to be the cause of her health problems, including a puffy, swollen face and feeling exhausted. While dental amalgam has been used for more than 150 years and is still a standard material to use, the amounts taken in from fillings is "minuscule" and there is "no evidence to suggest these fillings are anything other than safe to use".

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking confidently into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair as Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight believes his close friend, the champion boxer Floyd Mayweather, will come to his aid this weekend. Mayweather, an undefeated professional worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

In an interview with Puss Puss magazine, the 35-year-old British chef Gizzi Erskine revealed that her shorthair cat Kimchi has a discerning palate and loves crunchy human food, such as poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. The cat also enjoys caviar, salmon roe, jellied fish heads, and a seafood sculpture made of octopus, lobster, and prawns. Erskine, who lives in a foodie household, has had to put her cat on a diet due to her excessive weight gain.
A father of a little girl who appeared to be standing behind her in a photograph of a pair of boots in Japan has no idea what the boots could be.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will force EU migrants to pay tax and national insurance before they can receive welfare benefits, as part of a crackdown on net migration. The proposals include a ban on EU migrants receiving state support for four years and a ban on 'exporting' child benefit for children living in other EU countries. The Home Secretary, Theresa May, said the changes would act to limit the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU.
A severely disabled boy has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital ward for seven nights after the hospital did not have a suitable bed for him to sleep in.

The Masters is set to take place this week, with golfers from around the world vying for the coveted title. Rory McIlroy is the favorite to complete his career Grand Slam, while Tiger Woods is set to play in the traditional par-three tournament for the first time in over a decade with his two children. The tournament has a rich history, with the most famous shot in the tournament's history being made by Gene Sarazen on the 15th hole in 1930.

Italian champions Juventus have ruled out signing Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him. Juventus need to reinforce their forward line with Palermo's Paulo Dybala and Paris Saint Germain's Edinson Cavani.

David Cameron will launch a multi-billion pound sale of Lloyds Bank shares if he wins the Election, with proceeds used to help pay down the national debt. The shares will be offered at a discount of at least 5 per cent on the market rate at the time, with the proceeds used to help pay down the national debt.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' which increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by US researchers. The microscopic particles, mostly caused by traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and contribute to the deaths of 29,000 people every year in Britain.

Jessica Ainscough, the late wellness warrior, underwent radiation treatment in her final weeks of a seven-year-long battle with cancer, despite spurning chemotherapy and radiation. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed that Ainscough embraced a controversial Gerson Therapy treatment, which involves a vegan diet and coffee enemas, in her final weeks. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications, leading to Ainscough's death.

A multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west has resulted in the evacuation of 10 people, including four children, to hospitals. The crash, which occurred on Wednesday afternoon, involved three vehicles and resulted in injuries to the victims, including chest and shoulder injuries, arm injuries, and abdominal pain. The affected stretch of the highway has been closed off, with diversions in place south of Fernvale.
Colorado Gator Farm owner Jason McDonald, 34, walked a thin rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators.
The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies have become a sensation, with people lining up for hours to buy the "little bear cookies" at $9 a tin. The bakery has signs warning against buying "fake" cookies, but the demand is so high that bakeries are making and selling knockoffs. The frenzy has sparked outrage, with some people even hiring others to stand in line and resell the goods at a 70% markup.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, has overcome her struggles by becoming a bodybuilder. She was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain some weight, but it changed her life and gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She is now a healthy 9. 5st and a personal trainer. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has now been more than two million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square in the 4.20pm at Wincanton on Wednesday, which has made him an internet sensation. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, was hit by the barrier and performed a mid-air somersault before escaping the fall. The fall was described as the worst he had ever seen and was only his fifth race. Despite the fall, Ferguson is undeterred and plans to ride at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree every year.

Hillary Clinton's campaign launch was met with criticism from some media outlets, but many believe it was a successful rebranding effort. The campaign's new logo and road trip to Iowa helped Clinton reframe herself as an empathetic candidate who connects with everyday Americans.

More than 1,700 Chinese students took an exam in their high school's playground on Saturday because there wasn't enough indoor space. The school said the unusual move was a test of the students' organizing capacity. The students suggested and organised the outdoor exam themselves, and a regular radio announcement ordered them to turn their chairs and desks from time to time to avoid being dazzled by the sun.

Sportsmail has teamed up with Gillette to offer one lucky reader the chance to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize winner will also receive a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving foam. Joe Hart is the No. 1 for Manchester City and the England national team.

Kecil, a baby orangutan who had a tough start to life after his natural mother and another surrogate mother rejected him, has found love at the third time of asking with second surrogate mother Maggie at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie, 53, has proved her parenting prowess by helping to raise Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two now have an inseparable bond. Kecil, who had to be moved from his birthplace at Toledo zoo, in Ohio, 14 months ago after his natural mother failed to bond with him properly after birth, will go on display for the first time this weekend in two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, which were initially thought to have tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food, ate parts of her vital organs. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause of death could not be determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, a multiple world and Olympic gold medalist, is facing fraud charges over his suspected involvement in an illegal betting case. Karabatic, who was briefly detained when the case emerged, now plays for Barcelona in the Spanish league.

A gang of six men have been jailed for a total of 31 years after being convicted of a string of sexual offences against teenage girls. The offences, which ranged from inciting sexual activity with a child, to rape, happened in cars, woods or at the defendants' homes in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The men were found guilty in March and have now been handed sentences of between three and nine years in jail.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials after being convicted of murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd. Hernandez is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. The trial is set for May 28, but it has been postponed and no new date has been set.

The Emirates Airline has signed a three-year deal with the FA Cup, which will see the competition rebranded as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal is worth £30 million and will add to Emirates' ever-increasing portfolio of sporting sponsorship. The deal includes naming rights to Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, the Emirates Cup, and sponsorship of AC Milan's youth team. Emirates has also signed deals with other football clubs, including Hamburg and Arsenal.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in a fifth Olympics next year in Rio, but he won't be swimming at the world championships in Russia in August as part of the punishment set forth by the sport's U. S. governing body. Phelps, who had already qualified in three events before being banned from the last major international meet before the Rio de Janeiro Olympics, said he is looking forward to next year and that he enjoys being on those trips.

Gareth Bale is a huge doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg match against Atletico Madrid with a calf injury. Bale lasted just a few minutes before limping off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid is also without Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks.

Experts at Texas Tech University found that more than 50% of pensioners with investments during the 2007 and 2008 global financial crisis panicked and sold them after the stock market fell by 30%. If they had resisted the temptation to sell, the same pot would be worth £141,000 today.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around the club's fortunes, according to former City player Stuart Pearce. The club is struggling to finish in the top four and Pearce believes the manager should stay in place.
Manchester United players trained in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona on Monday, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and nine points behind fourth-placed Sampdoria. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to turn their domination into goals.
Miley Cyrus' armpit hair caused a stir on social media, with some users advising her to shave and others defending her choice.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32 and Suarez has 21. The trio's combined tally includes six penalties and two free-kicks. Barcelona's emphatic win boosted their Liga goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

A 44-year-old woman was hit by a cyclist who fled the scene after the incident in south London. The cyclist allegedly smiled at the woman's husband as he disappeared. The woman suffered facial injuries and is currently off work.

Paul Gregory, a 51-year-old man from Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 metres, when in fact he was a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff read an article in The Westmorland Gazette, describing how the 'experienced walker' had been attacked by cows in Cumbria on the third day of a hike in 2012. Gregory was also fined £60 for a victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a system that would allow users to unlock their devices by taking a selfie. The system would use the front-facing camera to scan the user's face and automatically unlock the device if the image matches one on file. The patent was filed by the California-based firm in March 2011 and awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident was captured on video and shared nearly 10,000 times on Facebook. Sedway's husband and two sons were forced to leave the plane, and the family was later removed from the flight. The airline was concerned that Sedway might collapse during the eight-hour flight.

A vintage Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while three adults were taken to hospital as a precaution. The crash occurred on Warringah Road, and the incident comes after police warned motorists to obey road rules during the Easter long weekend.

Google has set up a team to boost the battery life of phones, tablets and electric cars. The team is working on flexible, wearable and implantable batteries. Google has been working on similar projects since 2012.

The 223ft Explorer is a superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro. It comes with a helipad, infinity pool, and space for supercar and jetski storage. The yacht is capable of carrying a helicopter in a climate-controlled garage, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and a variety of inflatables water toys. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it likely to cost even more to purchase.
Ed Miliband is pushing ahead with his controversial cap on rents despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hoped Arsenal would win in a video was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a poll revealed 85% of readers felt he should not lead Steve Clarke's side out at Wembley.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to a study published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may even contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, which can be explained by the expansion of the universe and the different is marginal - typically about 70 nano-Kelvins - but it is enough to stand out when the entire cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB) of the universe is measured.

The Lincoln assassination chair, which was shot in Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C. in 1865, will be displayed at the Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, as part of the museum's observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is believed to be oil from other people's heads who sat in the chair before Lincoln. The chair has been part of the museum since its founding 85 years ago and was originally housed in the Logan County Courthouse where Lincoln practiced law in Illinois in the 1840s.

A 19-year-old vlogger from East Sussex, Jake Boys, surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking tickets to see One Direction in Cardiff. However, he mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead of Wales, where the concert was actually taking place. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A device has been created that can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs and weapons. The mobile X-ray scanner, heralded as the world's first 'airplane scanner', sweeps down a plane and can detect various objects inside. While the radiation emitted by the scanner is not safe yet for humans to be in the plane when it is operated, the company behind it thinks it could become a vital tool in aircraft safety.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Stephen Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair. Officers believe he may have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital in Winchfield.
Middlesbrough are top of the Championship, but the division is so unpredictable that it is impossible to predict the outcome of the season.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media and in fashion. The trend has been popularized by models and celebrities, with some embracing the look for its defiant feminist message, while others do it for its cool factor.

A couple from Ohio, Randy and Jodi Speidel, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after struggling to raise money for help. The couple, who had chronic conditions and were unable to make a living, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. The couple had been living without gas, water, and electricity, and had limited their food intake to one meal a day. The couple had also removed their pets from the house to spare their lives.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader of the party even if it is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications that he would quit if the party is left out of power after the election. Clegg said he would fight for his job "in all circumstances" and emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party. He also expressed optimism about the prospects of the Liberal Democrats and suggested that the party should be involved in and through the next Parliament.

A pensioner was saved from a badger by his Jack Russell terrier, which dragged him back indoors. The badger was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Premier League International Cup semi-final on Wednesday, while the Chelsea manager avoided the Champions League fixtures to visit Fulham's Motspur Park training ground. Mourinho joked with Fulham goalkeeping coach Vic Bettinelli, whose son plays for the first-team at Craven Cottage. Chelsea crashed out of the Champions League in the last 16 this season, but they are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010.

A property developer was attacked with corrosive liquid outside his home in Cornwall, leaving him with life-changing injuries and a loss of vision. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route is warning pilgrims and other visitors to stop defecating along the famous path. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have been erected in the municipality of Lastres. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there can be very few places to go when nature calls. The signs are posted next to warnings that urge people not to litter. The signs are found to be so amusing they have become an attraction.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a Michigan strip club on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze took place at a building located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. Only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected, according to local media. The site was not a vacant facility, the officials also said. Local resident Terry Rauh told MLive a fire took place at the building once before. An investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport, has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give her $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search, and held her for hours. The settlement sends a message that discrimination is not tolerated and will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

An Asiana Airlines flight crashed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people and skidding off the runway. The plane had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea, and overran the runway at 8pm local time. Local media reported that the plane had a tailstrike and spun 180 degrees after impact, facing the wrong way on the runway. The plane had missed the landing point on the runway, and local television footage appeared to show evidence of a hard landing and no sign of the landing gear.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a 26-year-old reality star on the TV show Made In Chelsea, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard. He revealed his most expensive watch, a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000. The watch has a sun or moon that moves on rotation depending on the hour of the day. Another of his flashiest watches is the Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, which he purchased on holiday in Italy and can be bought secondhand for £6,500.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The collection includes a diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew with a mother-of-pearl handle, and a painting of Mr. Hardy holding the bow. The auction, which takes place on Saturday, includes dozens of books, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and crystal chandeliers.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a man standing on the yellow line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which cleverly mocks conservative attitudes, has been shared thousands of times. The man in the photo was actually following a public transport safety regulation, and Felippe is warning others not to do the same. The post has received thousands of comments, with users praising Felippe's witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan who wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, a legendary Australian cricket player, almost 20 years ago has shared the Australian cricket great's response in the wake of his death. The letter, dated September 27, 1996, included a full sheet of notes about spin bowling for left-hand bowlers and tips on different deliveries. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler and middle-order batsman, wrote that the left-arm over-the-wrist bowler who spins the ball into the right-hander from outside the off-stump is said to have bowled a Chinaman, while the same bowler who spins one away from the right-hander has bowled a wrong'un.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg believes that virtual reality will play a key role in the future of travel, allowing users to experience new environments and locations without the need for physical travel. Zuckerberg's views are supported by Facebook's recent purchase of virtual reality headset maker Oculus and the company's promise of virtual reality gaming. The social media giant has also announced plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed, allowing users to explore locations with multiple viewpoints. Marriott hotels have already trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America, allowing guests to sample different holiday destinations.

A couple, Guo Kai and Dong Hui, who turned 22 on Monday, had planned to get married this month in Sichuan, China. However, Dong was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to hospital, postponing the ceremony. Despite her condition, Dong wanted to have wedding photographs taken for her birthday. Family and friends helped her put on a wedding dress and had professional photographers take pictures. Dong's husband, Guo, has been at her bedside every day, attending to her needs and planning the wedding. The couple met a year ago and have been committed to each other since then.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions that took place within three hours in Houston. The three wrecks killed 6-year-old Joshua Medrano, injured his mother, and led to the death of a homeless man.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company. The positions will be based at its Redmond campus in Washington and the program will be run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that helps train people with autism for careers in IT. The announcement was made by Microsoft Corporate VP of Worldwide Operations, Mary Ellen Smith, who has a teenage son, Shawn, with autism. Smith wrote on the company's blog that the program is part of Microsoft's commitment to expanding opportunity and having a diverse workforce that represents its customers.

Two Tulsa deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned because of threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime, but have come under criticism for pinning Harris' head to the ground as he said, "I'm losing my breath." The sheriff has suspended the drug unit of the agency pending the review of the April 2 shooting of Harris following a weapons sting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations in the shooting.

A couple who married in their teens and suffer from cystic fibrosis are in a race against time as the young wife waits for a life-saving lung transplant. Katie Prager, 24, was diagnosed with an infection in her lungs called Burkholderia Cepacia and is desperately in need of a transplant as doctors predicted she would not live a year without new lungs. Her husband Dalton, 23, pleaded for help, saying that his wife is being turned into a number, a statistic, and a dollar sign by her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, which will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.

The Sleep Cycle app tracked sleep data from over two million users in 47 countries between 2014 and 2017. The data revealed that the world sleeps the least on Mondays, with South Africa waking up at 6:09 am. Americans wake up at 7 am and are in the worst mood all week. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality in the world that night. The US sleeps in the most on Fridays, not rising until 8:24 am.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo wrote passionate love letters to Jose Bartoli, a Catalan artist, while she was married to muralist Diego Rivera. The letters, which were written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, which comprise more than 100 pages, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and were passed down through different generations of his family.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance and socialist ideology, is popular with Labour activists but is seen as a threat to British politics. He is linked to Unite, a powerful union that holds significant influence over Labour candidates, and his socialist policies could lead to a return to the dark days of the 1970s.

A zookeeper placed a GoPro camera at the bottom of water troughs to capture the different perspectives of animals drinking. The animals, ranging from a rhino who almost kisses the surface of the water to a lemur who delicately licks it, were recorded for a total of 30 hours. The zookeeper then cut the final footage down to four minutes and said it offered a completely unique perspective to anything he had ever seen before. Some of the animals were initially sceptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely.

A YouGov poll found that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, while 43% believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight. The poll also revealed that voters think Cameron wants to win less than Miliband.

A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev had previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev, and is accused of involvement in Nemstov's murder.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed more than 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before the soldiers found him. Sonit's face was coated in dust from the rubble, but he was uninjured and taken to Bhaktapur Hospital.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a land use battle over its plans to turn a patch of secluded land near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, is trying to prove that the property is historic enough to change its designation and build a center for twelve patients. The property, which includes stone cottages, is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose. The rehabilitation program, founded in 1966, claims to be non-religious and non-profit, but its methods include spending up to five hours a day in a sauna for 30 days straight and mega doses of the vitamin Niacin.

The article describes the transformation of Kabul, Afghanistan, into a city where English-speaking individuals are now isolated and fearful of reprisals due to their former job skills. The city has seen a significant increase in population, with many people arriving to avoid the violence in the provinces. The article highlights the changing dynamics of the city, with some areas reclaiming streets that were once empty, and others being deserted by businesses.

Two Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, a Navy spokesman said. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. The two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, which contains SEAL teams. The sailors were swimming in lap lanes and were not wearing gear at the time. One SEAL died and another was hurt on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story in Virginia.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. NBC's host Rebecca Lowe, a former BBC and ESPN journalist, is helping to enhance coverage of the Premier League in America. The move has resulted in more people watching Premier League matches live in the USA than in Britain, with some 13 million different Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2012-13 and 32 million in 2014-15.

Ed Miliband will do 'more damage to the country than he did to his brother', Boris Johnson said this morning as the pair clashed on live TV. The London Mayor, who appeared alongside Mr Miliband on the BBC's Andrew Marr Show, launched a furious personal assault on his rival - with their encounter descending into a furious shouting match.

A prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. Dustin Irons, 26, was appearing over video-link to a court in Oregon when he managed to pull down his pants for the lewd gesture, despite being in handcuffs. The outraged judge sentenced him to an extra 30 days in jail for contempt of court.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has made significant progress in Formula One since their poor start to the season in Australia. Although Button and teammate Fernando Alonso retired during the race at the Sepang International Circuit, the duo discovered the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Button is now hoping further steps have been taken going into this weekend's race in Shanghai. McLaren is comparing themselves with the Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses, and Button acknowledges the entire team, including Honda, still has a long way to go.

A hospital in Western Australia was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitised medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider and fined. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated a loss of morale within its workforce.

Becca and Dale Litchfield, a couple from Nottingham, decided to give up their dream wedding in order to have one last shot at IVF and have twins. They were overjoyed when they discovered the fertility treatment had worked and Becca gave birth to twins. The couple said their vows and are now blessed with yet another stroke of luck.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for almost 24 hours, and the page was replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company offered apologies and removed the inappropriate content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club centre in the US was filmed barking at a young husky dog, causing laughter and confusion among onlookers. The video shows the Shibu Inu attempting to bark at the husky, which responds with a high-pitched whine. The dogs continue to vocalize at one another, with people in the video laughing and mimicking the dogs' actions. The video concludes with the husky losing interest and the Shibu Inu settling down.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English fast bowler, is preparing to lead England in the upcoming Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to challenge the opposition and has trained hard to become the fastest bowler on the pitch. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the West Indies' conditions. He is determined to earn his spot and prove his worth in the competition.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight between the WBA's super-middleweight and regular middleweight champions. Ward, ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers, sees Smith as an ideal warm-up opponent before a rematch with Carl Froch. Froch, meanwhile, is turning his attention to his other ambition before retirement - a first appearance on the Las Vegas Strip, against the namesake son of Mexican legend Julio Cesar Chavez.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week, but her election victory was overshadowed by the departure of the majority of the city's police force, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their resignations, and residents rallied behind Byrd, saying the town didn't need as many officers as it had. The city has suffered a spate of break-ins recently, and despite the police force, residents rarely saw cops patrolling the streets.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the club are set to make him available this summer. The Ivorian has played a major role during City's recent trophy-laden period and is in no rush to leave. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, are interested but given his huge wages there are some doubts. City, meanwhile, will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, but instead have other psychiatric disorders. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of people taking SSRIs did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications. Dr. Howard Forman, medical director of the Addiction Consultation Service at Montefiore Medical Center, stated that clinical depression is distinct from temporary feelings of sadness and that these symptoms do not make someone mentally ill. The study also found that prescriptions for antidepressants have more than trebled since 1998 in the world's richest countries.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself last month, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that.

A 10-year-old boy nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. Koby Hodder's heart stopped for a staggering 12 minutes after he collapsed while playing British Bulldog, a game in which children run from one side of a playing field to another without being caught by one of the 'bulldogs', who often employ forceful tactics to trap runners, including rugby tackling opponents to the ground. His heart suddenly stopped beating blood around his body and he collapsed and lost consciousness. The 10-year-old was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, a former Bolton Wanderers player who collapsed after suffering a cardiac arrest during the first half of Bolton's FA Cup quarter-final against Tottenham in 2012. Teachers at Koby’s school in Doncaster, were able to give Koby CPR until paramedics arrived and saved his life. His father, Mark, 45, got a call from the school at

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, wants to see the bitterness taken out of most matrimonial disputes. She believes that divorce laws in England and Wales should remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame. The senators, including Republican John McCain, have called for economic sanctions against Russia and the condemnation of the Putin regime. Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on Feb. 10, 2017, and the third film in the series will debut Feb. 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, who is married and has two sons with the British author, will write the script for the second film. The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He praised Mayor Keith Summey for firing the officer who killed Scott and called for reform in national policing legislation. Sharpton also attended a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon.

Rodgers said he will speak with Sterling on the matter and move on from the situation. Union barons gave more than £1 million to Labour in the second week of the election campaign, swelling the party's war chest for the final 14 days of the campaign. The donations, which equate to £1. 22 a second, came from Unison, USDAW, and Unite, with Unison giving the most, followed by Unite and USDAW. The flight was unable to land at Manchester due to the operating crew exceeding their legal flying hours. Passengers were eventually allowed off the aircraft and bused to Manchester, where they were left waiting for transport. The flight was eventually able to depart for Doha.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300million Las Vegas mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Bieber, who has been close friends with Mayweather for years, will accompany the fighter on numerous occasions, including joining him on stage during a recent press conference. For-profit colleges Corinthian Colleges Inc. and others are closing down, with the U.S. Department of Education curtailing their access to federal student aid. Corinthian, which once enrolled more than 70,000 students, is one of the worst of the "predator colleges" that offer dubious degrees, saddle students with high amounts of debt, and gobble up tens of billions of dollars in federal money every year. The closure of Corinthian is a positive development in a long struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club on Thursday after 'being blamed' for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola has played down the claims. Muller-Wohlfahrt's decision came after Bayern boss Guardiola appeared to imply that the defeat was down to a lack of available players.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top on the eve of his world title defence against Bryant Jennings. The Ukrainian superstar will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years when he takes on the undefeated Philadelphian at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, believes age has no bearing on how long he can go on for and is happy with the preparation for this training camp.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. He said he would miss being on the show, but he also thanked those who supported him. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said it would be great if she were invited back to front Top Gear. In a bizarre incident during a La Liga match between Barcelona and Celta Vigo, Fabian Orellana, a Celta Vigo striker, threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets, a Barcelona midfielder, during the closing stages of the match. Orellana was shown a red card for the incident, and Busquets, who was hit by the grass, made a clutch of the turf on his neck. Tens of millions of people in China marked the annual 'Tomb Sweeping Festival' this weekend by travelling home to their ancestral villages. Families across the country descended on graveyards to clean their tombs of the deceased and honour their loved ones, burning fake paper money and leaving their favourite food and drink to ensure they are not poor or hungry in the afterlife.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from Simon's 50-year career, including hits from his days with Simon & Garfunkel, has outsold more youthful musicians such as Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping to propel him to the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas, Real Madrid's goalkeeper, insists he will stay at the club even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. The 33-year-old Spanish international claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking into the side as a 16-year-old in 1996. Real Madrid has repeatedly linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea, but Casillas claims he will continue to fight for the position if he is not the starter. The team is determined to defend their Champions League title, and Casillas is focused on helping Real Madrid reach the semi-finals.

The UK's employment rate hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, with the International Monetary Fund praising Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy. David Cameron said the Conservatives had overseen a 'jobs miracle' and Britain had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU put together. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth more than £6 billion, to power passenger jets for the Middle Eastern airline Emirates. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble praised Mr Osborne's 'wonderful job' of handling the economy. The plan had reduced the deficit from a record £153 billion under Labour in 2009-10 to £90 billion last year. Mrs Lagarde said she had 'no doubt that can continue to be the case in the future' under Mr Osborne's plans to return Britain to the black in 2018-19.

A chef created a 10in-tall, half-kilogram burger piled with six forms of three different meats and containing a whopping 2,000 calories. The Whole Damn Farm burger features two beef patties and a whole fried chicken thigh, and was created after a customer challenged the chef to create a burger containing three kinds of meat. The burger contains two beef burgers, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers, and costs £13. 50.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, which serves high-quality meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef, has opened its doors to the public. The canteen, which serves organic and locally sourced produce, has a menu that changes daily and includes dishes such as organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen and has a quirky interior with light fittings and high tables and stools.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now feeling much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has 30 Grammy nominations and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987. King suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago last year, forcing him to cancel the remainder of his tour.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a variety of headwear, including ships, rabbits, and flowers, as well as more conservative attire. The event was attended by Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists, and was organized by the Catholic cathedral.

The service asks people to use common sense when calling 999 and to stop and think about the potential consequences of making a prank call.

Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four who died three hours after giving birth to her daughter Poppy, was found dead in the same hospital bed where she had given birth. The deaths of Lianne Hindle and three other babies and one mother at North Manchester General Hospital prompted an investigation. The deaths, along with those of four babies and two mothers at the Royal Oldham Hospital, led to an investigation. The family of Lianne Hindle is calling for action to prevent further tragedies at the maternity unit.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, who gave birth to her second child just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant, has been congratulated by the official Australian Olympic team's Twitter and her former agency PACE Sports Management. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while she was pregnant with her son Cornelis, and won her second world title for hurdles seven months after he was born in 2006.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Mobile Bay, Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing people. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and crews searched late into the night for at least four people missing. Roseanne Barr, 62, revealed she is going blind due to macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that get progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain. The combination of the two is terrible. The risk for both diseases goes up for everyone after age 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of an Australian college baseball player who was killed while out for a jog. The Stephens County jury found Luna guilty in the August 16, 2013, death of Christopher Lane, who was shot in the back while running along a city street in Duncan. The university issued a campus alert advising students to shelter in place and continued reposting the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message. No injuries have been confirmed, and the university has not given the all clear as of 2am.

Edinson Cavani, a player known as El Matador, prepares for Paris Saint-Germain's quarter-final clash with Barcelona. If PSG are to progress beyond the Champions League's last eight, Cavani must torment the stars from Catalonia. Despite facing challenges, including a goal drought and injuries, Cavani has a towering reputation in the game and must perform well to help PSG break through the glass ceiling.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight in Liverpool. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, kept Luis contained behind the jab and landed a decent uppercut at the end of the second round. Luis showed aggression in the closing rounds but was unable to overcome Mathews, who was given a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

The U.S. Census figures show that the undocumented and documented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, and 78 million by 2060. The report from the Center for Immigration Studies predicts that immigrants could account for 82% of population growth in the country by 2060. The growth in immigrant population has important implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment. The report also suggests that the surge in immigrant population could potentially exempt about five million undocumented immigrants from deportation.

Arsenal's Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury in a 1-0 defeat by Reading's Under 21s at the Emirates Stadium. Wilshere was joined by other injured first team players including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby. Martin Keown's son Niall scored the winning goal for Reading in the opening minutes. Wilshere impressed during the game, finding Alex Iwobi and almost setting up a goal for himself. The match was supposed to showcase Arsenal's next generation of talent, but it was Keown's son who stole the spotlight.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has been struggling with his game recently, falling outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing. However, he has been working hard on the practice ground and has shown improvement in his play, hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signing for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose is optimistic about his chances at the Masters and believes he is on the right track.

A Mayfair mansion that was once a milking parlour has gone on the market for £25million. The property, which is decorated with modern furnishings and features a private lift and guest cloakroom, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank. Bayern Munich's squad is weakened by injuries, but the team's sense of unity is stronger, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles this season, are without Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League game against Porto. Muller believes the team's recent injury troubles have helped them build a strong unit on the pitch. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on the scoring prowess of Muller and Robert Lewandowski in the absence of Robben and Ribery as they look to become the first team to beat Porto in the Champions League this season.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base on Thursday to discuss a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. The pair attended the base to ensure Mercedes doesn't win the race, as Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel won the Malaysian Grand Prix. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that the German driver deserved to win and Ferrari got their tactics spot-on in the heat. Mercedes needs to analyze why Vettel's Ferrari was better suited to the high temperatures and a three-stop strategy.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable. The bill, which was signed on Friday, is the first time nitrogen gas has been used in an execution in the United States. The process is said to cause a quick loss of consciousness and death from lack of oxygen. The bill was signed in response to the U.S. Supreme Court's review of lethal injections, which have been put on hold while the court considers their use. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and leaving 13 missing. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking is believed to have been caused by a fishing net weighing 80 tons being pulled in, and 56 bodies have been recovered.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. The drug, called olaparib, works by blocking the cancer cell's ability to repair damage, targeting genetic mutations within the tumours. The study found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, stopping prostate cancer growth and improving responses in medical scans. The drug is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her photography skills and globetrotting into a business by launching a website called 'In Bed With' to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12, 000 followers on Instagram, Taylor has built relationships with hotels and PR companies over the past seven years, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature them on her site. Taylor's unique concept of documenting her experiences in an online magazine format has taken off, and she has generated further income from featuring companies on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death after getting caught up in a fight between two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. QPR is unlikely to face disciplinary action, but the FA will seek observations from each club and ensure that QPR and the police are taking necessary steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and for them to face a banning order. Chelsea's celebrations were marred by objects being thrown onto the pitch by the crowd, and the club is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses to come forward.

The right to buy policy, which allows council tenants to buy their homes at a discount, is being extended to housing association tenants, but Thornberry opposes it.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. His form has reportedly led to interest from abroad but Gomes has denied being contacted by Premier League leaders Chelsea.

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features a fake skinned fox, and PETA is in talks with billboard companies to mount the poster outside Harvey Nichols. Harvey Nichols, which previously stood against the fur industry, re-introduced it last year.

Chile has joined several of its South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history as they prepare to break the record of most days at the summit of the table in a single season. Mourinho's side have led the way since beating Everton 6-3 at Goodison Park on August 30, after Tottenham had led the table following the first two rounds of games.
