The country is seeking to tap into the economic potential of music, which has been acknowledged by its prime minister and minister of culture. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which celebrated its seventh edition, brought artists from the United States, Luxembourg, Brazil, and Cape Verde to the capital city of Praia. The festival was described as one of the most spectacular events in Cape Verde, with people from all corners of the world sharing in the music.

A hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney's Opera House has gone viral for the second time. The video was originally posted by Sydneysider Darren Johnson following strong storms and tandem heavy swells in June 2012. YouTube commenters quickly pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot.

Reading, beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost again to Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Although Reading dominated most of the match, they wasted several chances in the closing stages of the first half. Birmingham held firm and grabbed the winner seven minutes from the end, when Clayton Donaldson nodded in his 16th goal of the season.

David Luiz, a Brazilian defender for Paris Saint-Germain, suffered an injury during a Champions League match against Marseille, leading to his suspension for at least four weeks. The news has caused concern for the French champions, who are currently fighting for the Ligue One title and could be forced to play eight matches without Luiz.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. Figures by anti-piracy and security firm Irdeto revealed overall illegal downloading of show is up 45 per cent year-on-year, jumping from 4.9 million for the same two-month period in 2014. The top country for illegal downloads of Game of Thrones episodes was Brazil, which accounted for almost one million of them, followed by France in second, the US, Canada and the UK.

Leicester City host West Ham United in the Premier League on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles problem, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring injury. The match is expected to be a tough one for both teams, with West Ham unbeaten in their last seven away games against Leicester.

A statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from the TV show "I Love Lucy," has sparked controversy in Celoron, New York. The statue, based on a moment from the show where Ball is drunk and pitches a health tonic, has been criticized by locals as unflattering. The statue, which costs an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast, has attracted more than 600 likes on a Facebook page called 'We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue.' The statue depicts Ball during one of her most loved moments on the show, but locals say it looks nothing like the beautiful Lucy they know.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st lost nearly half her body weight after she was forced to stand during an 11-hour flight because she feared she was crushing the woman in the seat next to her. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, joined Weight Watchers Online and ran a 10k race on Sunday, when she would have struggled to walk half a mile, let alone run six. She lost 4st through joining a slimming club but then shed another four-and-a-half stone after taking up running.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice on raising a baby for the first time. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shared a post called "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" that highlighted the challenges of being a new mother.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, have been reported missing after allegedly traveling to Syria to join ISIS. The boys, who are believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, a 15-year-old who was arrested in 2006, have not been in contact with their families for several days and cannot be reached on their mobile phones. The families are in a state of profound shock and are urging anyone with information to contact the police.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, New South Wales, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding to Aaron Leeson-Woolley. The 24-year-old's body was found in nearby bushland, and her grieving father, Robert, explained that it is especially painful that her life was taken away when she had so much to look forward to. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers to pay tribute to the murder victim. The venue was turned into a memorial site after the discovery of her remains.

Southampton are reportedly interested in signing Dutch winger Tonny Vilhena, who is eager to leave Feyenoord this summer. The Saints are also monitoring their teammate Jordy Clasie, who has won 11 senior caps for Holland. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent, as he aims to strengthen his squad ahead of possible qualification for European competition next season.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere'. The move was met with anger from heritage experts who called it 'misguided'. The Trust said the beanbag experiment was 'short-term' and would not necessarily continue for the whole year. The National Trust presented each house in context and treated each appropriately, but some staff thought the beanbag seating was good as an experiment.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the side of the road with a flat tyre, but was helped by a driver who changed the tyre. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, noticed the vehicle and offered assistance. The former PM was described as a "complete gentleman" and agreed to a selfie with Waterford.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes that Barton's comments about the team's inability to finish the game were justified. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, which he believes is relevant to the current situation. Pulis praised the team's performances and hopes to continue that success in their upcoming match against QPR.

A new species of monkey has been discovered after scientists learned to distinguish it by the appearance of its penis. The white-cheeked macaque was discovered in the remote highland forests of south-east Tibet after researchers set up camera traps.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for the first time, where they are exploring the country's rich history and culture. The Kardashian-West crew is staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan, which is on Republic Square, a tourist attraction in itself. The hotel frames Republic Square at the heart of the city, and the Kardashian-West family is staying in the capital's finest digs.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now facing the possibility of losing it to the local town hall over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The couple, who are retired and plan to move back to the UK, are currently locked in a dispute over the property's legal status and are facing the potential loss of their money tied up in the property.

Apple's iPhone sales grew 40% in the first quarter of 2015, accounting for more than two-thirds of the company's $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The iPhone's success is attributed to strong sales in China, where the company has big hopes for expansion.

A 3-year-old girl who survived a 2017 SUV crash with her mother has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van, which her father believes may have something to do with the crash. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, said the little girl has been having nightmares and daytime visions about the accident. The white van in her dreams 'hurt' her and her car.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing and also the regions involved in encoding new experiences.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening tumour, has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her long-term boyfriend, Jackson Byrnes, who was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour four weeks ago. The 18-year-olds from northern NSW have raised over $80,000 from community generosity for his life-saving surgery to be performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. Jackson is paralysed and needs help dressing himself, and Jahnae has been raising the sum needed to pay the hospital. The surgery is likely to save his life, but he still has a long road of rehabilitation in front of him as he will be left paralysed for some time.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, has played regularly under Chris Ramsey and was in the starting eleven for the QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. Stoke manager Mark Hughes is also interested in Onuoha, and QPR have held talks over a move for Catania defender Nicolas Spolli. Onuoha is also being watched by Hull City and West Bromwich Albion, with Victor Anichebe being considered for sale this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that shows the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US. The map allows users to click on a location and see common phrases for a region, as well as its source. The overall pattern was clear; in the South, people found presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle" to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and take in the country's sights. The video shows him sitting in the chair, posing, and making gestures. He also danced and jumped around in front of rapids and teased some cows.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a 'win bonus' to young fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood revealed his 'win bonus' to the assembled media in reference to Pye's letter, which included a request for a signed claret and blue football, a WWE wrestling figure, and sweets. Sherwood reached down under the desk to reveal a Twix multi-pack as his 'win bonus' for Pye.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League darts in his home town of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson.

Italian midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in Paris Saint-Germain's Ligue 1 campaign, stating that his off-pitch contributions are just as important as his on-pitch performances. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the club this season, will be available for selection for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Barcelona.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details of the Falklands Islands' main base on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The manual, which includes GPS coordinates and runway depth information, was accidentally uploaded to a public section of the MoD's website and could have been downloaded by Argentine intelligence agents. The RAF is defending the islands with modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, but the publication of the manual could compromise their ability to defend against an invasion.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to kick-start his side's misfiring attack to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have plummeted from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter holiday period. Anderson says there is no hiding when facing Catalans Dragons, who have the league's best defensive record. Huddersfield can climb to a season-high fourth if they make it three wins in a row against Castleford.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa cafes less than 500 yards apart, sparking controversy among residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area. The new Costa will open on the site of the former Dedworth Road HSBC branch, while the other Costa replaced a cycle shop earlier this year. The Costa Express is also located between the two shops.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling had not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' of badgers could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow has accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying he received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. The first four episodes of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, are now available for fans to watch. The leaked episodes have been downloaded more than 550,000 times as of early Sunday morning, Variety reported, citing the piracy-tracking company Excipio. The series is the most illegally downloaded program in the world, with episodes from Game of Thrones's first four seasons being illegally downloaded more than seven million times between February and April 2015.

A best man left guests at his brother's wedding in tears after composing an emotional song to use as his best man's speech. Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old singer, performed the unique speech at his brother Adrian's March 29 wedding in Melbourne. The speech, which included tributes to his brother and his bride, was viewed over 100,000 times online.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after the birth of her daughter Mia. She started exercising every morning, hitting the exercise bike at her home before her daughter wakes up. She also spends time with horses at her mother's stables and squeezes in extra exercise like swimming or cycling. Zara hopes to qualify for Team GB in the 2016 Olympics and is eager for her daughter Mia to spend time around horses as she grows up.

Raheem Sterling's interview on Wednesday, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. Some fans are of the opinion that he should be allowed to leave the club, while others believe he has the potential to be worth more than the £100,000-a-week contract he has turned down. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and many fans are now of the belief that if he wants to go, he is welcome to.

The article discusses a series of images from Barcelona's training sessions featuring former and current coaches, including Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui. The images reveal a connection between the coaches, with some of them having played together in the 1996 Spanish Super Cup and later coaching at the same club. The article also mentions that some of the players from that team, such as Albert Ferrer and Sergi Barjuan, have gone on to manage clubs.

Former Manchester United striker Eric Cantona has claimed that Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore is the best player in the world, saying that he is the most creative player in the world. Cantona watched two games of Pastore playing and praised his ability to pass and create opportunities for his teammates. He also suggested that Spain won the World Cup because of the influence of Barcelona on the national team.

Lorenzo Simon, a 34-year-old landlord, was found guilty of murder after killing his tenant, Michael Spalding, then dismembering his body and stuffing the parts into suitcases which he dumped in a canal. Simon forced Spalding to decorate his flat before attacking him when he refused to work any longer. He then hacked the body up and stuffed the head, limbs, and tools into two suitcases, which he threw into a canal with broken concrete slabs. The case was heard at Birmingham Crown Court, where a jury took 15 hours to decide by unanimous verdict.

Two county councils in England have created 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents are most at risk of social isolation. Essex and Gloucestershire have used data on public health factors and surveys to create the maps, which show areas with large numbers of over-65s, people living alone, and those with mental health issues. The maps are being used to target vulnerable residents and provide support. The Campaign to End Loneliness has called on other councils to copy the maps and draw up their own versions for their local area.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, where she has been employed for half a century. She says it's the only job she's ever had or ever wanted. Eddingfield, who started working at the restaurant when she was 15, has been providing top-notch service for her family for over 60 years. She met her first husband outside the restaurant and they married 18 months later.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting believes that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, there might not be a place for Pietersen in the team. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014, but Gatting admits that more questions will be asked of the England skipper if he fails to find runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to the popular photo-sharing app directly from their computer rather than using only their smartphone. The app is currently making $1,000 a day, and Instagram is unhappy with the hackings its API. Benn is currently making $1,000 a day from the app, and Instagram is asking him to 'fix' the app by Monday.

Koreans have a tradition of drinking together called hoesik, which involves multiple rounds of alcohol at multiple venues. Foreign business travelers may find it challenging to participate due to the intense pressure to drink. Koreans view drinking as a way to get to know someone and an invitation to listen. To avoid offending someone, Koreans defer to the higher person in the relationship and turn their body away from senior figures when drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during a trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today. The Duke, who is the son of Prince George, has enjoyed a long military career and is the country's top Freemason. He has also performed royal duties on behalf of the Queen and is the President of the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been criticized by local business owners who believe advancements in parking meter technology have made the group irrelevant. The Meter Maids, who were originally introduced to stave off bad publicity associated with newly installed meters, now provide a service that has become outdated. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, argues that the Meter Maids are no longer a public service and are violating anti-touting laws by promoting branded merchandise. However, the Meter Maids' general manager, Michael Yarwood, claims that tourists love and embrace the group as a quintessentially part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece will in fact make the payment on time. Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after the social media platforms refused to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US.

A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a letter to George Lucas asking him to change the rule that bans Jedi Knights from marrying. Lucasfilm responded with a letter addressing his question, explaining that being a Jedi is about finding someone you can connect to in a selfless way, which prevents the dark side from taking hold. The letter was signed 'Your friends at Lucasfilm'.

The Wisconsin Badgers defeated Kentucky in the NCAA basketball tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten season and advancing to the final. Kentucky, trailing by four with 12 seconds left, missed a free throw that sealed the win for Wisconsin. The Badgers, led by Frank Kaminsky, won 71-64 and will face Duke in the final.

Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe's lead singer, was criticized for his rendition of the national anthem at a football game, while Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton have all been involved in controversial performances of the song.

Security footage of a violent altercation between brothers Patrick and Barry Lyttle, who were reunited for a holiday in Australia, was released for the first time. The footage shows Patrick pushing his brother Barry, who retaliates with a single punch that causes his brother to fall to the ground. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and has pleaded guilty. Magistrate Graeme Curran said a jail sentence was likely, but the brother's calls for charges to be dropped were not accepted. The brothers were found in a pool of blood and vomit after leaving a bar in Sydney. Patrick Lyttle has called on charges against his brother to be dropped.

The family of conjoined twin sisters, Faith and Hope Howie, were devastated when cemetery staff cleared their gravesite of mementos and tossed them in the rubbish. The Howies had built a small shrine at their gravesite, which they had added to since the funeral, but everything had been removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not notified them that they would be cleaned, and when the Howies returned later in the afternoon, everything had been laid out on shelves for people to collect.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court. He said judges and courtrooms should allow women to wear the traditional dress as they should 'show, and be seen to show' respect towards different customs.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year. He was executed by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri, at 10:15 pm on Tuesday. The execution was carried out despite the U.S. Supreme Court's rejection of several appeals, including one claiming Cole was mentally ill and unfit for execution.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after undertaking several engagements in Turkey. He was hoping to meet the new royal baby, but is being forced to return to Australia where he is on a month-long placement with the army, followed by a week long official tour of New Zealand.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has slapped a €50million (£36m) price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the 'new Messi'. Dybala is wanted by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini watched the Serie A match between Parma and Palermo on Sunday.

Protests have erupted across Brazil as President Dilma Rousseff faces a major political crisis. Rousseff is under fire for an alleged kickback scheme at the state-run oil company Petrobras, which has led to a massive bribery scandal. The protests are taking place as the economy is struggling, with inflation and currency value both at record highs. The demonstrations are meant to show support for Rousseff, but her approval rating has plummeted to 13% since the protests.

Eric Cantona, a former Manchester United midfielder, has refuted claims that he starred in a soft porn film called "You and the Night". The film, which includes a scene of Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear, has been both praised and criticized. Cantona insists that the film is a "piece of art" and not pornography, saying it is beautiful and should be seen. He also defended the film's director, calling it a "superb artistic orgy" and praising the actress who starred in the film.

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study by Professor Charles Spence. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding. The so-called digital seasoning also applies to wine, helping drinkers to enjoy their tipple by up to 15 per cent more, if served alongside the right music.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been linked with a move to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Sterling has been made an 'incredible offer' of £100,000-a-week by Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers, but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Ohio woman La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, discovered her biological mother Francine Simmons, who works at the same call-center operation company as her, after the Ohio Department of Health released birth records for people born between January 1, 1964, and September 18, 1996. The two met after connecting on Facebook, and Simmons called Mitchell-Clark, who had been searching for her biological mother for almost her entire life. The reunion was a relief for the family, and they found out they have three younger sisters they didn't know about.

Oscar Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker for Aaron Hernandez, was "awed" by the former New England Patriots star and "grateful to be noticed" when he sent Hernandez a rifle and two handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's killing. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection to his namesake's murder case.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning. He is also never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, while also acknowledging the influence of agents on players.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a 53-year-old Italian who had worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding, was abducted by four armed men and killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012. Lo Porto was a project manager with the aid group's clean water and sanitation program, working with 8 to 10 fellow international staffers and 100 to 200 locals. He had previously studied at London Metropolitan University and was passionate, friendly, and open-minded. Lo Porto was a popular student who was committed to helping others.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks gathered off the coast of south Florida, near Sebastian Inlet, on Thursday. The scene was so intimidating that it was shared more than 2,000 times on Facebook. The photographer, John Massung, was flying over the area when he saw the sharks, which he theorized were either Blacktips or Spinners, who migrate to breed in shallower waters.

Zeus, an 11-year-old retired K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession held by Ridgefield Police Department in Connecticut on Wednesday. Zeus, who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, took his last ride in a cop patrol car during the tribute. Zeus was put down because of a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute was held to celebrate Zeus's time on the force and to say goodbye to the police dog.

The number of child sex abuse reports has risen by more than 60% since Operation Yewtree, which was sparked by Jimmy Savile's assaults on dozens of children. Since 2011, thousands of people have contacted police with allegations of abuse, with nearly 9,000 reports filed in 2014. However, the number of arrests fell by nine percent, prompting critics to accuse the Government of failing victims of abuse.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Svinafellsjokull, Skaftafell National Park, Vatnajokull, Dettifoss, and Jokullsarlon lake being some of the most favoured filming locations.
A 100-year-old mechanic's garage in Sydney and a 1850's goal in Victoria have sold for a combined $3.46 million.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2021. The rare condition, which cannot be explained by medical science, causes uncontrollable shaking, loss of bladder control, and other neurological symptoms. Rawcliffe, who lost control of her body and crashed her car, has since been confined to her house, unable to walk and relying on a mobility scooter. She is now taking 32 different drugs each day to manage her symptoms.

The statue of Lucille Ball, which has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York, has been the subject of a social media campaign to have it removed. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has admitted to being "disappointed" in his work and has offered to fix it for free. Poulin has pledged to make a new statue that is more in line with Ball's beauty and abilities as a sculptor.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will be out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament after being injured while playing for Austria. Alaba, who was out for three months earlier this season, is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month. Bayern Munich is set to face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court today on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring. Nokes, 21, is accused of grooming three young women to sell their bodies for sex. She faces three charges of 'causing or inciting' prostitution 'in the expectation of gain' in September and October last year. Daniel Williams, a 37-year-old Met police officer, is also accused of running the ring and committing several further offenses, including voyeurism and hiding the profits of their activities in socks stuffed up the chimney of his home.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data offered details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, plastic surgery, credit cards, and health insurance. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2016 Masters tournament, expressed his thoughts on his autistic sister Ellie, who was not able to attend the tournament. Spieth said he misses his sister and wishes she could have been there to share in his victory. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and helped him understand the bigger picture of life.

Dick Advocaat, the Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle. Advocaat, who had previously underplayed the importance of the match in 1998, insists he will not make the same mistake. The match is crucial for Sunderland's chances of staying up in the Championship, and Advocaat hopes that the home crowd will support the team.

A young woman and a butcher in Sydney's eastern suburbs have been involved in a bitter war of words over a chicken purchase dispute. Belinda Bartholomew, the girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, claims she was racially abused and told to go to an 'Aussie butcher' when she tried to change her chicken selection at a Bondi shop. However, the butcher denies the claims, saying he was the one being rude and that she was the one causing trouble.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frogs chocolate amphibians by 20 percent, from 15g to 12g, while keeping the price the same. The change was spotted by a shop owner who stocks the treats. Cadbury's spokesman said the shrinkage is due to manufacturing cost increases that the company can no longer absorb. The Freddo Frogs are just one of many products to feel the pinch in the declining confectionery world.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met on Saturday in Brooklyn to outline their campaign's goals and values, according to a Democrat who attended the meeting. The document, which outlines the campaign's purpose, goals, and how they plan to win, maintains that the campaign must remain humble, disciplined, and united, something voters in Iowa and others states have said Clinton did not do in 2008. The campaign's name is "Hillary for America," and Clinton is planning to launch her presidential candidacy on Sunday through a video message on social media, according to Democratic sources.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed her struggle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was later diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, which requires lifelong feeding through a feeding tube due to the condition's permanent damage. Kyli's weight dropped to 80lbs, and she had to postpone her wedding. She found solace in a support group for people with chronic pancreatitis.

The article discusses memes posted in reference to the leaders' debate, including images of the five party leaders superimposed over characters from TV shows and movies, as well as a meme showing Nicola Sturgeon posing with a sceptical face. The memes were inspired by the debate, which saw Labour leader Ed Miliband warn Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg that they would not get into power without lurching left, as Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon told him he is 'not strong enough' to win power on his own.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather refused the Fight of the Century. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now looking forward to a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could be a dream come true for Khan, who has been looking forward to fighting in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, north London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in in maximum width. The property, which is described as 'well proportioned', has two bedrooms, a narrow galley kitchen, and a garden. The home, which was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, is now under offer. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

The SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon is launching an extraordinary bid to lead the UK, unveiling a manifesto including policies reportedly tailor-made for a power-sharing deal with Labour. Several of her election pledges overlap with Labour policy, including slashing tuition fees in England from £9,000 to £6,000 and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for people 'right across the UK' and aims to increase public spending on infrastructure in northern England and Wales. The SNP's manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP is on course for a landslide victory in Scotland, potentially triggering constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election.

Celtic U17s won the Glasgow Cup 2-0 against Rangers U17s at Hampden Park, with Josh Kerr scoring the opening goal and Robby McCrorie dropping a free kick over the line. The match was played behind closed doors after trouble among Rangers fans at the previous three finals.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis insisted he will never change his traditional playing style, including wearing a cap and track suit, even though he led his team to a 2-0 victory over his former club Crystal Palace. Pulis, who has worked wonders at West Brom and virtually assured their survival in the Premier League, will continue to wear his cap and track suit during matches.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after she experienced health problems, including a puffy, swollen face and feeling exhausted, that she believed were caused by the fillings. The fillings were removed because tests showed high levels of mercury, which is used to make them, and were replaced with white fillings. While dental amalgam has been used for more than 150 years and is still a standard material for fillings, the amounts taken in from fillings is "minuscule" and there is no evidence to suggest they are anything other than safe to use.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking confidently into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair as Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight believes his close friend, the champion boxer Floyd Mayweather, will come to his aid this weekend. Mayweather, an undefeated professional worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Knight's attorney Matthew Fletcher is confident part of that will come their way.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine posed with her pet cat Kimchi for a cat magazine shoot, where she revealed that her feline has a discerning palate and loves crunchy human food, such as poppadoms and tortilla chips. Kimchi is also obsessed with Dreamies cat biscuits and has expensive tastes, including expensive Korean food.

A father in Japan took a photograph of his daughter standing near a rocky outcrop in July 2014. The photograph, which showed a pair of black boots behind the girl, sparked debate online about the boots' origin and meaning. The father, Martin Springall, said he had no idea what the boots could be and that he had no idea if they were real or a trick of the light. The photograph has become a topic of discussion on Reddit, with some people believing it was modified and others arguing that there was no one standing behind the girl.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will force EU migrants to pay tax and national insurance before they can receive welfare benefits. The changes will ban EU migrants from receiving state support for four years and will also ban 'exporting' child benefit for children living in other EU countries. The plans are part of the government's effort to limit the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital ward for seven nights due to a lack of a suitable bed for him. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been without a hospital bed because staff do not have the special cot he needs to keep him safe in his sleep. His mother, Lynne Neatis, has slept with him on the floor for the past week, fearing that her son will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot he must sleep in, to prevent him from injuring himself in the night. Lynne Neatis is now demanding answers from the local health trust as she claims she has waited two years for the high-sided bed needed for Cody and other disabled children.

Rory McIlroy, Tiger Woods, and Ian Poulter are among the golfers set to compete at the Masters, where McIlroy aims to complete his career Grand Slam and Woods is expected to play in the traditional par-three tournament for the first time in over a decade.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has endured a difficult period at Old Trafford after arriving in an expensive loan deal from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him.

David Cameron will launch a multi-billion pound sale of Lloyds Bank shares if he wins the Election, offering the public £4 billion of shares still held by the Government after Gordon Brown's £20 billion panic bailout during the 2008 economic crisis. The shares will be offered at a discount of at least 5 per cent on the market rate at the time, with the proceeds used to help pay down the national debt. The sale of Lloyds shares would be the biggest privatisation since the 1980s when Mrs Thatcher's government sold £3. 9 billion of BT shares and £5. 6 billion of British Gas shares in the famous 'Tell Sid' campaign.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' which increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by US researchers. The microscopic particles, mostly caused by traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and contribute to the deaths of 29,000 people every year in Britain. The study involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes. The researchers found that increases in PM2.5 in towns and cities were linked with a 46 per cent higher risk of silent strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, the late wellness warrior, underwent radiation treatment in her final weeks, despite her decision to fight cancer with Gerson Therapy, which lacks scientific support. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, revealed that Ainscough embraced the last chance option, leading to a difficult and risky decision. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but complications arose during the final stages, resulting in Ainscough's death.

A multi-vehicle crash occurred on the Brisbane Valley Highway, 2km south of Fernvale, resulting in the involvement of ten people, including four children. Three vehicles collided, and the injured were flown to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off, and diversions were in place. The incident involved a man with chest and shoulder injuries, a five-year-old boy with chest pain, a 27-year-old woman with arm injuries, and a six-year-old girl suffering from abdominal pain.

Colorado Gator Farm owner Jason McDonald, 34, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators, surprising the reptiles. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years, said he thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. The imam, Abdul Hadi Arwani, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work. The man who asked Arwani to return another day was identified as black and speaking with an African accent. The imam's children are in little doubt that their father was killed by the man asking for the building quote.

Tourists and locals in Hong Kong are lining up for hours to buy butter cookies from a small shop, which has sparked a black market for the treats. The original store has signs warning against buying "fake" cookies, but the bakery also tries to discourage people from buying knockoffs. The frenzy in Hong Kong over the cookies is by no means an isolated example, with other foods such as cronuts and ramen burgers also causing food mania.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, turned her life around by becoming a bodybuilder. She was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain some weight, but it changed her life and gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She is now a healthy 9. 5st and a personal trainer. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has now been more than two million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square in the 4.20pm at Wincanton on Wednesday, which made him an internet sensation. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, was hit by the fence and performed a mid-air somersault before escaping the fall. The fall was described as the worst he had ever seen and was only his fifth race. Ferguson escaped the fall and the only real pain was the cut on his nose and the banter from his friends.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to rebrand herself and frame her campaign. Many critics dismissed her launch, but marketing experts believe it was successful. The campaign aims to flip Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic and forward-looking, and to change how voters emotionally experience her brand.

More than 1,700 Chinese students took an exam in their high school's playground on Saturday because there wasn't enough indoor space. The school allowed the freshmen students to sit the exam outside as a test of their organizing capacity. The students suggested and organised the outdoor exam themselves, and a regular radio announcement ordered them to turn their chairs and desks from time to time to avoid being dazzled by the sunshine.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a chance for one reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The lucky winner will also receive a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving foam. Hart is the No. 1 for Manchester City and the England national team. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but was adopted by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie proved her parenting prowess by raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two now have an inseparable bond. Kecil was moved to Maggie's care after his natural mother and a surrogate mother rejected him. Maggie and Kecil were seen cuddling up to each other earlier today, and Kecil was moved to a new enclosure at the zoo for his first public outing this weekend.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, which were initially thought to have tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food, ate parts of her vital organs. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause of death could not be determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka and 15 other players, has been accused of match fixing and is facing a trial for fraud. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, now plays for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The case has raised concerns about the integrity of the sport and the potential for corruption.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offences against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offences ranged from inciting sexual activity with a child to rape, and occurred in cars, woods, or at the defendants' homes. The victims, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule, who was sentenced to nine years in jail. The gang used social media to lure victims and sexually abused them from 2009 to 2014. Judge Zoe Smith rejected the defense's argument that the girls came forward because they were victims, stating that it stops other girls from coming forward.

Aaron Hernandez, a former New England Patriots football player, faces multiple trials for the murder of Odin Lloyd, a 25-year-old man who was shot and killed in Boston in 2012. Hernandez is accused of killing two men and wounding another person in the incident. He is also facing a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez is being sued by the families of Odin Lloyd and Daniel de Abreu and Safiro Furtado, who were killed in the incident. He is also being sued by Alexander Bradley, who claims Hernandez shot him while they were in a limousine in Miami in February 2013. Hernandez is also being sued by the NFL players union on behalf of Hernandez, who signed a contract in 2012 that potentially was worth more than $40 million.

The Emirates Airline has signed a three-year deal with the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal is worth £30 million and will add to Emirates' portfolio of sporting sponsorship. The deal includes naming rights to Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, the Emirates Cup, and sponsorship of AC Milan's youth team. Emirates has also signed deals with other football clubs, including Hamburg and AC Milan.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in a fifth Olympics next year in Rio, but he won't be swimming at the world championships in Russia in August as part of the punishment set forth by the sport's U. S. governing body. Phelps, who had already qualified in three events before being banned from the last major international meet before the Rio de Janeiro Olympics, said he is looking forward to next year and that he enjoys being on those trips.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks. Real's striker Karim Benzema is also out with a knee injury.

Experts at Texas Tech University found that more than 50% of pensioners with investments during the 2007 and 2008 global financial crisis panicked and sold their investments after the stock market fell by 30%. Those who followed that path and sold at the lowest point eight years ago with a pension of £100,000 would only have £63,000 today. If they had resisted the temptation to sell, the same pot would be worth £141,000 today provided they had not spent any of the cash.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is facing criticism for his inability to turn around the club's fortunes, with Stuart Pearce believing the 61-year-old should be given more time to improve the team. The team's recent poor performance, particularly a defeat to Manchester United, has contributed to the criticism. Pearce, who has experience managing the club, suggests that the squad needs significant changes in the summer.

Manchester United's stars trained in the sunshine on Friday as they put together their final plans for their Premier League showdown with rivals Manchester City. Manchester United players train in the sunshine ahead of their game against Manchester City on Sunday.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona on Monday, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and nine points behind fourth-placed Sampdoria. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to turn their domination into goals. The match ended with Verona's substitute Mounir Obbadi scoring a late goal, and Fiorentina's goalkeeper, Neto, failed to save a shot from Lazaros Christodoulopoulos. Fiorentina is now in sixth place on 49 points, one place and a point behind Sampdoria who occupy the final Europa League qualifying spot.

Miley Cyrus, 22, was photographed at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, with her armpit hair showing. Some users on social media were concerned about Cyrus' armpit hair, while others defended her choice to leave it be. Cyrus is not the first or the last to leave her armpit hair on show, and many users on social media were not bothered by her choice.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance has boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

A 44-year-old woman was hit by a cyclist who fled the scene after being knocked down by the vehicle on the pavement in south London. The cyclist allegedly smiled at the woman's husband as he disappeared. The woman suffered facial injuries and is currently off work sick. The police have issued an appeal for the cyclist to be caught.

Paul Gregory, a 51-year-old man from Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 meters, when in fact he was a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory was found guilty of two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work, pay a £60 victim surcharge, and undergo 19 sessions of 'thinking skills'.

Apple has filed a patent for a system that would allow users to unlock their devices using a selfie. The patent details a method of scanning a user's face using the front-facing camera each time the phone is moved into a certain position. If the scanned face matches a previously taken photo, the phone unlocks automatically. This system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or is placed flat on a table. The screen wouldn't need to be enabled, and once the phone is moved and positioned in front of the face, the camera would begin scanning. It will only unlock if the angle of the face matches, or.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed Sedway had put on a surgical mask to shield herself from germs and asked if she needed anything. When she initially said she was fine, the representative approached her a second time and indicated that she might require extra time to board the plane due to her cancer. The family was eventually allowed to board the plane, but the incident caused a stir on social media, with many people expressing sympathy for Sedway and her family.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while three adults were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. The crash occurred on Warringah Road, and the incident has sparked sympathy from car enthusiasts. The incident comes after police warned motorists to obey road rules during the Easter long weekend to avoid similar accidents.

Google has set up a team to boost the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars. The team, which consists of four men, is working on flexible and wearable batteries. Google has been working on similar projects since 2012. The team is also developing batteries that function at subfreezing temperatures, which is vital for Google's Project Loon balloons.

The 223ft Explorer is a superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, which comes with its own helipad, infinity pool, and space for supercar and jetski storage. The yacht is capable of carrying a helicopter in a climate-controlled garage, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and a variety of inflatables water toys. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it likely to cost even more to purchase.

Ed Miliband is pushing ahead with his controversial cap on rents despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire. The Labour leader said rent controls would give millions of 'forgotten' renters a fairer deal by helping those stuck in so-called Generation Rent by soaring house prices. However, the Generation Rent campaign group said his plans were 'riddled with loopholes' and may make tenants' lives worse.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hoped Arsenal would win in a video was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was offered the chance to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to a study published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, which can be explained by the expansion of the universe and the energy lost by light as it travels through it.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is believed to be oil from other people's heads who sat in the chair before Lincoln. The museum has owned the chair since its founding 85 years ago.

A 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, East Sussex, booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland for a One Direction concert in Cardiff, mistaking the Welsh capital for the Irish one. The boyfriend, Jake Boys, is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has developed a device that can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons. The Roboscan 2M Aeria uses a cone of radiation to sweep across planes and can detect various objects inside. The device is accurate enough to find a filament in a light bulb. While the radiation emitted by the scanner is not safe yet for humans to be in the plane when it is operated, the company behind it thinks it could become a vital tool in aircraft safety. The device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in small or medium-sized jets that land at low-security airports.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. He was last seen leaving a hospital in Hampshire, and officers are searching for him. Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, is described as about 5ft 8ins tall and has dark hair. He was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl.

Middlesbrough are top of the Championship, with only four weeks remaining. They have a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth, with Watford and Norwich also in contention. The match against Watford on Monday is a lunchtime kick-off, which could give Middlesbrough an advantage. The promotion race is so tight that a win for Watford and Bournemouth could change the top two. Jonathan Woodgate, Middlesbrough's captain, is expected to play through a broken toe.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media. The trend has been popularized by fashion designers and celebrities, with models sporting silver hair at Paris Fashion Week. The trend has been embraced by women of all ages, from young women to older women, and has been praised for its feel-good factor.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and had no running water or electricity, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after their online fundraisers for help went ignored. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had turned to online fundraising to help pay their landlord and stretch their meager funds, but their efforts were unsuccessful. The couple had removed their pets from the house to spare their lives and were found wandering outside.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue serving as leader of the party even if it is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications that he would quit if the party is left out of power after the election. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, and expressed optimism about the prospects of the Liberal Democrats. He also appeared to lean towards another deal with the Conservatives, saying he deserved "credit" for forming the Coalition while enduring "five years of constant bile from the Labour Party."

A pensioner was attacked by a badger in his garden, but his Jack Russell dog saved him. The badger was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Premier League International Cup semi-final on Wednesday. Mourinho, who is also Chelsea's son, visited Fulham's Motspur Park training ground with his son Jose Junior. Mourinho joked with Fulham's goalkeeping coach, whose son plays for the first team at Craven Cottage and is linked with a move to Chelsea. Chelsea crashed out of the Champions League in the last 16 this season, but Mourinho is closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured in a December 2014 acid attack on his home in Truro, Cornwall. The attack left him with life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, Sussex, has been charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. The businessman, who attended King's College in Taunton, Somerset, and graduated from Plymouth University, is also a director of Chase 3000 and owns several properties around Newquay.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, sparking controversy. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have been posted next to warnings against littering. The signs have become an attraction, with pilgrims posing for photos with them. The town is now considering adding public facilities for pilgrims along the historic route.

A massive fire broke out at a former strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon, destroying the building and nearby power lines. The blaze started at about 1pm and was reported to have affected only the building itself and a few nearby power lines. The site was not a vacant facility, and local resident Terry Rauh said a fire had taken place there before. The fire was reported to be under investigation.

Shoshana Hebshi, a woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport, has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give her $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search, and held her for hours. The settlement sends a message that discrimination is not tolerated and will help protect future passengers from similar experiences.

An Asiana Airlines flight crashed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people and skidding off the runway. The plane, which had just landed from Seoul, South Korea, reportedly missed the runway and overran it, causing a hard landing. Local media reported that the plane spun 180 degrees after impact and was left facing the wrong way on the runway. The crash occurred at 8pm local time and resulted in a temporary closure of the airport.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality TV star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. The most expensive watch in his collection is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought from a shop on Sloane Street in Chelsea earlier this year.

Actor Robert Hardy, 89, is selling his extensive collection of antiques, including a 3D diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, at a £100,000 auction. The collection, which includes paintings, furniture, swords, and books, is being sold by Dominic Winter auctioneers in South Cerney, Gloucestershire.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a man standing on a yellow safety line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which he claims is a homophobic rant, actually exposes a public transport safety regulation and warns against the normalization of such behavior. The post has received thousands of comments, with users praising Felippe's witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man." The letter included notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers and tips on different deliveries.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize the future of travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised that virtual reality gaming would be available 'this year.' Zuckerberg's views on the future of virtual travel are unsurprising given Facebook's acquisition of Oculus and the company's plans to support virtual reality on its newsfeed. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America, allowing guests to sample different holiday destinations.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, but her boyfriend arranged for her to have wedding photographs taken for her birthday. The couple met a year ago and fell in love after a mutual friend introduced them. Despite her condition, Dong chose a wedding dress and posed with her husband-to-be, who arranged for professional photographers to take the pictures. The couple's love and commitment to each other are evident in their decision to make the wedding and photo shoot a dream come true for them.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death after three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has an extensive DUI record in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologizing for comments about women needing to trust the system to pay them well.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have come under criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended operations of the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting of Harris. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations in the shooting.

A couple, Katie Prager and Dalton Prager, who married in their teens and suffer from cystic fibrosis, are in a race against time as Katie Prager waits for a life-saving lung transplant. Katie Prager was diagnosed with an infection in her lungs called Burkholderia Cepacia and is desperately in need of a transplant as doctors predicted she would not live a year without new lungs. Her husband, Dalton Prager, pleaded for help, saying that his insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton Prager is pleading for help, saying that his wife is struggling to negotiate her healthcare options from her hospital bed at the University of Kentucky.

The Sleep Cycle app analyzed data from over two million users to discover that the world's earliest wake-up time is on a Monday in South Africa, while the worst mood is experienced on Tuesdays. Slovakia topped the list for national average sleep quality, with the UK in 45th place and the US in 49th. The best sleep quality occurs on a Wednesday night, with over half of countries surveyed reporting the most restful sleep on this day. The app tracked sleep phases using the phone's accelerometer and gathered data between 1 June 2014 and 31 March this year from users aged 18 to 55 in 47 countries.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, 25 of which are headed to auction, were written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949 and saved by Jose until his death in 1995. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance and socialist ideology, is highly popular with Labour activists during his election campaign in South Wales. However, his union, Unite, is a potent, sinister force in British politics, seeking to impose socialist revolution on the country. McCluskey's influence on Labour candidates is chilling, and his yearning for the 1970s is reminiscent of the dark days of the socialist revolution. Unite, with a claimed membership of 1.42 million, is intertwined with the Labour Party's structure, MPs, and finances, and remains addicted to failed socialist policies.

A zookeeper at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv captured footage of animals drinking water in their own unique ways using a GoPro camera placed at the bottom of their water troughs. The footage, which lasted 30 hours, showed a variety of animal behaviors, including a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water and a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper, Elad Hershkowitz, said the experiment was special and offered a unique perspective on animal drinking habits. Some animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely. The footage, which was cut down to four minutes, showed a range of animal behaviors, including a lion aggressively breaking the surface of the water with its tongue and a herd of zebra humorously bare their teeth while gently sipping.
David Cameron is seen as less hungry to win the election than Ed Miliband, according to a poll.

A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev had previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev, and is accused of involvement in Nemstov's murder.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before soldiers found him alive. Sonit's face was covered in dust, but he was uninjured and taken to Bhaktapur Hospital. The rescue provides hope to a country devastated by the disaster.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a land use battle over plans to turn a patch of secluded land near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, is trying to prove that the property is historic enough to change its designation and build a center for twelve patients. The property, which includes stone cottages, is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose. The rehabilitation program, founded in 1966, claims to be non-religious and non-profit, but its methods include spending up to five hours a day in a sauna for 30 days straight and mega doses of the vitamin Niacin.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English fluently due to their work with NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. They sleep in market stalls and avoid traveling to see their families. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and new residents reclaiming streets. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment.

Two Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, a Navy spokesman said. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. The two were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two and were not wearing gear at the time. One SEAL died and another was in critical condition at a civilian hospital. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. NBC's host Rebecca Lowe, a former BBC and ESPN journalist, is helping to enhance coverage of the Premier League in America. The move has resulted in more people watching Premier League matches live in the USA than in Britain, with 32 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2013-14.
