Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said on the Andrew Marr Show, as the pair clashed over Labour's leadership. Johnson accused Miliband of "stabbing the country in the back" by forming a deal with the SNP to get into power. Miliband responded that Johnson was "better than that." The exchange ended with a shouting match, with Johnson waggling a finger at Miliband.

A 26-year-old prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The incident occurred when Dustin Irons, who was appearing over video-link, became disgruntled with the proceedings and exposed himself despite being in handcuffs. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days in jail for contempt of court.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since their slow start to the Formula One season, with Fernando Alonso and Button discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. The team is now comparing themselves with the Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses, and Button acknowledges the entire team still has a long way to go. McLaren's improvement in Malaysia, compared to Australia, was due to the cooler temperatures, which could affect tyre temperature and lap-time benefits. Button is excited to see how much change they can make in Shanghai.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco and fined $60,000. The incident has raised concerns about the hospital's sanitation practices and may damage its public image.

Becca Litchfield and her partner Dale, who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for fertility treatment, have welcomed twins and found a way to say their "I do's" after winning a wedding competition.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company offered an apology and removed the inappropriate content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the US caused a commotion by attempting to bark at a husky dog, leading to a video of the two dogs engaging in a humorous vocal exchange. The video, which shows the Shibu Inu attempting to bark at the husky, then responding with a whine, has gone viral and has caused people to laugh and mimic the dogs' actions.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is preparing to lead England in a Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to challenge the opposition and has trained hard to become the fastest bowler on the pitch. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the West Indies' conditions. The competition is fierce, and Plunkett is determined to prove his worth and earn his place in the team.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. The bout is seen as a warm-up for Ward's rematch with Carl Froch, who is also a contender for the title. Froch is willing to travel to the UK to face Smith, but Ward prefers to box in London rather than Nottingham. The WBA has ordered their two super-middleweight champions to meet in a unification fight, and Froch is also considering a first appearance on the Las Vegas Strip against Julio Cesar Chavez Jr.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but her election victory was overshadowed by the departure of the majority of the city's police force, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor. The officials cited 'safety concerns' in their resignations, and residents rallied behind Byrd, saying the town didn't need as many officers as it had. The city, which is 175 miles south of St. Louis, has suffered a spate of break-ins recently, and despite the surge in crime, residents said they almost never saw cops patrolling the streets.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the team is set to make him available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role during City's recent trophy-laden period, is said to be content with life at the Etihad Stadium despite the difficulties and is in no rush to leave. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, are interested but given his huge wages there are some doubts. City, meanwhile, will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, challenging the common belief that these drugs are prescribed for clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of people taking SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant, did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications. This study comes amid a significant increase in antidepressant prescriptions, with the OECD noting a 300% rise in prescriptions since 1998, particularly in the use of SSRIs. The study suggests that many individuals may be misdiagnosed or prescribed antidepressants for conditions other than depression.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter, Natalie, lived with an incurable disease that filled her head with devils that eventually led to her death. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known, and her suicide doesn't change that.

A 10-year-old boy nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. Koby Hodder's heart stopped for a staggering 12 minutes after he collapsed while playing British Bulldog, a game in which children run from one side of a playing field to another without being caught by one of the 'bulldogs', who often employ forceful tactics to trap runners, including rugby tackling opponents to the ground. Koby was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who collapsed after suffering a cardiac arrest during the first half of Bolton's FA Cup quarter-final against Tottenham in 2012. His father, Mark, 45, got a call from the school at around 11am on March 2, and was told to get to the school immediately. He said: 'I was working around the corner so I was able to get straight over there and when I saw Koby on the ground I knew he was

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed reforms to divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. The current system requires couples to cite one of five reasons for divorce, with unreasonable behavior being the most widely used. Lady Hale suggests a one-year cooling off period after declaring that the marriage has permanently broken down, during which couples would be encouraged to sort out arrangements for children and money. This overhaul aims to make the divorce process more equitable and less reliant on fault-based claims.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a synthetic surface beneath a grass pitch, allowing for NFL-style games. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and the proposed stadium could be more suitable for NFL games than Wembley, which has hosted NFL matches since 2007. The new stadium would have a capacity of 65,000, which is more realistic than Wembley's 90,000 seats.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia from the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, are calling for economic sanctions against Russia and the condemnation of the Putin regime.

Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. The husband of the author, Erika Leonard, will write the script for the second film, and Sam Taylor-Johnson is no longer directing the sequel.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and his overall record is one of the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently the only manager in the Premier League with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but he is facing a difficult season with West Bromwich Albion, who are currently stuck on 33 points and facing four of their final five fixtures against Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Arsenal. Pulis has a good reputation as a smart tactician and able to get the best out of players and bend the laws of the game

Fenerbahce, a Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus drove to the airport after a match in Turkey's Super Lig. The injured driver, who was taken to hospital, is seeking medical attention. Fenerbahce has stated that the attack is not solved in a way that satisfies the club and public opinion, and a suspension of the championship is inevitable. The incident followed Fenerbahce's 5-1 win against Rizespor.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more. The avalanche, which occurred during the earthquake that killed over 4,300 people in Nepal, left climbers and local workers dazed and shocked. Helicopters rescued hundreds of stranded climbers, but many were unable to descend on their own due to the dangerous Khumbu Icefall. The avalanche struck Base Camp, while climbers at higher camps were able to avoid it.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, found himself again in the middle of war in Ukraine decades later. Margolin, who survived one war, was able to survive another, even as a stray missile hit his house on February 10, killing his daughter Ira. The family, who had settled in Donetsk, Eastern Ukraine, moved to Israel, where they arrived on March 24. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews, an organization that works to build interfaith understanding and support for Israel, has brought 600 Jews to Israel since December, including Margolin.

John Carver, a former assistant to Ruud Gullit, is relishing the chance to take charge of Newcastle United against Sunderland on Sunday. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson in a 1999 derby led to Newcastle's defeat and Gullit's eventual resignation. Carver's memories of the incident remind him of the potential consequences of such decisions. The match is crucial for Carver's chances of winning the head coach position beyond the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He spoke about the need for reform in national policing legislation and the importance of using this moment to change what is happening in North Charleston. Sharpton also denied that Scott's family barred him from attending his funeral on Saturday because it would cause a 'circus' of media attention.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as 'hippy crack', and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. The 20-year-old faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action over his behaviour, and Liverpool manager Rodgers now says he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails.

Union barons gave more than £1 million to Labour in the second week of the election campaign, swelling the party's war chest and boosting Ed Miliband's chances of winning the election. The donations, which equate to £105,420.80 a day, came from Unison, USDAW, and Unite, with Unite's donations worth more than £400,000. The Conservatives received just £492,512 in donations, while the Liberal Democrats and Ukip received £50,000 and £8,000 respectively. The union donations exposed the type of government Ed Miliband would lead as Prime Minister, with the Conservatives saying they would demand more spending, borrowing, higher taxes, and a bigger welfare bill.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight were stranded at Manchester Airport for five hours after their plane was diverted due to severe winds, causing a delay in their return flight to Doha. Police were called to the tarmac twice, first to address disruptive passengers and then again after the delay caused by the initial diversion. The airline apologized for the inconvenience, arranging for passengers to be transported to Manchester.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will accompany boxing champion Floyd Mayweather Jr. into the ring for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday in Las Vegas. Bieber, who has been Mayweather's friend for years, has accompanied the fighter on numerous occasions, including a press conference in May. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record, is expected to be the main attraction at the event, with Bieber joining him as part of his entourage.

The article discusses the closure of Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college that has been struggling to hold accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled more than 70,000 students, is one of the worst "predator colleges" that offer dubious degrees, saddle students with high amounts of debt, and gobble up tens of billions of dollars in federal money every year. The closure of Corinthian is a positive development in a long struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club on Thursday after 'being blamed' for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola has played down the feud. Muller-Wohlfahrt's decision came after Bayern boss Guardiola appeared to imply that the defeat was down to a lack of available players.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden in New York for a world title defence against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, believes age is not a disadvantage and that his experience and preparation have helped him maintain his dominance in the heavyweight division.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has admitted he will "miss" fronting the BBC2 show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said it would be "great" if she were invited back to front Top Gear. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract, citing his "crossing of the line".

In a bizarre incident during a La Liga match, Barcelona's Sergio Busquets was given a straight red card for throwing a lump of grass at Celta Vigo's Fabian Orellana during the closing stages of the game. The incident led to Orellana being shown the red card, and Busquets was able to grab his eye despite the turf striking him. Barcelona earned a crucial three points, while Real Madrid won 9-1 against Granada earlier in the day.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the finish line of the Boston Marathon. In 2015, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, one of the bombers, was convicted of using weapons of mass destruction, bombing a place of public use, conspiracy, and aiding and abetting. The sentencing phase of his trial began on April 21, and the judge warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the anniversary or the current running of the marathon.

Millions of Chinese people traveled to their ancestral villages for the annual Qingming Festival, marking the start of spring and honoring their loved ones. The festival, which falls in the first week of April, involves cleaning tombs, burning fake paper money, and leaving food and drink to ensure the deceased are not hungry or poor in the afterlife. The festival is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and is celebrated with parades, outdoor celebrations, and traditional dances.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits from Simon & Garfunkel and solo work, has outsold more youthful musicians such as Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping to propel him to the top of the charts.

Iker Casillas, the 33-year-old goalkeeper for Real Madrid, insists he will stay at the club even if David de Gea, a Manchester United player, arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. Casillas, who has been at the Bernabeu since breaking into the team as a 16-year-old, claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he made his own. Real Madrid has linked to a move for de Gea, while the Spanish giants are determined to defend their Champions League title, having reached the semi-finals with a 1-0 aggregate victory over Atletico Madrid.

David Cameron said the Conservatives had overseen a 'jobs miracle' and Britain had created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU put together. The number of people in work rose above 31 million in the three months to February, official figures showed. The IMF praised Chancellor George Osborne's 'wonderful job' of handling the economy. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth more than £6 billion, to power passenger jets for the Middle Eastern airline Emirates. The fiscal deficit has been significantly reduced over the last few years, and the UK and the UK economy has done a wonderful job in the last couple of years, George Osborne said.

SsangYong, a Korean car manufacturer, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli, priced under £13,000, in the UK. The SUV is aimed at thrifty motorists who want a value-for-money car. It comes in three trim levels, with a choice of front-wheel drive or 4x4, and has seven airbags. The entry-level SE model starts at £12,950 and comes with 16-inch alloys, cruise control, and seven airbags. The top-of-the-range ELX model, from £16,000 to £19,000, includes a TomTom navigation system with a 7-inch touch screen and a rear-view camera. SsangYong expects the Tivoli to double the firm's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 a year.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10in-tall, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers. The creation was inspired by a customer's request for a burger with three kinds of meat.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, which serves high-quality meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef, has opened to the public at a higher price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, offers meals like organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen, which has been open to the public since earlier this week, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is now feeling much better and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has 30 Grammy nominations and has won his first Grammy in 1970 for "The Thrill Is Gone." King suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago last year, forcing him to cancel the remainder of his tour.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The event, known as the 2015 Easter Parade, featured a diverse range of headwear, from elaborate ship-shaped hats to rabbit puppets and floral bonnets. The parade, which has been held annually since the 1880s, was a mix of religious and secular attire, with both Christians and non-religious participants joining the festivities. The event, which attracted a wide range of attendees, from churchgoers to atheists, showcased creativity and individuality in headwear.

Emergency crews in East of England received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including one woman who phoned to say she felt ill after eating too much takeaway food and a man who reported that his feet were hurting after wearing shoes that were too tight.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. The players aimed to sink balls into the boot of a car from close range and from long range, with Hazard and Ake winning the first round and the final round. The final challenge involved shooting at cars from long range, with Willian and Remy winning the game but damaging one of the Audi cars in the process.

Brendan Rodgers has criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, suggesting that the player is being manipulated by outside forces and that he would be inclined to stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Sterling has rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season, but Rodgers said: 'I've had a good chat with him. I have given him my opinion on it. This is a young kid who has been advised to do something else. A 20-year-old boy does not pick up the phone to ask to speak to the BBC. 'You don't do that; him in particular. He just wants to play his football. But of course if he's asked to do that by other parties then that's what he'll do. 'In the modern game it is obviously something that frustrates us all but it is the market and where football is at. In fairness to

Rachel Riley, Countdown co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up a rude eight-letter word as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as a blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word 'erection'. The incident is not the first time the show's host has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who was arrested after attempting to buy deadly poison online, was spared jail after pleading guilty to the charge. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, expressed an interest in buying the poison and showed awareness of its toxicity. He was arrested during a raid on two homes in Tameside on February 16. The dark web is a subsection of the deep web, used for illegal activities such as selling drugs and sharing pornographic photographs.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The death came just months after three babies and one mother died at the maternity unit. The deaths, along with those of four babies and two mothers at the Royal Oldham Hospital, prompted an investigation. Lianne Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, and his sister, Karen, have called for action to prevent further tragedies at North Manchester General Hospital.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a seven-year-old mother of a little girl named Emily, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born seven months after he was born in 2006. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said that Pittman trained every second day and was careful to monitor her core temperature throughout her training program.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and missing people. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was rescued by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm affected about 100 sailboats and 200 people, with scattered boats across Mobile Bay. At least one person was confirmed dead, and the mayor of Dauphin Island reported that the storm was the worst they had seen.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has been diagnosed with macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that are getting progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Barr said in the interview that she helps relieve the pressure by using marijuana. The combination of the two diseases is terrible. Macular degeneration takes away her central vision, and glaucoma is taking away her peripheral vision. The risk for both diseases goes up for everyone after age 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager, Chancey Luna, was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. Luna was found guilty of the crime after a jury recommended he be sentenced to life in prison without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant only to scare Lane when he shot him from a passing car.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his team's poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their match against Chelsea on Sunday. Wenger has lost seven and drawn five of their 12 encounters. Chelsea, who are 10 points ahead, are expected to be favored, but Wenger believes Arsenal can still win.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career fighting in the Far East before gaining recognition in 2001 when he fought against Lehlo Ledwaba in an IBF world super-bantamweight title fight in Las Vegas. He has since made a remarkable rise through the weight divisions and is set to face Mayweather in the Fight of the Century on Saturday.

A young footballer named Jack Grealish has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that is considered illegal. The incident has sparked debate about the role of drugs in professional sports and the need for athletes to prioritize their health. Grealish, who has been praised for his performance, has been compared to Arsenal's Arsene Wenger, who emphasized the importance of professional athletes taking care of their bodies. The incident has led to a discussion about the balance between enjoying oneself and making the right choices for one's career.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality TV star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men with eggs on Easter Monday after being targeted online for his appearance. The attack occurred at a pub in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, where Barton had checked in on Facebook minutes before the incident. The attackers, who tracked Barton down using his Facebook posts, threw six eggs at him, leaving him with yolk and shell on his face. Barton believes he was targeted because he had "checked in" at the pub on Facebook minutes earlier. The attack came just two days after Barton spent the day being pampered at a beauty salon and enjoying drinks with reality show stars Joey Essex and Harry Derbidge. Barton is currently in debt of £100,000 on 15 credit cards and store cards, and has admitted to going bankrupt after racking up debts of £35,00

Manchester University in Indiana was on lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police said they received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. The university issued a shelter in place warning and continued to repost the message for hours after the original message. No injuries have been confirmed, and the university's website says that it is the home of the country's first peace studies program.

Edinson Cavani, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, prepares to face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Despite PSG's suspension of key players and injuries, Cavani must overcome Barcelona's star-studded lineup to progress beyond the last eight. His reputation as a prolific striker and recent goal drought have raised questions about his future in Paris.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, won a unanimous points decision with scores of 114-112, 114-112, and 115-112. Mathews, known for his relentless style, kept Luis contained behind the jab and landed a decent uppercut in the second round. Luis, who was forced to pull out due to visa issues, showed aggression in the closing rounds but was unable to overcome Mathews' superior performance.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory, overcoming a 12-10 deficit after the break. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, while St Helens' Jordan Turner scored a try and Tom Makinson added the conversion. The win was Hull's first since their derby defeat to Hull KR on Thursday.

The U.S. Census figures predict that the undocumented and documented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the population. By 2060, the immigrant population could reach 78 million, representing 82% of the total population. The Center for Immigration Studies report suggests that immigration will steadily increase over the next 45 years, totaling 64 million immigrants. Without any changes to current immigration policy, the total immigrant population in the United States will reach 14.8% of the population by 2023, and 15.8% by 2030, 17.1% by 2040, and 18.8% by 2060. The growth in immigrant population has important implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Arsenal Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading U21s in a top-of-the-table clash, with former Arsenal defender Martin Keown's son Niall scoring the only goal. Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury but could not prevent the defeat.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a poor performance in Florida. Rose, who has been in the top five for the last three years, has hit 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signed for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose believes that he has done some good work over the past two weeks and feels like he is going in the right direction again.

A Mayfair mansion that once served as a milking parlour has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which now features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was originally used as a milking parlour and a depot before being demolished in the 19th century. The mansion, which is 8, 139 square feet, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank for £25 million.

Bayern Munich's squad is weakened by injuries, but the team's unity is stronger, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles this season, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Muller believes the team's recent games played with a decimated squad will help them build a strong unit on the pitch. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on the scoring prowess of Muller and Robert Lewandowski in the absence of Robben and Ribery. The team will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-final, first leg on April 15, followed by a second leg on April 18.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. After a victory by Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted they were surprised by Vettel's win and Ferrari's tactics. Mercedes struggled with a three-stop strategy, with Vettel's Ferrari stopping twice compared to three for Hamilton and Rosberg. The team needs to analyze why Vettel's car performed better in high temperatures.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, is the first time nitrogen gas has been used in an execution in the United States. Fallin's office claims the method is quick and painless, with the person becoming unconscious within 8-10 seconds and death occurring a few minutes later. The bill, authored by Rep. Mike Christian, is seen as a compromise to address concerns about the state's execution process, which has been put on hold while the U.S. Supreme Court reviews its use of lethal injections. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous and that capital punishment must be performed effectively and without cruelty.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, was unstable due to empty fuel tanks and a lack of ballast. The sinking occurred at 4am local time, and the trawler did not send any distress signals. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The ship tipped over when a fishing net weighing 80 tons was pulled in, and two bodies have been found. The incident occurred at around 4am local time, and temperatures in the water can dip to as low as -2 degrees Celsius.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a pioneering drug originally meant for women, according to new clinical trials. Olaparib, already used to treat women with breast cancer, showed promise in extending the length of time that men with genetic defects in their prostate cancer tumours live without the disease getting worse. The drug, called olaparib, is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her photography skills and globetrotting into a business by launching a website called 'In Bed With' to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, Taylor has built relationships with hotels and PR companies over the past seven years, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature their properties on her site. Taylor has photographed and reviewed hotels in locations such as Australia, Indonesia, and the US, and has generated further income from featuring companies on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association is investigating an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. QPR are unlikely to face disciplinary action, but the FA will seek observations from each club and ensure that QPR and the police are taking the necessary steps to identify the culprit via CCTV and for them to face a banning order. Chelsea's celebrations were marred by objects being thrown onto the pitch by the crowd, and the club is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses to come forward.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police did not say how he died, they did not rule out homicide. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is raising money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, was forced to resign from the shadow cabinet after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside, which was seen as hypocrisy in her opposition to the right to buy policy. The incident highlighted Thornberry's ownership of expensive properties, including a £3 million home in north London.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during a chase for an artificial scent. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attackers, Wiltshire Police dropped the investigation three months later, angering Lane and hunt supporters.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. He says he wants to stay at the club because he is very happy here. Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. Reports have linked Gomes with a move to Premier League duo Manchester United and Chelsea, but he denies being contacted by Premier League leaders Chelsea. Gomes says he just thinks about spending the next season in Spain.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice on Christmas Eve in Bali while holidaying with her family. The 19-year-old claims she was lured to a remote home by a man named Henry Alafu, who then attacked her twice. Alafu allegedly lured her to a villa and raped her, and then forced her into a taxi where he raped her again. Ms Pekin sought help from passing motorists and workers in a nearby service station, but Alafu allegedly told them to ignore her. CCTV footage captured Alafu waiting in the lobby for Ms Pekin, as she stopped at the hotel before they continued with their night out.

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features James holding a fake skinned fox, with the slogan "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat." Harvey Nichols has since re-introduced its fur-free policy, with a range of fur products priced between £300 and £1,500. PETA is currently in talks with billboard companies to mount the campaign outside Harvey Nichols.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in recognizing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet enacting a new law on Monday. The new law will take effect in six months and will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, having led the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2005/06, surpassing Manchester United's record of 262 days. The Blues are currently leading by seven points with a game in hand on their rivals.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese territory off the coast of Africa, is tapping into its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, which has few natural resources, is promoting music and culture as a way to attract visitors and create jobs. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been held in Cape Verde for seven years, has become a major event, attracting artists from around the world and bringing people from all over the globe to share in the music. The festival has helped to showcase Cape Verde's unique musical styles, such as the batuque and morna, and has helped to promote the country's cultural heritage.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney's Opera House went viral for the second time after being uploaded to Twitter by popular Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa, quickly being reposted by other sources. The video, originally posted by Sydney resident Darren Johnson following strong storms and tandem heavy swells in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot.

Reading, the FA Cup semi-finalists, were defeated 1-0 by Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium on Wednesday night. Reading dominated most of the match but wasted several chances in the closing stages. Birmingham's Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who had fumbled a crucial goal against Arsenal in the last four of the Cup, was retained against Birmingham.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, has been ruled out of the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury sustained during a run against Andre-Pier Gignac. The Brazilian defender will miss at least four weeks, potentially impacting PSG's title defense and their upcoming quarter-final against Barcelona.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. The show's illegal downloads have increased by 45% year-on-year, jumping from 4.9 million in 2014 to 7 million in 2015. Brazil, France, the US, Canada, and the UK are the top countries for illegal downloads of Game of Thrones episodes. HBO has announced that the forthcoming season will air across 170 countries at the same time and has launched a new internet streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

The town of Celoron, New York, has faced backlash over a statue of Lucille Ball, a beloved comedian, that locals find unflattering. The statue, based on a moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," has attracted criticism on social media, with a Facebook page calling for its removal. The anonymous creator of the page, who describes himself as a "big fan of Lucy's," argues that the statue should be more like statues of other comedians. The town has tried to honor Ball with a museum, but the statue controversy has overshadowed this effort.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st lost nearly half her body weight after being forced to stand during an 11-hour flight due to her fear of crushing the woman in the seat next to her. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, had struggled to fit in the plane seat before and now weighs in at a healthy 9st 9lb, having lost 4st through joining a slimming club and another 4-and-a-half stone after taking up running.

A new mother, Nicola Bonn, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences of raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy and the challenges she faced. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shared a post about why she stopped justifying herself and the hurdles she faced, such as the overwhelming opinions of others.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, have been reported missing after allegedly traveling to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for his role in a terrorist plot. The families are in shock and are calling for information about their sons' whereabouts.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described the pain of losing his daughter, who had planned a perfect wedding for her childhood sweetheart, Aaron Leeson-Woolley. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but now the family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who wants to leave the club this summer. The Saints are also monitoring Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, and Eljero Elia, a Dutch winger, who is on loan from Werder Bremen. Southampton is currently seventh in the Premier League table and is on track to qualify for the Europa League.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment designed to encourage visitors to dwell and take in the atmosphere. The move was intended to attract a new audience but was met with criticism from heritage experts who deemed it patronizing. The Trust has since announced similar experiments at nine other venues around the country.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the side of the road with a flat tyre, but was helped by his driver to change it. Felicity Waterford, a mother waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, noticed the vehicle and offered assistance. The former PM, who was a complete gentleman, agreed to a selfie with Ms Waterford. This incident came just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes Barton's comments about the team's inability to finish the game were justified. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, highlighting the importance of finishing games. The teams will meet again at the Hawthorns on Saturday.

A new species of monkey has been discovered after scientists learned to distinguish it by the appearance of its penis. The white-cheeked macaque was discovered in the remote highland forests of south-east Tibet after researchers set up camera traps.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for an eight-day trip, including a stay at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan. The visit is their first to the country, where they are exploring landmarks and attending cultural events. The Kardashian-West crew is staying in the capital's finest digs, with bodyguards and police in tow. The city is known for its cultural and economic significance, with a mix of Soviet-era architecture and Neo-Classical official buildings.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now facing the possibility of losing it to the local town hall due to illegal alterations made by a previous owner. The couple, who are retired and plan to move back to the UK, are currently locked in a dispute over the property, which is located in Los Alcornocales Natural Park in the Andalusian province of Cadiz.

Apple reported strong sales of its iPhone in the first quarter of 2015, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for over two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone's sales growth in China was particularly notable, with a 72% increase over the previous quarter.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van that she believes may have caused her mother's death in a car crash. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, believes the van may have been involved in a series of hit-and-run accidents in the area. The incident occurred in February 2023, and the crash was ruled a tragic accident by Virginia police.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally neutral events, such as neutral events like a lunch date, and how emotion affects memory retention. Emotion increases the strength of our memory over time, a process called consolidation. Strong emotion can strengthen memory for positive events, such as a surprise birthday party, and for negative events, such as making an embarrassing faux pas.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The surgery is scheduled for Wednesday, and Jahnae and her girlfriend have reached their fundraising goal. Although Jackson's surgery is likely to save his life, he will have a long road of rehabilitation ahead.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back with 15 months left on his contract, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha played for QPR in their crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that shows the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US, revealing that every state has its own set of phrases that can seem bizarre to the rest of the English-speaking world. The map focuses on the US, but also has a small amount of data for the UK. The overall pattern was clear; In the South people found that sentence to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and took videos of himself rocking and making gestures. The journey was part of his work, and he met his dad along the way.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a 'win bonus' of sweets and chocolate to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus was sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack under the desk.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the Premier League darts event in his hometown of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place in the table. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has commended Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his crucial role in the club's Ligue 1 campaign, emphasizing his off-field contributions. Despite Ibrahimovic's suspension for the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona, Verratti believes the Swedish striker's influence extends beyond the pitch, helping young players and boosting team morale.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details on the Falklands Islands' defenses, including GPS coordinates and runway depth, on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The information was accessible to anyone, including Argentine intelligence agents, and was available for download. The MoD acknowledged the mistake but denied it was particularly sensitive. The incident highlights the ongoing sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina over the Falklands Islands.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to kick-start his team's offensive struggles as they look to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have lost all three games over the Easter holiday period and have a poor defensive record. Anderson attributes the team's poor start to the games coming thick and fast. If Huddersfield can win their next game, they could leapfrog their French visitors, who have won just one of five away games so far this year.

Planners in Windsor have approved two Costa coffee shops, one of which is less than 500 yards from the other, in a move that has sparked controversy. The new Costa will open at the site of a former HSBC branch, while the other Costa replaced a cycle shop earlier this year. This has led to concerns from residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the controversial pilot culls of free-running badgers, which were to be completed by trapping and shooting the animals. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling had not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' of badgers could be effective and humane. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, while animal welfare campaigners welcomed the news but criticized the BVA's ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting. The culls have been fiercely criticized by wildlife groups, and the Environment Secretary pledged that any future Conservative government would 'take the difficult decisions to deal with this disease' and not walk away from the strategy.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow has accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying he received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves. Artists have long railed against low royalties paid from streaming companies, leading to Jay-Z launching his own Tidal service, promising bigger returns for musicians.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. The first four episodes of the show's next season are titled The Wars to Come, The House of Black and White, High Sparrow and The Sons of the Harpy. They had been downloaded more than 550, 000 times as of early Sunday morning.

A best man left guests at his brother's wedding in tears after composing an emotional song to use as his best man's speech. Melbourne singer Daniel Buccheri, who composed the tune to the popular music from artists such as Sam Smith and the Backstreet Boys, toasted his brother Adrian and his new wife Sarah at their March 29 wedding in using his voice. The unique speech performed by Daniel at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, east of Melbourne, has been viewed over 100,000 times online and included tributes to his brother and his bride and also delves into his childhood and says he always looked up to his older sibling.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after the birth of her daughter Mia by hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up. The 33-year-old, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, has committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was seen as ill-timed and unprofessional, and it has been speculated that Sterling's agent may have engineered the situation. Sterling returned to training ahead of the weekend's game against Arsenal and was linked with a move to Arsenal. Liverpool fans have a popular mantra that no player is bigger than the club, but they are now of the belief that if Sterling wants to go, he is welcome to.

Barcelona's 1996-97 team, led by former Barcelona coach Luis Enrique and assistant Jose Mourinho, included current PSG coach Laurent Blanc, Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, and four other coaches from the same club at the same time. The team won the Spanish Super Cup against Atletico Madrid 6-4 on aggregate.

Former Manchester United striker Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore the best player in the world, saying he is the most creative and exciting player. Cantona watched two games of Pastore's and praised his ability to pass and score spectacular goals. He also suggested that Spain's World Cup victory in 2010 was due to Barcelona's influence on the national team.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder after killing his tenant, Michael Spalding, 39, and dismembering his body. Simon forced Spalding to decorate his flat before attacking him when he refused to work. He then hacked the body up and stuffed the head, limbs, and tools into two suitcases, which he threw into a canal with help from his girlfriend, Michelle Bird, 35. The court heard Simon murdered Spalding by stabbing him in the neck at the flat they shared in Smethwick, Birmingham, on April 26 last year. The case was heard at Birmingham Crown Court, and Bird was cleared of murder and manslaughter but admitted assisting an offender.

Two county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have implemented 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents are most likely to suffer from social isolation. The maps are based on statistics on public health factors and surveys of residents to identify those who rarely speak to their neighbors, are unsatisfied with their social life, and say they don't have someone to talk to. The maps are used to target vulnerable areas and help local councils reach those in need. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the maps as a way of treating the problem across the country.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she's ever had or ever wanted. She remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents at the restaurant she's worked at for half-a-century. Eddingfield says she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat on her first day, but it was forgiven after the coat was cleaned. She has two brothers, her sister, her mother, two aunts, two cousins, and lots of friends who have worked at the restaurant. Eddingfield met her first husband outside the restaurant and they married 18 months later.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting believes England needs to have players who are not playing well to get Pietersen in, and that if he does get runs, it's not the end of it. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014, and Gatting admits more questions will be asked of the England skipper if he fails to find runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student named Caleb Benn developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day in revenue. However, the app has been accused of violating Instagram's terms of service, and the company has threatened to take legal action against Benn. The app's success has led to concerns about the potential for abuse and the impact on Instagram's ecosystem.

Koreans have a tradition of drinking together called hoesik, which involves multiple rounds of alcohol at multiple venues. Foreign business travelers may feel pressure to participate, but drinking etiquette is important. Koreans consider drinking a way to get to know someone, and drinking is a big part of Korean life. To avoid offending someone, follow these seven rules: identify the "higher" person in the relationship, defer to them, and turn your body away from senior figures when drinking.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who believe the outdated and outdated practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The controversy has split the Gold Coast community, with business leaders calling for the end of an era, while local business owners label the group as outdated and no longer providing a service.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece will in fact make the payment on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but the country is heavily indebted and has not received bailout funds since August last year.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The government blocked access to social media platforms because the images were "deeply upset" the prosecutor's family.
A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a letter to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would help Jedi avoid becoming Sith.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA basketball tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak. Wisconsin advances to the final, while Kentucky finishes the season with 38 wins, two short of becoming the first undefeated team since 1975-76.

Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe's lead singer, was criticized for his rendition of the American national anthem at a football game, prompting comparisons to past performances by Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton.

A video of a violent altercation between brothers Patrick and Barry Lyttle, who were reunited for a holiday in Australia, has been released for the first time. The video shows Patrick pushing his brother Barry, who retaliates with a single punch that causes his brother to fall to the ground. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and has pleaded guilty. Magistrate Graeme Curran said a jail sentence was likely, and Barry could spend up to two years in a Sydney jail. The brothers were reunited for a night out in Kings Cross, and the video shows them exchanging words before the fight escalated. Patrick was treated by paramedics at the scene and was found in a pool of blood and vomit. The matter is set to return to court for a possible sentencing hearing.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite stripped of mementos and flowers after cemetery staff cleared the baby section of the site. The Howies had built a small shrine at the gravesite, which they had maintained since the funeral, but everything was removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not been notified that they would be cleaned, and the Howies were only able to retrieve about 25 percent of their memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, Britain's most senior judge, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer put to death in Missouri this year. The execution took place on Tuesday night at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. The inmate declined to order a last meal and received the day's inmate tray meal of a turkey and bologna sandwich, a cookie, and fruit punch. The execution was carried out by lethal injection. Governor Jay Nixon, who refused a clemency petition, read a statement about the importance of remembering Anthony Curtis and his loved ones.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. The prince will return to Australia in mid-May to meet the new royal baby.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has placed a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, claiming he is the "new Messi" and that Paris Saint-Germain will have to spend big to sign him. Dybala is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG, with Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini spotted watching the Serie A match between Parma and Palermo. Zamparini claims Dybala is worth €40 million but is willing to negotiate for €50 million, with PSG being the fiercest competition.

In Brazil, thousands of protesters have taken to the streets in demonstrations against President Dilma Rousseff, who is facing an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at the state-run oil company Petrobras. Rousseff's supporters are holding rallies in her support, while her opponents are calling for her impeachment. Petrobras was once considered Brazil's corporate jewel, but an investigation into a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme has led to widespread protests. The country is divided, with roughly half of the voting population not voting for Rousseff, and many of those who did joined protests immediately after the election. The Petrobras scandal has grown, and the economy is expected to contract this year, with inflation and currency value both at record highs.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, You and the Night, includes a scene with Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a "beautiful" work of art. The film has been both praised and criticized, with some calling it an "orgy" and others an "artistic failure".

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding. The so-called digital seasoning also applies to wine, helping drinkers to enjoy their tipple by up to 15 per cent more, if served alongside the right music.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have stalled. Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, is reportedly considering a move to Arsenal or Spain. Taylor, the PFA chief, believes Sterling should wait until the end of the season to resume contract talks, as it is "not necessarily a bad thing" for both club and player to focus on football and other matters. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ohio woman La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, who works at the same call-center operation company as her, after the Ohio Department of Health released birth records for people born between January 1, 1964, and September 18, 1996. The two met after connecting on Facebook, and Simmons called Mitchell-Clark, who had been searching for her biological mother for almost her entire life. The reunion was a relief for the family, and Mitchell-Clark found out she had three younger sisters she didn't know about.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and sent him an assault rifle and handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges and faces up to 30 months in prison.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but the incident led to Parker being arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, while also acknowledging the influence of his agent on players.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a 53-year-old Italian who had worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife on a reconstruction project in Pakistan following deadly flooding, was abducted by four armed men on January 19, 2012, along with colleague Bernd Muehlenbeck. Two years later, Lo Porto died accidentally by a U.S. drone strike in Afghanistan and Pakistan, along with Warren Weinstein, a fellow al Qaeda hostage. Lo Porto was a project manager with Welthungerlife's clean water and sanitation program in Pakistan, working with 8 to 10 international staffers and 100 to 200 locals.

A photographer captured a terrifying scene of hundreds of sharks gathered off the coast of south Florida, with one theory suggesting they were Blacktip or Spinner sharks migrating to breed. The photos were shared widely on social media, with experts unsure of the exact species but agreeing they were likely Blacktips or Spinners.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession on Wednesday before he was put down because of a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute for the police dog, who served eight years in the force, began around 4:45 pm and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital. The tribute was held by the Ridgefield Police Department, fellow officers, and residents of Ridgefield. Zeus was being taken to Ridgefield Veterinary Clinic where he was to be euthanized. The vehicles traveled from the police headquarters and ended at the veterinary hospital. The grand procession was held in Ridgefield, Connecticut, and was attended by officers from the department and police departments across the state.

Since Operation Yewtree, the number of child sex abuse reports has risen by 60% in the UK, with thousands more people contacting police. However, the number of arrests fell by 9% and the number of prosecutions and convictions dropped. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation was launched.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park and Svartalfheim providing stunning settings for Game of Thrones and Thor: The Dark World, respectively. The country's dramatic landscapes, including the Svinafellsjokull glacier and Dettifoss waterfall, have been used in Interstellar, Prometheus, and Game of Thrones.
A 100-year-old mechanic’s garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, while a 1850’s goal in Victoria has been converted into a home.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2021. The rare condition, which causes uncontrollable shaking and neurological symptoms, has left her unable to walk and confined to her house. She now takes 32 different medications daily to manage her symptoms, including choking fits and tremors.

The statue of Lucille Ball, depicting her intoxicated pitch for the Vitameatavegamin health tonic, has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York. Sculptor Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has admitted to being "disappointed" in his work and offered to fix it for free. Poulin pledged to make a new one, but the town's mayor said the statue should be removed.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, out for seven weeks with a torn knee ligament, will miss the end of the season after being ruled out for another seven weeks. Alaba, 22, is set to start rehabilitation in about a month. He had been in excellent form for Bayern, helping them stay on track for a treble of titles. Bayern, top of the Bundesliga, will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court today on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring. Nokes, 21, is accused of inciting three young women to sell their bodies for sex. She faces three charges of causing or inciting prostitution in the expectation of gain in September and October last year. Daniel Williams, a 37-year-old Met police officer, is also accused of running the ring and committing several other offenses, including voyeurism and hiding profits in socks stuffed up the chimney of his home. He is suspended from duty and faces seven further charges, including controlling prostitution for gain and using police computers to check clients.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including sensitive teeth, credit card information, and health insurance. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2016 Masters, expressed his thoughts on his autistic sister Ellie, who was not able to attend the tournament. Spieth said he misses his sister and wishes she could have been there to share the victory. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and provided him with perspective. Spieth's victory was considered one of the most prestigious events in sports, and he became the second-youngest winner of the tournament, behind only Tiger Woods.

Dick Advocaat, the Dutch manager of Sunderland, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, despite his previous underestimation of the match in 1998. Advocaat, who has won just twice at home this season, believes that the home crowd will provide an extra weapon for the team, and he is confident that his team can win the game.

A young woman and a butcher in Sydney's eastern suburbs have engaged in a heated argument over a chicken purchase, with the woman claiming she was racially abused and the butcher denying it. The incident occurred at Sam the Butcher in Bondi, where the woman, Belinda Bartholomew, was trying to buy a chicken for a Game of Thrones-inspired feast.
