The woman claims the butcher called her a "f***ing c***" and told her to go to an "Aussie butcher," while the butcher denies the claims and says the woman was the one being rude.

Cadbury has reduced the size of its Freddo Frogs chocolate amphibians by 20 percent, from 15 grams to 12 grams, while keeping the price the same. The change was made due to manufacturing cost increases that the company cannot absorb. The Freddo Frogs were previously 20 grams, and the change is part of a broader trend of declining confectionery sales. The company's profit before tax rose 46 percent from $87 million to $127 million in 2013. The change has been met with anger from chocolate fans, who believe it is not worth the price increase.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday to outline their values and goals for the upcoming presidential campaign, according to a Democrat who attended the meeting. The document, distributed by Robby Mook, outlines the campaign's purpose, goals, and how they plan to win, including avoiding mistakes from Clinton's 2008 campaign. The document mentions issues that sunk Clinton's first campaign and calls for humility, discipline, and unity. Clinton is planning to launch her presidential candidacy on Sunday through a video message on social media, and will travel to Iowa and New Hampshire for early primary and caucus states.

A 29-year-old woman named Kyli Wilfson, who was 26 when she first experienced severe abdominal pain, was diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half. Despite her intense hunger, she was unable to eat without experiencing excruciating pain. Kyli's weight dropped to 80lbs, and she had to rely on a feeding tube to survive. The disease is so rare that it affects less than 0. 01% of people. Kyli found solace in a support group for people with chronic pancreatitis on Facebook.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon posed with a sceptical face in a meme referencing the leaders' debate. The Labour leader, Ed Miliband, was superimposed over London rapper Plan B, issuing a call to 'come at me bruv'. The images were inspired by a debate that saw Miliband warned he would not get into power without lurching left, as Sturgeon told him he is 'not strong enough' to win power on his own. Cameron and Clegg stayed away, with the Prime Minister and his deputy superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb, two men from Brighton who appear on Channel 4 series Gogglebox.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather refused the Fight of the Century. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now looking forward to a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could be a dream come true for Khan, who has been looking forward to fighting in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in at its widest. The property, which has a narrow 'galley kitchen' and a garden, is described as 'well proportioned' by the estate agency. The home, which was put on the market for £750,000 in 2001, is now under offer and has attracted a lot of interest. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon is launching an ambitious manifesto to challenge Labour in the upcoming election, aiming to form a power-sharing deal with the opposition. The SNP's policies overlap with Labour's, including reducing tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, potentially totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP aims to build a "progressive alliance" for policies across the UK, with a focus on infrastructure spending in northern England and Wales. The surge in support for the SNP could lead to constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, where Irish Nationalists surged and ended up with more than 70 seats.

Celtic U17s won the Glasgow Cup 2-0 against Rangers, with Josh Kerr scoring twice. The match was played behind closed doors after trouble at previous finals. Rangers struggled to create chances, and Celtic dominated possession and pressure.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis insisted he will never change his traditional playing style, wearing a cap, track suit, and shiny white trainers at every game. Pulis led his side to a 2-0 victory over his former club Crystal Palace, ending their run of 10 away games without a victory. Pulis will continue to wear his attire at every match, even after the game, to address the press. Pulis has worked wonders at West Brom and virtually assured their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood tests, which suggested they were the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. While dental amalgam has been used for over 150 years and is still commonly used, the amounts taken in from fillings are considered minuscule and there is no evidence to suggest they are anything other than safe to use.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking confidently into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair as Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight's attorney believes that his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, an undefeated professional worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, posed in a lavish feast for her fussy feline Kimchi, a British shorthair, in an interview with Puss Puss magazine. Kimchi, who loves crunchy human food, is described as having a discerning palate and will steal food from her owner's plate if she's not looking. Erskine, who lives in a foodie household, admits that living with a cat isn't to blame for her cat's expensive tastes.

A father in Japan took a photograph of his daughter standing near a rocky outcrop in July 2014. The image, which showed a pair of black boots behind the girl, sparked controversy online. The father, Martin Springall, said he had no idea what the boots could be and that he had no one else in the vicinity. The photograph has been the subject of debate on Reddit, with some believing it was modified or a trick of the light, while others argue it was real. Springall insisted the image was 100% untouched and that he would view it the same way if he saw it online.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will require foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax and national insurance before they can claim benefits. The measures, which will be outlined in the Tory manifesto, will ban EU migrants from receiving state support for four years and will also ban the 'exporting' of child benefit for children living in other EU countries. The changes are aimed at limiting the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU and are part of a broader plan to negotiate a new deal with Europe, including curbing access to benefits.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, eight years old with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and fed by a tube, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital bed because the hospital does not have a suitable bed for him to sleep in. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot he must sleep in to prevent him from injuring himself in the night. Cody's mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with him for the past week, fearing her son will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. She is now demanding answers from the local health trust as she claims she has waited two years for the high-sided bed needed for Cody and other disabled children.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson will provide daily updates from behind the scenes, focusing on Rory McIlroy's chances of completing a career Grand Slam and Tiger Woods' comeback. Ian Poulter forgot his golf clubs, Henrik Stenson is recovering from flu, Tiger Woods will play in the traditional par-three tournament with his children, and Vijay Singh and Martin Kaymer have skipped the water at the 16th hole.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has endured a difficult period at Old Trafford after arriving in an expensive loan deal from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount of at least 5% on the market rate. The sale would be the largest privatisation since the Thatcher era, with a loyalty bonus of one free share for every ten held for at least a year. The move is seen as a Conservative attempt to remind voters of economic problems under Brown's premiership.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' which increase the risk of dementia, according to a study by US researchers. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and are linked to a 46% higher risk of silent strokes in towns and cities. The study involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, decided to undergo radiation treatment in her final weeks, despite the risks and complications. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, wrote an emotional letter to her followers, revealing that she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks and "giggling and drinking green smoothies" until the day she died. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but "some complications arose during the final stages of treatment."

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a five-year-old boy, and chest pain for a five-year-old boy. The crash occurred near Fernvale, with six others, including an infant and two young girls, taken to Ipswich Hospital with minor injuries or for further assessment. A man suffered hand lacerations, and two females escaped injuries. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off, with diversions in place south of Fernvale.

Colorado Gator Farm owner Jason McDonald, 34, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators, surprising the reptiles. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years, said he thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. The imam, Abdul Hadi Arwani, was called to a job in the area he was killed days before his death. When the imam, who had links to the Muslim Brotherhood in the UK and abroad, arrived to the house with his son and not on his own, the supposed potential client asked Arwani to come back another day. The man, who has not been otherwise been identified, also told the imam that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular treat, have sparked a black market, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The bakery has signs warning against buying "fake" cookies, but the demand is so high that knockoffs are made and sold, and the original store hires people to stand in line to buy the goods, which are then resold at a 70% markup. The frenzy in Hong Kong over the buttery treats is not an isolated example, with other foods such as cronuts and ramen burgers also causing food mania.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and anorexia, turned her life around by becoming a bodybuilder. She was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain some weight, but it changed her life and gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She is now a healthy 9. 5st and a personal trainer. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has now been more than two million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square in the 4.20pm at Wincanton on Wednesday, which made him an internet sensation. Ferguson, who was mucking out the stables as usual, was hit by the fence and performed a mid-air somersault. The fall was described as the worst he had ever seen and was only his fifth race. Ferguson escaped the fall and the only real pain was the cut on his nose and the banter from his friends.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. Critics dismissed her efforts as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and "boring as s---," but marketing experts argue that her launch may have been more successful than initially thought. The campaign aims to flip Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic and to change how voters emotionally experience her brand.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday, the first time the school allowed students to sit exams outdoors due to limited indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their chairs and desks to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school reported that the outdoor exam could be a test of the students' organizing capacity and that many students believe it is a novel way to broaden their horizons and feel more relaxed.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a chance for one reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The lucky winner will also receive a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving foam. Joe Hart is the No. 1 goalkeeper for Manchester City and the England national team. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but was adopted by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie proved her parenting skills by raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two have an inseparable bond. Kecil is now preparing for his first public outing this weekend, where he will be displayed for two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her two dogs after being locked in the house for days. The dogs, which had been given medication, ate parts of her body, including her vital organs. The dogs' owners, who found her body, were concerned and called the police. The coroner ruled that the woman may have had a stroke, but there was no evidence of suicide or an accidental fall.

French handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka and 15 other players, is facing fraud charges over their alleged involvement in an illegal betting case. Karabatic, who was briefly detained, competes for France in the Handball World Cup. He denies placing bets on a match in which his Montpellier club lost to a struggling team. The trial is expected to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offenses ranged from inciting sexual activity with a child to rape. The victims, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule, who was sentenced to nine years in jail. The gang used social media to lure victims and sexually abused them. Judge Zoe Smith rejected the defense's argument that the girls came forward because they were victims. The case highlights the importance of reporting sexual offenses and the bravery of the victims in coming forward.

Former New England Patriots player Aaron Hernandez faces multiple trials for murder and other charges in the death of Odin Lloyd, including a potential third trial for a 2012 shooting near Boston. Hernandez is also being sued by the families of two victims and a man who claims he was shot in a Miami limousine.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal will add to Emirates' existing portfolio of sporting sponsorships, including a £150 million deal with Arsenal, a £80 million deal with AC Milan, and a £17 million deal with Hamburg.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio next year, but he won't be swimming at the world championships in Russia this summer. Phelps, who had already qualified in three events before being banned from the last major international meet before the Rio de Janeiro Olympics, said he won't be participating in the world championships due to the punishment set forth by the sport's U.S. governing body.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the team's Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid also lacks Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who is expected to be out for six weeks with a knee ligament strain. Real Madrid's striker Karim Benzema is expected to be fit for the match after missing Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists at Texas Tech University found that more than 50% of pensioners with investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis panicked and sold their stocks after the market fell by 30%. Those who followed that path and sold at the lowest point eight years ago with a pension of £100,000 would only have £63,000 today. If they had resisted the temptation to sell, the same pot would be worth £141,000 today. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, reveals that retirees with better-than-average ability to solve 'logic problems' were more unlikely to make misjudgments in the investment market based on their emotions.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is under pressure to improve the team's fortunes, with Pearce believing the club should give Pellegrini more time to turn things around. The team's recent poor form, particularly a defeat to Manchester United, has contributed to the pressure on Pellegrini.

Manchester United's stars trained in the sunshine on Friday as they prepared for their final match against Manchester City in the Premier League. Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and other key players were in action, with Robin van Persie returning to training after an injury. Manchester United, currently in fourth place, hopes to end their seven-game unbeaten streak against Manchester City, who have won their last three visits to Old Trafford.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma and nine points behind sixth-placed Sampdoria. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to turn their domination into goals.

Miley Cyrus, 22, was photographed at the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy on social media, with some users advising Cyrus to shave her armpits and others defending her choice. Cyrus is not the first, and probably won't be the last, to shun her razor in favor of the fuzz.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance has boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match against Almeria.

A 44-year-old pedestrian named Andrea McVeigh was hit by a cyclist who was riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene and was chased by McVeigh's husband. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to the middle of her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact but then sped off. McVeigh is now off work sick and has two black eyes, a swollen nose, stitches, and feeling very scared to go out onto the street. The police have issued CCTV footage of a cyclist they want to speak to in connection with the crash.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for claiming he could only walk 200 metres when he was actually a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper article describing his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new way to unlock its devices using a user's face. The patent details a system that would automatically unlock the device if the scanned face matches a previously taken photo. The system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table. The patent was filed by the Californian tech giant in March 2011 and awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed she had put on a surgical mask to shield herself from germs and asked if she needed anything. Mrs Sedway initially said she was fine, but when the representative approached her a second time, she indicated that she might require a little extra time to board the plane because she sometimes felt 'weak.' The family eventually boarded the plane and were awaiting takeoff in their seats when an airline representative came on board and announced that the cancer-stricken passenger could not fly without a note from her doctor. The incident has been shared nearly 10,000 times on Facebook.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off, while all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. The incident occurred on Warringah Road at a traffic light intersection. The crash happened during the Easter long weekend, when police warned motorists to obey road rules to avoid similar accidents.

Google has set up a team to boost the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars, according to reports. The team, consisting of four men, is working on flexible and wearable technologies, as well as subfreezing temperature batteries for Project Loon. This follows a similar project by Apple, which has been working on battery life for its devices.

The 223ft Explorer is a superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It is capable of carrying a helicopter, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and inflatables. The yacht is expected to cost approximately 40 million euros to build, making it likely to cost even more to purchase. The layout includes a variety of different areas for guests to retreat to, ensuring they don't get fed up with each other while sailing around the world.

Ed Miliband, Labour leader, announced plans to cap rents in an attempt to help Generation Rent, despite warnings from experts that the plans will backfire, leading to more tenants being evicted and investment in new housing being slashed.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal after a video emerged of him backing Arsenal. The young supporter, Ryan Dearnley, said he hoped Arsenal would win, sparking outrage from Reading fans. The Football Association moved him to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to astronomers seeking to understand what is causing this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may even contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, with a temperature difference of about 70 nano-Kelvins, which is enough to stand out when the entire cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB) of the universe is measured.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is part of the museum's collection and has been housed in various locations since its founding.

A 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, East Sussex, booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland for a One Direction concert in Cardiff, mistaking the Welsh capital for the Irish one. The mistake was discovered when the girlfriend found out about the booking. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has developed a mobile X-ray scanner, the Roboscan 2M Aeria, that can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons. The device, which costs €3 million, is already being used to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe and has helped seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. The device can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in low-security airports. The device can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. He was last seen leaving a hospital in Hampshire and is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair. Munden, formerly of Marchwood, near Southampton, was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. He is believed to have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital and has released images of him with both facial hair and a clean shave. Munden, formerly of Marchwood, near Southampton, was convicted of sexually touching a child under the age of 13 and is subject to a hospital order.

Middlesbrough are top of the Championship, with just four weeks remaining. They have a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth and are favored to win the title. The match against Watford on Monday is a lunchtime kick-off, which could give Middlesbrough an advantage. Watford's Odion Ighalo is excited to play in the English top flight, while Bournemouth's Alex Neil has impressed since taking over at Norwich. The promotion race is so tight that a win for Watford and Bournemouth could change the top two.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women embracing the look on social media and in fashion. The trend has been popularized by models and celebrities, with some embracing the look for its defiant feminist message, while others do it for its cool factor. The trend has been traced back to Jean Paul Gaultier's catwalk show at Paris Fashion Week earlier this month, and has been popularized by models and celebrities such as Rihanna, Lady Gaga, Kelly Osborne, and Nicole Richie.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial difficulties, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after living without gas, water, and electricity for months. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. Their meager funds were stretched to the limit, and they were forced to limit their food intake to one meal a day. The couple had removed their pets from the house to spare their lives, and they left behind two daughters.

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the potential risks of losing the center ground and undoing past sacrifices. Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope to be made Chancellor if the Lib Dems form another coalition with the Conservatives. Clegg also appeared to lean towards another deal with the Tories, saying he deserved "credit" for forming the Coalition while enduring "five years of constant bile from the Labour Party."

A pensioner was attacked by a badger in his garden, but his Jack Russell dog saved him. The badger was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth. The National Farmers' Union advises residents to protect their property from badgers by using badger-proof fencing and keeping bins covered.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto U21s on Wednesday, while the Blues were knocked out of the Champions League. Mourinho visited Fulham's Motspur Park with his son Jose Junior. Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off, but Porto's Leandro Silva scored a hat-trick to progress to the Premier League International Cup final. Chelsea are closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play, 10 points above Arsenal.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured in a December 2014 acid attack on his home in Truro, Cornwall. The attack left him with life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, Sussex, has been charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Mr Christopheros, a father-of-one, used to organise the Run To The Sun event and was a director of Chase 3000, a car rally across Europe planned for 2015. The privately-educated businessman, who attended King's College in Taunton, Somerset, before graduating from Plymouth University, also used to run a holiday park in Newquay.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have been posted next to warnings that urge people not to litter. The signs are part of a campaign to discourage defecation on the trail, which attracts thousands of pilgrims every year. The signs have become an attraction, with pilgrims posing for photos with them. The town's mayor and residents have complained about pilgrims defecating outside their homes.

A massive fire destroyed a building that once housed a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze started at about 1pm and affected only the building itself and a few nearby power lines. The site was not a vacant facility, and an investigation into the cause of the fire continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give Shoshana Hebshi $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search and held her for hours.

An Asiana Airlines flight OZ162 crashed and skidded off the runway at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people. The plane had a tailstrike and spun 180 degrees before landing, facing the wrong way. The crash occurred after the plane missed the landing point at Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea. Local media reported the incident as a crash landing, with images showing hard landing and no sign of landing gear. The airport was closed, and emergency services were at the scene.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality TV star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought from a shop on Sloane Street in Chelsea earlier this year.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The 89-year-old, known for his roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and "Winston Churchill," is auctioning off more than 200 items he has collected over his career. The most unusual item is a hand-painted limewood diorama depicting the Battle of Agincourt in 3D, estimated to fetch £4,000 to £6,000. The sale includes paintings, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and a fine collection of crystal chandeliers.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a man standing on a yellow safety line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which initially appeared to be homophobic, actually revealed that he was observing a public transport safety regulation. The image sparked controversy and led to thousands of comments, with users praising his witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, asking for tips on leg spin bowling almost 20 years ago. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man." The letter included notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers, explaining the difference in coaching between right-handed and left-handed bowlers. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler, also provided advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised virtual reality gaming would be available "this year." Zuckerberg believes VR will create a range of human experiences, and Marriott hotels have already trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent turning. Dong Hui, who is bedridden, whispered to her partner that having him by her side is important. Guo Kai, a firefighter, has been at her bedside every day, and the couple exchanged rings, despite not being able to officially get married.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death after three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has an extensive DUI record in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy. The man was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was forced to apologize for comments suggesting women don't need to ask for raises.

Two Tulsa deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended the drug unit pending a review of the April shooting. The FBI cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery and unqualified training, with the sheriff denying these claims. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

A couple, Katie Prager and Dalton Prager, who married in their teens and suffer from cystic fibrosis, are in a race against time as Katie needs a life-saving lung transplant. Katie was diagnosed with Burkholderia Cepacia in September 2009 and is waiting for a transplant, but her insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Dalton, who has already received new lungs, is pleading for help to save his wife.

The Sleep Cycle app analyzed data from over two million users to discover that the world's earliest wake-up time is on a Monday in South Africa, while the worst mood is experienced on Tuesdays. Slovakia topped the list for national average sleep quality, with the UK in 45th place and the US in 49th. The best sleep quality occurs on a Wednesday night, with over half of countries surveyed reporting the most restful sleep on this day. The app tracks sleep phases using a pre-defined 30-minute alarm window and has more than two million active users.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written between 1946 and 1949, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, 25 of which are headed to auction, were written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949 and saved by Jose until his death in 1995. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance, is popular with Labour activists but is seen as a threat to British politics. He is linked to Unite, a powerful union with a claimed membership of 1.42 million, which has a close relationship with the Labour Party. McCluskey's socialist policies, including increased public sector spending and higher taxes, are seen as problematic by some.

A zookeeper at the Zoological Center in Tel Aviv captured footage of animals drinking water in their unique ways using a GoPro camera placed at the bottom of their water troughs. The footage, totaling 30 hours, shows a variety of animal behaviors, including a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water and a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper, Elad Hershkowitz, cut the footage down to four minutes and noted that some animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to it. The experiment was conducted to offer a unique perspective on animal drinking behavior.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, a poll reveals today as the Prime Minister tries to step up his campaign passion.

A man accused of assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, one of five Chechen men accused of killing Nemstov, told the court he was abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing. Dadaev previously confessed to the murder but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. Dadaev is being held with his cousins, Anzor and Shagid Gubahsev, and other suspects. The outspoken politician was shot in the back four times as he crossed a bridge near the Kremlin and Red Square in Moscow. More than 20, 000 people marched through the capital city in protest of his murder, holding posters of his face and signs saying 'I am not afraid'.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before soldiers found him at 10 a.m. on Sunday. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue, but he was uninjured. The rescue provides hope to a country devastated by the disaster.

A Church of Scientology-affiliated drug rehabilitation center, Narcocon, is attempting to change the designation of a historic property near Camp David to build a drug rehab center. The property, Trout Run, is valued at $4. 85 million and has been bought by a real estate company in 2013. Narcocon claims that the property is historic and can be used for drug rehabilitation, but opponents argue that the zoning laws do not permit such a use. The rehabilitation program, founded in 1966, is based on the teachings of Scientology's founder L. Ron Hubbard and claims to eliminate addiction cravings through a regimen of exercise, sauna sessions, and vitamin therapy. The program can cost more than $30, 000 per month and typically lasts for six months.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the economic and social impact on Kabul. Five men who once spoke English due to their work with NATO are now blacklisted and isolated, sleeping in market stalls and avoiding their families. The city has transformed, with its population swelling and violence in the provinces causing people to flee. Neighborhoods that were once overpriced have become empty, and even popular tourist spots like Chicken Street are deserted. The article highlights the contrast between the city's current state and its former glory, with the U.S. Embassy and NATO declining to comment.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base on Friday. The incident occurred at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story, where the two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, which contains SEAL teams. The sailors were swimming in lap lanes and were not wearing gear at the time. One was pronounced dead, and the second is listed in critical condition. An investigation into the incident is ongoing.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. NBC's host Rebecca Lowe, a former BBC and ESPN journalist, is helping to enhance coverage of the Premier League in America. The move has resulted in more people watching Premier League matches live in the USA than in Britain, with 32 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2013-14.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said on the Andrew Marr Show, launching a personal attack on his rival and ending up laughing off the assault. The London Mayor accused Miliband of "stabbing the country in the back" by doing a deal with the SNP to get into power.

A 26-year-old prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The incident occurred when Dustin Irons, who was appearing via video-link, became disgruntled with the proceedings and exposed himself despite being in handcuffs. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days for contempt of court. Irons, who had been arrested for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside, was known as a difficult inmate and needed two officers and handcuffs to move him. He faces another disciplinary investigation and could be placed in a segregation unit for his misdemeanor.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since the Australian Grand Prix, with Fernando Alonso and Button discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Despite Button's retirement, McLaren's progress was noted, and the team is now comparing themselves with the Force Indias, Saubers, and Lotuses. Button acknowledges the team still has a long way to go, but is pleased with the progress made, especially in the cooler Shanghai weather.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to its medical service provider being stripped of its contract and fined. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitized instruments, raising concerns about patient safety. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated morale issues among its workforce.

Becca Litchfield and Dale, who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for IVF, have welcomed twins and found a way to say their "I do's." The couple, from Nottingham, won a wedding competition and were able to have the white wedding they had always wanted.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the US caused confusion and laughter with its vocalizations after meeting a young husky dog. The Shibu Inu squeaked and squawked, attempting to bark at its new companion, which caused the husky to whine. The dogs continued to converse, with the Shibu Inu attempting to get closer to the husky. People in the video laughed and mimicked the dogs' actions, and the husky eventually lost interest and chewed on its handler's sleeve.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is preparing to lead England in the upcoming Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to challenge the opposition and has trained hard to become the fastest bowler on the pitch. Plunkett, who has recovered from an ankle injury, is competing for a place in the England Test team alongside Chris Jordan and Mark Wood. The competition is fierce, with Plunkett emphasizing the importance of bowling well in practice and warm-up games to earn his spot in the first Test against the West Indies.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Smith, who has lost two previous title defenses to Arthur Abraham, is seen as a potential warm-up opponent for Ward, who is ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Froch willing to travel to the UK if Ward returns the favor by coming to the US. Smith is the only boxer from Liverpool's family of four fighting brothers who is not fighting for a title.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a sudden departure of five of her six police officers and several other top officials. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," and the outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, has no idea why the employees quit. The town, with a population of 713, has a predominantly black population and has experienced a surge in crime. The new mayor's father, Simon Wofford, insists his daughter has a good relationship with the police department.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the team is set to make him available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-winning period, is said to be content with his life at the Etihad Stadium and is not in a rush to leave. However, his wages are a stumbling block towards a potential move, with Inter Milan showing interest but concerns over his huge salary. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression, challenging the common belief that these drugs are prescribed for clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of those taking SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant, did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are often prescribed without clear evidence-based indications. This study comes amid a significant increase in antidepressant prescriptions, with the OECD noting a 300% rise in prescriptions since 1998, particularly in the use of SSRIs. The study's findings raise questions about the effectiveness and appropriateness of antidepressant use.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about her daughter's life in a long article for the Washington Post, describing how her illness went undiagnosed until her early 20s and how her daughter lived with an incurable disease that filled her head with devils that eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that.

A 10-year-old boy nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. Koby Hodder collapsed while playing British Bulldog, a game involving running from one side of a field to another without being caught. His heart stopped for 12 minutes, leading to a cardiac arrest. He was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as Fabrice Muamba, who had a similar cardiac arrest in 2012. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived, who used a defibrillator to save his life.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, wants to see bitterness taken out of most matrimonial disputes in England and Wales. She believes that divorce laws should remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, and that couples should be encouraged to sort out arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. Lady Hale, who is deputy president to the Supreme Court and the only woman among the 12 Supreme Court justices, wants a one-year "cooling off period" after declaring that their marriage has permanently broken down, during which they can sort out arrangements. She is behind the move for "no fault" divorce in England and Wales 20 years ago.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a 'slide-out' grass pitch with an NFL-style synthetic surface. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. Tottenham's new stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, is seen as more advantageous for NFL teams than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL is keeping its options open, but a new London stadium designed with American football requirements would be highly advantageous.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA, urging the organization to remove Russia from hosting the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, are calling for economic sanctions against Russia and a condemnation of the Putin regime.

Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. The husband of the author, Erika Leonard, will write the script for the second film, and Sam Taylor-Johnson is no longer directing the sequel.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and his overall record is one of the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and he is the only manager in the Premier League with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but his current record is not as good as his previous record. Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match against Caykur Rizespor. The bus was attacked as it drove to the airport after the match, resulting in the driver being wounded and taken to hospital. Fenerbahce believes the attack is not being solved in a way that satisfies them and public opinion, leading to the suspension of the championship. The incident occurred after Fenerbahce won a match against Rizespor 5-1.

A massive snowstorm struck Everest Base Camp, trapping climbers and causing at least 17 deaths in Nepal's devastating earthquake. Helicopters rescued hundreds of stranded climbers, with the avalanche striking Base Camp and leaving hundreds missing or buried under the snow.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Donetsk, Ukraine. In 2014, he found himself again in the middle of a war in Eastern Ukraine, where a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. Margolin and his family fled to Israel, where he arrived in March 2014. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews has brought 600 Jews to Israel since December, including Margolin.

John Carver, a former assistant to Ruud Gullit, is eager to take charge of Newcastle United against Sunderland on Sunday. Gullit, who was assistant to Newcastle manager Ruud Gullit in 1999, controversially decided not to start star players Duncan Ferguson and Alan Shearer, leading to a 2-1 defeat. Carver believes a positive result could bolster his chances of winning the head coach position beyond the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina. He spoke about the need for reform in national policing legislation and the importance of using this moment to change what is happening in North Charleston. Sharpton also attended a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as 'hippy crack', and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. The 20-year-old faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action over his behaviour, and Liverpool manager Rodgers now says he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails.

Labour received more than £1 million in union donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservative party, in a boost to Ed Miliband's election campaign. Unions gave more than £700,000 to Labour, with Dave Prentis and Len McCluskey's Unite contributing £112,000 and £400,000 respectively. The donations equate to £105,420.80 a day, or £1.22 a second.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight were stranded at Manchester Airport for five hours after their plane was diverted due to severe winds, causing delays and unrest. Police were called to the tarmac twice, first for disruptive passengers and then again after the delay caused by the diversion. The flight eventually landed at Birmingham Airport, where passengers were allowed off the aircraft and bused to Manchester. Qatar Airways apologized for the delay, citing legal flying hours as the reason for the diversion.

Canadian pop star Justin Bieber will be part of Floyd Mayweather's entourage for his $300 million fight against Manny Pacquiao on Saturday in Las Vegas. Bieber, who has been close friends with Mayweather for years, has accompanied him into the ring on numerous occasions, including a recent press conference. Mayweather, who has a 47-0 record, is expected to make this fight the biggest of his career, with the fight being billed as the biggest fight in history.

The U.S. Department of Education announced that Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit career college, will shut down all of its remaining 28 campuses. Corinthian, which once enrolled more than 70,000 students, is one of the worst "predator colleges" due to its dubious degrees, high student debt, and federal money mismanagement. The closure is a positive development in the struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable. Corinthian's aggressive recruitment tactics, including making 100 phone calls and leaving 100 messages a day, have led to student debt and joblessness. The closure will help transition students into legitimate postsecondary schools.

Pep Guardiola denies a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged. Guardiola played down the claims, saying the defeat was not his fault and that injuries are part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years and was a world leader in his field.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden in New York for a world title defence against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, recalled how it changed his life and the world. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, he remains dominant and believes age is a big advantage.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear in March after attacking a producer during filming, has finally spoken out about his dismissal. Clarkson, 54, said he would "miss" fronting the BBC2 show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said she would be keen to return to the motoring show if invited back. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract. Nick Knowles, a DIY SOS star, has been linked to becoming the new Top Gear presenter. BBC bosses are trying to hold onto James May and Richard Hammond, Clarkson's co-presenters, for the show.

In a La Liga match, Fabian Orellana of Celta Vigo threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets during the closing stages, leading to a red card for Orellana. Busquets, in retaliation, grabbed his eye with the turf. Referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido awarded a straight red card to Orellana. Despite the incident, Barcelona secured a crucial 1-0 victory against Celta Vigo, while Real Madrid won 9-1 against Granada.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when bombs went off at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the man convicted of the bombings, faces sentencing. Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to it. The sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday in China, by watching parades and travelling home. The festival, which celebrates the start of spring and outdoor celebrations, falls in the first week of April and is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits like "Mrs Robinson" and "The Only Living Boy in New York," has outsold more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts. This marks his first number one album since The Rhythm of the Saints in 1990.

Iker Casillas insists he will stay at Real Madrid even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper at the Bernabeu. The 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking in to the side as a 16-year-old in 1996. Real Madrid has repeatedly linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea.

David Cameron hailed the Conservatives' economic strategy as a 'jobs miracle' and Britain as a 'job-creating machine' as employment rose to its highest level in history. The International Monetary Fund praised Chancellor George Osborne, and Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order. Labour's opposition to austerity measures was criticized, and the Chancellor said the UK economy had done a 'wonderful job' in reducing the deficit and delivering results. Greece's economic crisis poses a threat to the global economy.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced under £13,000. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden. It features a 1.6-liter engine, manual and automatic transmissions, and a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli is pitched as a value-for-money option for thrifty motorists, with entry-level SE and top-of-the-range ELX models available. The vehicle aims to change perceptions and double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, England, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers. The restaurant owner, Mike Edge, said the burger is a "supersized version" of a homemade burger stuffed with cheese and cold meats.

Yeo Valley, a dairy firm in North Somerset, has opened its staff canteen to the public, offering a gourmet menu of organic and locally sourced dishes at a subsidised price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, features quirky light fittings and high tables and stools, and serves meals such as organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen's menu changes daily based on the available produce.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is "much better" and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has 30 Grammy nominations and has won his first Grammy in 1970 for "The Thrill Is Gone." King suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago last year, forcing him to cancel the remainder of his tour.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a mix of conservative and outlandish headwear, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets. The event attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists, who participated in the mild, sunny day. The parade, which started in the 1880s, was a departure from its original strolling display and featured a wide range of creative and colorful headpieces.

Emergency crews in East of England received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including one where a squirrel was mistaken for a human victim, and one where a woman reported feeling ill after eating too much takeaway food. The service prioritizes life-threatening calls but warns that inappropriate calls can affect their response times.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge organized by Audi. The challenge involved shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range and from long range. Hazard and Ake won the first round, while Remy and Willian won the second round. In the final round, Hazard and Ake won again, securing a 6-0 lead. The final challenge involved shooting at cars from long range, with Willian and Remy winning but causing damage to one of the Audi cars.

Brendan Rodgers criticized Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to advise him to stay at the club, despite the player rejecting a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and having just two years left on his deal. Sterling had previously rejected a contract extension and had just two years left on his deal at the end of the season.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up a rude eight-letter word as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as the blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word 'erection'. The incident is not the first time Hewer has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up on the show.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison online and later pleaded guilty to trying to commit suicide, was spared jail after the court heard he was unaware his online requests were being tracked by counter-terrorism officers. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was arrested in February after receiving information that he was attempting to obtain the poison. He pleaded guilty to trying to buy the toxin at Manchester Youth Court earlier this month. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web, a subsection of the deep web used for illegal activities, and the importance of vigilant law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The death came just months after three babies and one mother died at the maternity unit. The deaths, along with those of four babies and two mothers at the Royal Oldham Hospital, prompted an investigation. Lianne Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, and his sister, Karen, have called for action to prevent further tragedies at North Manchester General Hospital.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, 32, plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, incorporating training into her pregnancy until the final trimester. Her coach, Mike Hurst, said she trained every second day and monitored her core temperature. Pittman, who turned 32 in 2016, is a two-time world champion and is pursuing a degree in medicine. She fell pregnant with an anonymous sperm donor before meeting her current partner, James Gurr.

At least one person died and at least four people were missing after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats participating in a regatta in Alabama, according to the Coast Guard. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused damage to multiple vessels and resulted in scattered boats across Mobile Bay. The mayor of Dauphin Island reported at least one death, but the cause was not known.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has been diagnosed with macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that are getting progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Barr said in an interview that she helps relieve the pressure by using marijuana. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision; while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain, and is often caused by fluid build-up and pressure in the eyes. The risk for both diseases goes up for everyone after age 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments that may delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration are available.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of an Australian college baseball player who was killed while jogging. The Stephens County jury found Luna guilty of the August 16, 2013, death of Christopher Lane, who was shot in the back while running along a city street in Duncan. Luna was sentenced to life in prison without parole.

Arsene Wenger insists his record against Jose Mourinho will not influence Arsenal's match against Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday. Wenger has lost seven and drawn five of their 12 encounters. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces. Wenger expects a good game at home, emphasizing the importance of performance over the managers' relationship.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become a global superstar after a series of mega-fights, including a fight against Floyd Mayweather on Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before being given his chance on the big stage in 2001. He has made a remarkable rise through the weight divisions from being an incredibly slight light-flyweight when he made his debut. Pacquiao left home aged 14 to move to the Philippines capital Manila to pursue his career in the sport.

Jack Grealish, a talented young player, has been caught on camera inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that is still legal but is considered harmful to athletes. Grealish, who starred for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, has not yet made it to the top level. Grealish's behavior has been compared to that of professional athletes who prioritize their health and well-being. Wenger, the manager of Arsenal, has emphasized the importance of professional athletes taking care of their bodies and avoiding substances that can slow down their performance.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality TV star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men with eggs on Easter Monday after being targeted online for his appearance. The attack occurred at a pub in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, where Barton had checked in on Facebook minutes before. The incident, which left him with yolk and shell on his face, was believed to be a result of online abuse and the use of his Facebook posts to track him down. Barton, who has spent £20,000 on teeth treatment, £5,000 on Botox, £2,000 on waxing, and £2,500 on tanning, has also been involved in a financial struggle, owing £100,000 on credit cards and store cards. His appearance on reality shows and his plastic surgery have led to financial difficulties, including bankruptcy

Manchester University in Indiana was on lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police said they received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students at its North Manchester campus, some 36 miles west of Fort Wayne, to shelter in place. The person was possibly armed with explosives, according to the university. North Manchester Police, a bomb squad from Fort Wayne and Indiana State Police were all at the scene, according to WANE. No injuries have been confirmed, and the university has continued reposting the shelter in place warning for hours after the original message and had not given the all clear as of 2am.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," will face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Cavani, who has a reputation for his class, must torment the stars from Catalonia to help Paris Saint-Germain progress beyond the Champions League's last eight.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds and was awarded a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull FC defeated St Helens 28-20, surprising the home side after a derby loss. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, and Jordan Rankin added the extras. The win was Hull's first since a defeat to Wigan. St Helens were led by Jordan Turner, who scored a try, but Hull's Tom Makinson brought the team level. The match was tense, with Hull scoring early and St Helens leveling the score. Hull regained the lead with a penalty and a try from Joe Westerman, while St Helens were forced to make tactical changes.

The U.S. Census predicts that the undocumented immigrant population could reach 51 million by 2023, and 78 million by 2060, accounting for 82% of the population growth. This growth is expected to continue steadily over the next 45 years, with immigrants making up 14.8% of the population by 2023 and 18.8% by 2060. The Center for Immigration Studies report suggests that undocumented immigrants could be exempt from deportation, and the Republican presidential candidates are expected to address their stance on the subject.

Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury for Arsenal's Under 21s, but the team lost 1-0 to Reading's U21s. Wilshere was joined by other injured players including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby. Martin Keown's son, Niall, scored the winning goal for Reading in the opening minutes. Wilshere struggled to find the back of the net, but the Gunners' other players, including Krystian Bielik and Alex Iwobi, performed well. The match was supposed to showcase Arsenal's next generation of talent, but it was Keown's son who stole the spotlight.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing. Rose, who has been a fixture in the top five for the last three years, has been hit by three missed cuts and a 55th-place finish at the Cadillac Championship in four PGA Tour starts. Rose's solution to his poor form was to spend long hours on the practice ground. The 34-year-old hit 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signed for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. Rose's return to the sixties is welcome, as he has been unforgiving in the past. Phil Mickelson enjoyed his best round in months with a 66 on Thursday. Rose is focused on his game and hopes to improve his rankings.

A Mayfair mansion, once a milking parlour, has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which now features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was originally a depot and has since been demolished. The mansion, which has four bedrooms, is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is weakened by injuries, but the team's unity is stronger, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Muller believes the team's recent games, played with a decimated squad, helped build a strong unit. Bayern will rely heavily on Muller and Robert Lewandowski, who are expected to score goals, despite the injuries. Pep Guardiola, Bayern's coach, is confident in the team's ability to reach the semi-finals despite the injuries.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. After being beaten by Sebastian Vettel at the Malaysian Grand Prix, the duo aimed to find a winning formula. Rosberg tweeted a picture of him and Hamilton on a flight back from Brackley. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that he was surprised by Vettel's victory, which was attributed to Ferrari's tactics and the cooler temperatures. The race in Malaysia saw Vettel win by 8. 5 seconds, with Hamilton and Rosberg finishing third and fourth, respectively. Mercedes now faces the challenge of analyzing why Vettel's Ferrari was more efficient in the heat.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is deemed unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within 8-10 seconds and die a few minutes later from lack of oxygen. This follows a review by the U.S. Supreme Court of Oklahoma's use of lethal injections, which has been put on hold. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous and that capital punishment must be performed effectively and without cruelty.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, was unstable due to empty fuel tanks and a lack of ballast. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The ship hit an object in the sea, likely drifting ice, and temperatures in the water can drop to -2 degrees Celsius.
