The rescue operation includes 26 fishing boats, a helicopter, and an emergency services ship. The ship's crew, including 78 from Russia, 42 from Myanmar, and the rest from Latvia, Ukraine, and Vanuatu, are involved in the rescue effort.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a pioneering drug originally meant for women, according to new clinical trials. Olaparib, already used to treat women with breast cancer, showed promise in delaying the disease's progression in men with genetic defects within their prostate cancer tumors. Up to 30% of men with advanced prostate cancer have tumours with DNA defects, and these respond particularly well to olaparib. The drug, called Lynparza, extended the length of time that a prostate cancer patient lives with the disease without it getting worse. Olaparib is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her photography skills and globetrotting into a business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies over the past seven years, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature their properties on her site. The website's name, "In Bed With," is a play on her Instagram handle, and the concept is unique, as she has turned her lifestyle into a business.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players were targeted by objects thrown from the crowd during their victory celebration. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses to come forward. The club is banning those involved and appealing to the Metropolitan Police to identify the perpetrators.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. LaTasha Gosling, 27, and her two daughters, Janyaa, 4, and Jenika, 8, and her son Landen, 7, were discovered early Wednesday one day after they were reported missing. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police would not say how he died, they did say it was not a homicide. He also had a six-month-old baby with him who was unharmed. The Goslings were living in a mobile park with a man who was living with the mother and three children. The family's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is raising money for their funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, lost her frontbench job after tweeting a photo of a house covered in England flags and with a white van outside. She owns three homes, including a £1 million property she bought from a housing association eight years ago. The article highlights Thornberry's hypocrisy in opposing right to buy but renting out a property she bought from a housing association.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during an attack on his hounds in Everleigh, Wiltshire, three months after the incident. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, Wiltshire Police dropped the investigation, leading Lane to condemn the decision as "pathetic." The attack occurred despite the hounds chasing an artificial scent rather than a fox.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes, 21, insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. He says remaining at the Mestalla is his preferred option. Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. Reports have linked Gomes with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea, but he denies being contacted by Chelsea. Gomes says he just thinks about spending the next season in Spain, and his agent is not aware of any opportunity.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice in Bali while on holiday with her family. The 19-year-old claims she was lured to a remote home by a man named Henry Alafu, who then attacked her twice. Alafu allegedly told her a party was taking place at a nearby villa, and the pair agreed to go together. During the ride to the house, Pekin felt unwell due to her diabetes, but Alafu locked the door and forced her to the bed where he raped her. After the first attack, Pekin tried to escape, but Alafu followed her and forced her to flee again. CCTV footage captured Alafu waiting in the lobby for Pekin, who stopped at the hotel before continuing with her night out. Pekin escaped the cab when it got back into the city of Kuta, and Alafu stalked after her again. The Indonesian police let Alafu escape back to

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features James holding a fake skinned fox, with the slogan "Harvey Nichols: Here's the Rest of Your Fur Coat." Harvey Nichols, which has 12 locations worldwide, previously reintroduced its fur-free policy last year. The store's current range includes coyote fur from Canada Goose, raccoon fur from Charlotte Simone, and rabbit pelts from Vince. James, who leads a mostly vegan lifestyle, believes that people should make informed decisions about their purchases. Harvey Nichols claims to source products from reputable brands and seek assurance of responsible animal welfare. However, PETA's recent undercover investigation exposed issues at fur farms.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in recognizing civil unions between people of the same sex, following President Michelle Bachelet's enactment of a new law. The law, set to take effect in six months, will grant legal status to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The change is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples, such as not being allowed to visit partners in hospital, make medical decisions on their behalf, or decide what to do with their remains. The law also gives the couples greater rights in property, health care, pensions, and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, leading the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2005/06, surpassing Manchester United's record of 262 days. Chelsea's 2005/06 title-winning side under Mourinho led the way for 257 days, while Manchester United's 2000/01 title-winning side led for 241 days.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese territory off the coast of Africa, is known for its rich musical heritage, which includes batuque, morna, and other unique styles. The country is seeking to tap into the economic potential of its music and culture, which have been shaped by its diverse history and geography. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been celebrating its seventh edition, has brought artists from around the world to share in the music. The festival has become one of the most spectacular events in Cape Verde, with people from all corners of the world coming to share in the music.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House went viral again after being reposted by other sources. The video was originally uploaded by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa on Tuesday morning. Some users have referenced the weather as the trigger of the strange phenomenon, with musician Fortafy uploading the video with the caption 'storm brings out surfers in Sydney Harbour.' The video was posted following heavy storms and tandem heavy swells in June 2012. YouTube commenters pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot. Wave experts rebutted the video, saying it was a sham and theorized that ocean swells would struggle to break that far inside the Harbour.

Reading, the beaten FA Cup semi-finalists, lost to Birmingham in a 1-0 Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winner in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who fumbled in the opening goal against Arsenal, was retained. Birmingham, with little to play for, struggled to create chances. Reading's Garath McCleary scored an equalizer against Arsenal.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, will miss the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury. The Brazilian defender, who had a run that led to his injury, will be out for at least four weeks, potentially affecting PSG's title defense.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. The show's illegal downloads increased by 45% year-on-year, jumping from 4.9 million in 2014 to 7 million in the two-month period from February to April. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO announced in March that the forthcoming season will air across 170 countries at the same time, and launched a new internet streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham have won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

For six years, a statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, has been a source of controversy. The statue, based on a moment from her show "I Love Lucy," depicts her as drunk and pitchy for a health tonic, which locals find unflattering. A Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has attracted over 600 likes, with the anonymous creator claiming the statue is "monstrous" and "nothing like the beautiful Lucy we all know." The town has tried to honor its most famous resident, but the statue has become a source of tension.

A woman who was forced to stand during an 11-hour flight to lose weight has shed nearly half her body weight. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, who was a size 26 when she went on the business trip in December 2012, lost 4st through joining a slimming club and then shed another 4.5 stone after taking up running. She now weighs 9st 9lb and is a size 10. The turning point came for Sharon after having to 'squeeze' her bulky frame into seats on trains and planes.

One new mother, Nicola Bonn, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences of raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy and the challenges of being a first-time mother. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shared a post called "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves," which highlighted the overwhelming amount of opinions and judgments new mothers face.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for his role in a terrorist plot. The families are in shock and worry about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, used the Easter holidays to flee Britain.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described the pain of losing his daughter, who had planned a perfect wedding for her childhood sweetheart, Aaron Leeson-Woolley. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but now the family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead. The wedding was originally scheduled for Saturday, April 11, but the day before her remains were discovered, police were led to the location by the family of the accused killer.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who wants to leave the club this summer. Koeman, the manager of Southampton, is keen to bring Vilhena to the south coast. The Saints are also monitoring their teammate Jordy Clasie, who has won 11 senior caps for Holland. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent, as he looks to strengthen his squad ahead of possible qualification for European competition next season.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment that has angered heritage experts. The move was designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere' but was branded 'misguided' by critics. The Trust said the beanbag experiment was 'short-term' and would not continue for the whole year. The move sparked controversy and led to similar experiments at nine other Trust venues around the country. The National Trust presented each house in context and treated each appropriately, but some staff thought the beanbags were good as an experiment.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, approached Howard and asked if she could help. Howard agreed to a selfie, and the pair spent about 15 minutes changing the tyre.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis, who has instilled a solid core of players at West Brom, believes Barton's criticism of the team's finishing is justified. Pulis also recalled his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, highlighting the importance of maintaining composure in high-pressure situations. The teams will meet again at the Hawthorns on Saturday.

A new species of monkey, the Bouvier's red colobus monkey, has been discovered in the remote rain forests of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The primate, which was thought to have been extinct for more than 50 years, was first discovered in 1887 and is only known from three specimens. The discovery proves that the primate is not extinct and has been captured on camera for the first time. The researchers hope to study the monkey to learn more about it.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for an eight-day trip, including a stay at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan. The visit is their first to the country, where they are exploring landmarks and attending cultural events. The Kardashian-West crew is staying in the capital's finest digs, with bodyguards and police in tow. The city is known for its cultural and economic significance, with a mix of Soviet-era architecture and Neo-Classical official buildings.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now trapped in the property due to an ongoing legal dispute with the local town hall over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The Jubbs claim they have done nothing wrong and are seeking to return to the UK, but their money is tied up in the property. The couple's property, La Vina de Linan, is located in Jimena de la Frontera, southern Spain, and is currently listed for sale with a guide price of €875,000.

Apple's iPhone sales surpassed analysts' expectations in the first quarter of 2015, with the company reporting a 40% increase from the previous year, selling more than 61 million iPhones, accounting for more than two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone has become the engine behind Apple's success, with the company's shares gaining more than 50% over the last year, making it the world's most valuable company.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a mysterious white van that she believes may have caused her mother's death in a car crash. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, says she has been having these visions since the crash, which occurred two months ago. The white van is believed to be a delivery-style box truck, and the girl's father thinks it may have caused the crash. The incident has led investigators to investigate a series of hit-and-run accidents involving the same truck in nearby communities.

Researchers at New York University have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study focused on how the brain stores memories for emotionally neutral events, such as neutral events like a lunch date, and how emotion affects memory retention. Emotion increases the strength of our memory over time, a process called consolidation. Strong emotion can strengthen memory for positive events, such as a surprise birthday party, and for negative events, such as making an embarrassing faux pas. A power nap of just 45 minutes can boost memory by five times, research has found.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The surgery, performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo, is expected to save his life but will leave him paralysed for some time. The community in the small town of Casino, northern NSW, has shown overwhelming support for the couple, raising more than the initial goal.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha has 15 months left on his contract and has played regularly under Chris Ramsey. He was part of QPR's 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion on Saturday. Onuoha is also being considered by Stoke manager Mark Hughes and could potentially join Everton or West Ham. Additionally, Hull City is showing interest in West Bromwich Albion's Victor Anichebe, who is expected to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have discovered regional variations in English sentence structure across the United States, with some states using unique phrases that are unfamiliar to others. The study, which involved nationwide surveys and an online crowdsourcing platform, found that people in the South are more likely to use presentative sentences like "Here's you a water bottle," while those in the North are less likely to use such phrases. The researchers, led by Larry Horn, a professor of linguistics and philosophy at Yale University, note that this variation in sentence structure may be found among speakers who live in a certain geographical region, belong to a certain age group, or belong to a particular social or ethnic group.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and interact with the landscape. The video shows him sitting in the chair, posing, and making gestures. He also danced and played with his dad. The journey was a bonding experience for the father and son.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a 'win bonus' of sweets and chocolate to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and revealed a Twix multi-pack under the desk.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the darts in his hometown of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, who won both of his games in week 10, moved onto 17 points in second place in the table. Chisnall said it was a confidence boost to beat the world champion and that he felt good up on stage. Chisnall is second in the Premier League table behind Michael van Gerwen, who snatched a 7-5 victory against Stephen Bunting. Raymond van Barneveld beat Phil Taylor 7-2 to inflict Taylor's fourth defeat in five.

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Marco Verratti has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club, saying he is always on hand to help his teammates and exerts confidence in the team. Ibrahimovic, who has scored 17 goals for the club this season, will be available for selection ahead of the return fixture in the Champions League quarter-final.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details on the Falklands Islands' defenses, including GPS coordinates and runway depth, on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The information was accessible to foreign intelligence agents, and the MoD admitted the manual was available on the internet but disabled. The Falklands Islands are defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the UK is considering leasing 12 Russian Sukhoi SU-24 bombers from Argentina.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to improve the team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they aim to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period. Anderson attributes the team's poor start to the fast-paced nature of the season and acknowledges the need to fix issues with the offense. If Huddersfield wins their next game, they could leapfrog Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league. The article also mentions that Widnes are the only team yet to take a point from their travels, while Castleford, coached by Denis Betts, is expected to present a tough challenge for Vikings coach Daryl Powell's improving side.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa coffee shops to open less than 500 yards apart, sparking controversy among residents who fear it will lead to an overabundance of fast food and coffee shops in the area. The new Costa will open on the site of the former Dedworth Road HSBC branch, while a Costa that replaced a cycle shop opened earlier this year. The Costa Express, located at a nearby petrol station, will also be within a five-minute walk.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire, stating that the first two years of culling did not demonstrate conclusively that 'controlled shooting' could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, while animal welfare campaigners welcomed the news but criticized the BVA's ongoing support for cage-trapping and shooting.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, has accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves. Artists have long railed against low royalties paid from streaming companies, leading to Jay-Z launching his own Tidal service, promising bigger returns for musicians.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. Fans of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, now face the daunting task of avoiding spoilers online as the first four episodes are released over the course of the month.

A best man composed an emotional song at his brother's wedding in Melbourne, leaving guests in tears. Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old singer, performed a song to the tune of Stay With Me, which he composed to the music of artists like Sam Smith and the Backstreet Boys. The unique speech, which has been viewed over 100,000 times online, included tributes to his brother and his bride, Sarah, and delved into Daniel's childhood and his admiration for his older sibling. The speech documented Daniel's brother, Adrian, falling in love with Sarah and the challenges they faced in their relationship.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after the birth of her daughter Mia by hitting the exercise bike every morning before her daughter wakes up. The 33-year-old, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, has committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was seen as ill-timed and unprofessional, and it has been speculated that Sterling's agent may have engineered the situation. Sterling returned to training ahead of the weekend's game against Arsenal and was linked with a move to Arsenal. Liverpool fans have a popular mantra that no player is bigger than the club, but they are now of the belief that if Sterling wants to go, he is welcome to.

Barcelona's 1996-97 team, led by former Barcelona coach Luis Enrique and assistant Jose Mourinho, included current PSG coach Laurent Blanc, Porto coach Julen Lopetegui, and four other coaches from the same club at the same time. The team won the Spanish Super Cup against Atletico Madrid 6-4 on aggregate.

Former Manchester United legend Eric Cantona has declared Paris Saint-Germain forward Javier Pastore the best player in the world, saying he is the most creative and interactive player in football. Pastore, who cost £29 million, has three goals and five assists this season, compared to Lionel Messi's 45 goals for Barcelona and Cristiano Ronaldo's 51 for Real Madrid. Cantona's assessment was made at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, where he was third in the Ballon d'Or in 1993 behind Roberto Baggio and Dennis Bergkamp.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by dismembering his body and throwing the parts into a canal. The trial took 15 hours and involved a jury of 11 people. Simon, with the help of his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, dumped the suitcases containing the body parts into the canal. Bird was cleared of murder and manslaughter but admitted assisting an offender. The case was solved when police found the suitcases and recovered the body parts.

Two county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have implemented 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents are most vulnerable to social isolation. The maps are based on statistics on public health factors linked to loneliness and survey data from residents. Gloucestershire's map, adapted from Essex County Council's model, identifies high-risk areas with red markings. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the maps as a way to treat the problem across the country. The report identifies other risk factors for chronic loneliness, including ethnic minorities, recent bereavement, and childless pensioners.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she's ever had or ever wanted. She remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents, and her first day on the job when she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat. Eddingfield, who has been working at the restaurant since 1965, has trained her siblings and many of her friends, and met her first husband there. She even met her true love who she calls 'Frog' at Winstead's and the pair married 18 months later.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. England were held to a draw in the opening Test of a three-match series against West Indies last week, and calls for a Pietersen comeback continue to linger ahead of the Ashes this summer.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day in revenue. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violated the company's terms of service. Benn has denied the allegations, stating that he was aware of the legal gray area and that he would have fixed the app had he been given a chance. The controversy highlights the tension between social media platforms and developers who want to monetize their services.

South Korean companies often hold hoesik dinners, where employees drink alcohol together. This practice is seen as a way to get to know colleagues and is considered a way to get to know someone's true character. However, foreigners may feel pressured to participate, as drinking is seen as a way to get to know someone. Koreans defer to senior figures in the relationship and pour alcohol for them first. It is considered rude to have an empty glass, and after everyone has poured, they say "Gunbae!" and chug the entire glass of alcohol.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George, the younger brother of King George VI and King Edward VIII. He is the country's top Freemason and has performed royal duties on behalf of the Queen.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been criticized by local business owners who claim the group is outdated and no longer providing a public service. The controversy stems from advancements in parking meter technology, which have made it unnecessary for Meter Maids to place money into expired meters. Local business leaders argue that Meter Maids are now violating anti-touting laws by promoting branded merchandise. The Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president, Peter Yared, supports the removal of Meter Maids, stating they are no longer relevant due to the electronic nature of parking meters. However, Surfers Paradise Meter Maids general manager, Michael Yarwood, disputes this claim, arguing that tourists love and embrace the group as a quintessential part of the Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece will in fact make the payment on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but the country is due to repay a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund on April 9.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US.

A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a heartfelt letter to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage would not lead to the dark side and that it would be a good path for a Jedi. Colin was overjoyed to receive the letter and was able to receive a package of Star Wars merchandise.
Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak. Wisconsin advances to the final, while Kentucky finishes the season at 38-1.

Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe, and other performers have been criticized for their renditions of the national anthem, with some likened to "butchers" for their poor performances. The article highlights several notable instances where famous individuals have been called out for their singing of the anthem, including Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton.

CCTV footage of a violent altercation between Irish brothers Patrick and Barry Lyttle, resulting in Patrick's near-death, has been released for the first time. Barry, charged with grievous bodily harm, faces a potential jail sentence of up to two years. The brothers, who had only been reunited for a holiday, had a heated argument at a bar in Sydney, with Barry hitting Patrick in the head with a single punch. Patrick was rushed to the hospital with severe head injuries.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite stripped of mementos and flowers after cemetery staff cleared the baby section of the site. The Howies had built a small shrine at the gravesite, which they had maintained since the funeral, but everything was removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not been notified that they would be cleaned, and the Howies were only able to retrieve about 25 percent of their memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, Britain's most senior judge, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year. The execution took place on Tuesday night at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri. The inmate declined to order a last meal and received the day's inmate tray meal of a turkey and bologna sandwich, a cookie, and fruit punch. Governor Jay Nixon, who refused a clemency petition, read a statement about the importance of remembering Anthony Curtis and his loved ones.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. The Duchess is expected to give birth mid to late April, and details of the new baby's arrival will be announced on social media.

An alleged fraudster, Justin Jackson, has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson, a Florida man, is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and is accused of variously posing as Oprah herself, Oprah's nephew, Love, an executive at the Oprah Winfrey Network (OWN), and managers of Madonna and Johnny Depp. The earliest fraud involved Jackson tricking a New York City jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million by pretending to be Madonna's manager. Jackson was convicted for grand theft over the ruse but later dreamed up new celebrity-linked schemes.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the 'new Messi'. A bidding war is set to break out over Dybala, who is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus and PSG. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was spotted at the Stadio Ennio Tardini on Sunday, when Palermo lost 1-0 against Parma, and the Inter manager was understood to be there to watch Dybala.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is facing an economic downturn and a bribery scandal. The protests are calling for Rousseff to be impeached. Petrobras, the state-run oil company, is under investigation for a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme. Rousseff has defended Brazilians' right to protest and acknowledged the need to clean up corruption at Petrobras, but her supporters say the position is merely a figurehead. The country was already sharply divided during presidential elections, and participation in the protests has not been consistently strong.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, You and the Night, features racy scenes, including Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a "piece of art" and that it is "beautiful". The film includes a scene in a cage with Cantona and Beatrice Dalle in just their underwear.

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding. The so-called digital seasoning also applies to wine, helping drinkers to enjoy their tipple by up to 15 per cent more, if served alongside the right music.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100,000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have stalled. Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, is reportedly considering a move to Arsenal or Spain. Taylor, the PFA chief, believes Sterling should wait until the end of the season to resume contract talks, as it is "not necessarily a bad thing" for both club and player to focus on football. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ohio woman La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, 38, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center operation company she does. After connecting the dots, she found Simmons on Facebook and realized her mother was closer than she could imagine. They met after a phone call and found out they work at the same company and live six minutes away from one another. Mitchell-Clark also found out she has three younger sisters she didn't know about.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker, was "awed" by New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez and sent him an assault rifle and handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection to his namesake's murder case. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole for first-degree murder of Odin Lloyd.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. Parker was arrested for battery and issued a trespass warning. He is never allowed to use the bus again.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, saying he has been "fantastic" and "brilliant" at the club.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who worked with the German aid organization Welthungerlife to help rebuild Pakistan after deadly flooding, was killed by a U.S. drone strike in 2012. Lo Porto, who had studied at London Metropolitan University and was passionate about helping others, was working on a reconstruction project in Pakistan when he was abducted by four armed men. He died along with his colleague Bernd Muehlenbeck, who was also killed by the drone strike. Lo Porto was a project manager with Welthungerlife's clean water and sanitation program, working with 8 to 10 fellow international staffers and 100 to 200 locals.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks near a beach in south Florida, prompting speculation that the sharks were Blacktips or Spinners migrating to breed. The incident was shared more than 2,000 times on social media.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession on Wednesday before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute for Zeus began around 4:45 pm and ended at the Ridgefield Veterinary Hospital. The police department wrote an emotional message about Zeus on their Facebook, expressing their thoughts and prayers for Zeus, Officer Murray, and his family during this difficult time. During the grand procession, residents of Ridgefield lined the streets as they watched the cop cars drive by through the town. Zeus had the special tribute before he was put down because of a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health.

Since Operation Yewtree, the number of child sex abuse reports has surged by more than 60%, with thousands of new cases filed in 2014. Despite a 9% drop in arrests, critics accuse the Government of failing to protect victims. The South Yorkshire force saw a 577% increase in reported cases, with 501 investigations in 2014. Thames Valley Police made 191 arrests in relation to child sex abuse, up from 13 in 2011. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation's launch.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park and Svartalfheim providing stunning settings for Game of Thrones and Thor: The Dark World, respectively. The country's dramatic landscapes, including the Svinafellsjokull glacier and Dettifoss waterfall, have been used in Interstellar and Prometheus, respectively. The Icelandic film industry has grown rapidly, with 17 production services companies in the country.

A 100-year-old mechanic's garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, with the proceeds expected to be used to convert the building into a home. The grey-fronted building, which was built as a fire station in 1917, is now being renovated to create a three-bedroom, four-storey house. The property is located in Paddington, Sydney's inner city, and is situated a stone's throw away from Oxford Street and Five Ways. The building is expected to be turned into a cozy home for the couple who have lived there for 18 years.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after a car accident in May 2021. The rare condition, an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that doctors cannot explain, has left her with no feeling in her bladder and struggles with mobility and cognitive functions. She is now confined to her house, unable to walk and relies on a mobility scooter. The condition, which can be as debilitating as Parkinson's disease and MS, has no effective treatment plans and is very rare.

The sculptor of a Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, has admitted to being "disappointed" in his work and offered to fix the sculpture for free. The statue, based on a moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents. The sculptor, Dave Poulin, pledged to make a new one, but it would cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000. The statue depicts Ball during her intoxicated pitch for the health tonic.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba, out for seven weeks with a torn knee ligament, will miss the season's final matches after being ruled out for another seven weeks. Alaba, 22, is set to begin rehabilitation in about a month. He had been in excellent form for Bayern, helping them stay on track for a treble of titles. Bayern, top of the Bundesliga, will face Porto in the Champions League quarter-finals later this month.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a Scotland Yard detective, appeared in court on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring with her boyfriend Daniel Williams. Nokes, 21, is accused of inciting prostitution in London and grooming three young women. Williams, 37, a Met police officer, is also facing multiple charges including voyeurism and hiding profits. Both are on bail and will return to court.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is offering to sell information on 43 different health conditions, including skin problems, insomnia, migraines, and credit card information. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, the 21-year-old golfer who won the 2017 Masters, expressed his thoughts on his autistic sister Ellie, who was not able to attend the tournament. Spieth said he misses his sister and wishes she could have been there to share the victory. He also mentioned that his sister has shaped his upbringing and provided him with perspective. Spieth's victory was considered one of the most prestigious in golf history, and he became the second-youngest winner of the tournament.

Dick Advocaat, 67, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, unlike his 1998 mistake with Celtic. Advocaat takes charge of Sunderland for the first time on home soil, with North-East rivals Newcastle as the visitors. Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe trains with his team-mates ahead of the game. Rangers' Rod Wallace runs forward with the ball as his side were thrashed 5-1 by Celtic in 1998. Advocaat admits he did not realise the significance of the Old Firm fixture, leading to a humiliating loss. He recalls: 'To be honest, I did not realise at that moment it was so huge. 'We lost that game and I remember saying in the press conference when they were really upset, 'It is no problem for me because it is just one of 38 games and we will not lose any more.' 'I would not say that anymore! But we became champions

A young woman named Belinda Bartholomew, girlfriend of Roosters star Aidan Guerra, had a heated argument with a butcher in Sydney over a chicken purchase for a Game of Thrones-themed dinner. Bartholomew claims the butcher called her a "f***ing c***" and told her to go to an "Aussie butcher" when she tried to change her chicken selection. The butcher denies the claims, saying he was slow with his eftpos machine and that Bartholomew was the one being rude.

Freddo Frogs, a popular children's chocolate, has been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g, despite keeping the price the same. This change was spotted by a shop owner and is part of a broader trend of declining confectionery sales. Cadbury's parent company, Mondelez International, has faced increased costs and is reducing the size of their family blocks by one row, from 220g to 200g, to cut costs. The change has caused backlash from chocolate fans, who believe it is not worth the price increase.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met on Saturday in Brooklyn to outline their values and goals for the upcoming presidential campaign, according to a Democrat who attended the meeting. The document, distributed by Robby Mook, outlines the campaign's purpose, goals, and how they plan to win, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign will avoid mistakes that plagued Clinton's 2008 run and will focus on issues such as family prosperity and election on the ground. Clinton is planning to launch her presidential candidacy on Sunday through a video message on social media, and will travel to Iowa and New Hampshire for early primary and caucus states.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed details about her long battle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, she was later diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, which only worsened over time. Kyli, who had digestive problems for years, was initially misdiagnosed as having acute pancreatitis. She lost 30 pounds and had to postpone her wedding due to her condition. Kyli found a support group on Facebook for people with chronic pancreatitis, some of whom said they had similar experiences.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon posed with a sceptical face in a meme referencing the leaders' debate. Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg were superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb, two men from Brighton who appear on Channel 4 series Gogglebox. The images were inspired by a debate that saw Labour leader Ed Miliband warn that he would not get into power without lurching left, as SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon told him he is 'not strong enough' to win power on his own.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the fight. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now looking forward to a fight with Pacquiao. The fight could be a dream come true for Khan, who has been looking forward to fighting in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The property, which is described as "well proportioned" by the estate agency, has two bedrooms, a narrow galley kitchen, and a garden. The home, which was put on the market for £750,000 in 2001, is now under offer for £750,000, with buyers paying £27,000 in stamp duty. The home's backyard is a narrow strip of land stuck between the house and a neighbor's fence.

Scottish First Minister Nicola Sturgeon is launching an ambitious manifesto to challenge Labour in the upcoming election, aiming to form a power-sharing deal with the opposition. The SNP's policies overlap with Labour's, including reducing tuition fees and rolling back NHS competition. The manifesto includes plans for spending increases funded by more borrowing, potentially totaling £180 billion over five years. The SNP aims to build a "progressive alliance" for policies across the UK, with a focus on infrastructure spending in northern England and Wales. The surge in support for the SNP could lead to constitutional turmoil similar to the 1910 election, where Irish Nationalists gained more than 70 seats and triggered conflict and eventual secession.

Celtic U17 team won the Glasgow Cup 2-0 against Rangers, with Josh Kerr scoring the first goal and Robby McCrorie doubling Celtic's lead. The match was played behind closed doors due to trouble among Rangers fans.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis insisted he will never change his traditional attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers, even though he previously played for Crystal Palace. Pulis led his team to a 2-0 victory over his former club, despite the opposition dominating the game. Pulis, who has worked wonders at West Brom, has virtually guaranteed their survival in the Premier League.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. The fillings were removed due to high levels of mercury detected in her blood tests, which suggested they were the cause of her symptoms, including puffy faces, heavy heads, and fainting. While dental amalgam has been used for over 150 years and is still commonly used, the amounts taken in from fillings are considered minuscule and there is no evidence to suggest they are harmful.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, was refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million as he awaits trial for murder and attempted murder. Despite walking confidently into court, he had to be carted out in a wheelchair as Judge Ronald Coen rejected his pleas. However, Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, an undefeated professional worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

TV chef Gizzi Erskine, 35, posed in a lavish feast for her cat Kimchi, a British shorthair, in an interview with Puss Puss magazine. The cat, known for his discerning palate, loves crunchy human food like poppadoms, tortilla chips, and taramasalata. Kimchi, who won't eat anything unless it's proper meat, has a penchant for caviar, salmon roe, jellied fish heads, and a two-tiered cake covered in cat treats. Despite living in a foodie household, Gizzi insists that Kimchi's love for human food is not her influence.

Martin Springall, a father in Japan, photographed his daughter standing near a pair of boots in 2014. The boots were later found to be behind the girl, sparking debate online about their origin and meaning. Springall, who initially dismissed the boots as a trick of the light, now admits he has no idea what they are or where they came from.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will force EU migrants to pay tax and national insurance before receiving welfare benefits, with a four-year ban on benefits for those in work. The measures are part of a broader plan to negotiate a new deal with Europe, including curbing access to benefits. The crackdown is aimed at reducing net migration to the UK and limiting the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, eight years old with Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and fed by a tube, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor at Royal Preston Hospital since last Thursday due to a lack of a suitable bed. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has slept with him for the past week, fearing he could injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the necessary high-sided cot for Cody, and he has been without a bed for years. Lynne Neatis is demanding answers from the local health trust about why they still do not have a suitable bed for disabled children.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson reports on the excitement and challenges faced by players. Rory McIlroy aims for a career Grand Slam, while Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, and Tiger Woods, accompanied by his children, face the tournament. The tradition of skipping golf balls across water at the 16th hole is observed, with no player matching Vijay Singh and Martin Kaymer's feats.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has endured a difficult period at Old Trafford after arriving in an expensive loan deal from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging loyalty. This is the largest privatisation since Thatcher's era. The sale would be the biggest since the 1980s when BT and British Gas were sold. The sale would be used to help pay down the national debt.

Living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' which increase the risk of dementia, according to a study. Researchers found evidence that living near congested roads or polluted areas can lead to 'silent strokes' which cause shrinkage of the brain and other damage. The study, published in the journal Stroke, involved more than 900 people aged 60 and over who did not have dementia or a history of strokes. The researchers found that increases in PM2.5 in towns and cities were linked with a 46% higher risk of silent strokes. The study will add to mounting pressure on the Government, which faces a judgment at the Supreme Court next week over its failure to meet EU legal limits for air pollution.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, wrote an emotional letter to her followers, revealing she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks. She had chosen to fight the cancer with controversial Gerson Therapy, which involves a vegan diet and coffee enemas. After discussions with experts, she began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, which was among the toughest for her and her partner. The radiation successfully managed to shrink the tumour but caused complications, and she died shortly after. Her partner, Tallon Pamenter, described her as a "wellness warrior" who displayed courage and grace, and her death has stripped him of the magic that brought joy to his life.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway near Fernvale on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, and arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a 6-year-old girl. The incident occurred at 2km south of Fernvale, with diversions in place and the affected stretch of the highway closed off. The Rescue 500 helicopter airlifted patients to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Brisbane.

Colorado Gator Farm owner Jason McDonald, 34, walked a thin slackline over more than 50 hungry alligators at the farm. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years, said he thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. The imam, Abdul Hadi Arwani, was called to a job in the area he was killed days before his death. When the imam, who had links to the Muslim Brotherhood in the UK and abroad, arrived to the house with his son and not on his own, the supposed potential client asked Arwani to come back another day. The man, who has not been otherwise been identified, also told the imam that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a popular treat, have sparked a black market, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to buy them. The original store warns against buying "fake" cookies, while bakeries make knockoffs and resell them at a higher price. The frenzy has spread to other parts of the world, with people waiting in long lines for food mania.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and battled depression and anorexia, has revealed how bodybuilding gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. At just 6st, she was deemed clinically underweight and was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain some weight. There, she turned her life around and is now a personal trainer. Ms Hollis says bodybuilding changed her life and gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She was also helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic in Tamworth and medication from her doctor. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has now been more than two million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, causing him to perform a mid-air somersault. The incident, which was captured on video and viewed by millions online, has led to Ferguson gaining a reputation as an internet sensation. Despite the fall, Ferguson returned to mucking out the stables and said he was undeterred from getting back in the saddle. The incident was described as the worst fall the author had ever seen, and Ferguson's parents were worried about his safety. The fall was Ferguson's fifth race and his first time falling while riding out.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. Critics, including Ruth Marcus and Jon Stewart, dismissed her efforts as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and "boring as s---." However, marketing experts argue that her launch may have been more successful than critics think, projecting a confident, empathetic image of Clinton. The campaign's rebranding strategy aims to change how voters perceive Clinton, while the reframe strategy seeks to change how voters emotionally experience her.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday, the first time the school allowed students to sit exams outdoors due to insufficient indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their chairs and desks from time to time to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school said the outdoor exam could be a test of the students' organizing capacity and that it could help prevent cheating.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a chance for one reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The lucky winner will also receive a Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor and shaving foam. Joe Hart is the No. 1 for Manchester City and the England national team. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but was adopted by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie proved her parenting skills by raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two now have an inseparable bond. Kecil, who had to be moved from his birthplace at Toledo zoo 14 months ago after his natural mother failed to bond with him properly, will have his first public outing this weekend in two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her pet dogs after lying undiscovered for days. Noelle Baynham collapsed and died following an accidental overdose of medication. Her dogs, a Jack Russell and Staffordshire Bull Terrier, partially ate her body, which was found by her friend after she failed to answer the door. The inquest was told that the most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose, but the dogs ate parts of her vital organs, making it impossible to determine the exact cause of death. The dogs' scratch marks on her chest indicated that they may have tried to wake her after she collapsed.

France's handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka, faces fraud charges over their alleged involvement in an illegal betting case. Karabatic, a multiple world and Olympic gold medalist, was banned by the French league for betting on a match in which his Montpellier club lost to a struggling team. The trial is expected to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine. He has denied placing bets on the match.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire. The offenses occurred in cars, woods, and at the defendants' homes from 2009 to 2014. Hassan-Sule and Saleh were sentenced to nine and four years in jail, respectively. The girls, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge criticized the defense's argument that the girls came forward because they were victims, stating that it stops other girls from coming forward.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials, including a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment. The trial was originally slated for May 28, but was postponed and no new date has been set.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. The deal will add to Emirates' portfolio of sporting sponsorships, including a £150 million agreement with Arsenal, a £80 million deal with AC Milan, and a £17 million deal with Hamburg.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is aiming to compete in the Rio Olympics next year but won't swim at the world championships in Russia this summer. He was suspended by USA Swimming after a second drunken driving arrest and will compete in his first meet since the suspension. Phelps, 29, is in rehab for alcohol addiction and has enrolled in Alcoholics Anonymous.

Gareth Bale, a key player for Real Madrid, is doubtful for the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Atletico Madrid due to a calf injury. The Welsh forward limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Real Madrid's medical staff found a muscular lesion in Bale's soleus muscle. Los Blancos are also without Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks. Real Madrid is hopeful striker Karim Benzema will be fit for the match.

Scientists warn older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions over their retirement. A study found that more than 50% of pensioners with investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis panicked and sold their investments after the stock market fell by 30%. Those who followed that path and sold at the lowest point eight years ago with a pension of £100,000 would only have £63,000 today. If they had resisted the temptation to sell, the same pot would be worth £141,000 today provided they had not spent any of the cash. The study, carried out by experts at Texas Tech University, found that retirees with better-than-average ability to solve 'logic problems' were more unlikely to make misjudgments in the investment market based on their emotions. The study, which has been published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, reveals that retirees with lower cognitive ability in old age

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is criticized by Stuart Pearce for not being given enough time to turn around the club's poor form. Pearce believes the team should stay with Pellegrini, who has been around the block long enough to realize the squad needs freshening up this summer.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday. Manchester United, currently in fourth place, hopes to win the match and move four points clear of City in the league standings. The game is significant as it is Manchester United's first derby against City since the Sir Alex Ferguson era, and victory could give them a significant advantage in the league.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona at home, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to turn their domination into goals. Fiorentina is now in sixth place on 49 points, one place and a point behind Sampdoria who occupy the final Europa League qualifying spot.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy, with some users advising her to shave, while others defended her choice. Cyrus is known for her controversial sartorial choices, and her personal grooming habits have caused a social media stir.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance has boosted Barcelona's goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

A 44-year-old pedestrian named Andrea McVeigh was struck by a cyclist who was riding on the pavement in Bermondsey, south London. The cyclist fled the scene after hitting McVeigh, who suffered two three-inch gashes to the middle of her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. The cyclist initially stopped after the impact but then sped off. McVeigh's husband chased the cyclist, who turned around and smiled at him as he disappeared. The police have issued CCTV footage of the cyclist they want to speak to in connection with the crash. McVeigh is currently off work sick with facial injuries and is seeking justice for the incident.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for claiming he could only walk 200 metres when he was a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report about his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new way to unlock its devices using a user's face. The patent details a system that would automatically unlock a device if the user's face matches a previously taken photo. The system would use the front-facing camera to scan the user's face and unlock the device if the image matches one on file. This would replace current methods of unlocking a device, which are "inconvenient and time consuming." The patent was filed by Apple in March 2011 and was awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, a 51-year-old mother of two battling cancer, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. The incident occurred when an airline representative noticed she had put on a surgical mask to shield herself from germs and asked if she needed anything. Mrs. Sedway initially said she was fine, but when the representative approached her a second time, she indicated that she might require a little extra time to board the plane because she sometimes felt 'weak.' The family eventually boarded the plane and were awaiting takeoff in their seats when an airline representative came on board and announced that the cancer-stricken passenger could not fly without a note from her doctor. The incident has been shared nearly 10,000 times on Facebook.

A vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar was involved in a head-on collision with a 1973 Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off. No one was injured, but all three adults involved were taken to hospital for precautionary measures. Police are investigating the incident. The crash occurred on Warringah Road. The Jaguar is considered a rare and valuable classic car. The incident comes after police warned of increased risks during the Easter long weekend.

Google has set up a team to boost the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries since 2012. The team is also developing batteries that function at subfreezing temperatures for Google's Project Loon balloons. Apple has nine job listings related to batteries on its recruitment site, including an iOS battery life software engineer and an iOS software power systems engineer.

The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro. It features a helipad, infinity pool, car storage, and space for 12 guests. The yacht is capable of carrying a helicopter, twin limo tenders, car, submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and inflatables. The cost to build the yacht is approximately 40 million euros, making it expensive to purchase. The layout includes a large carrying capacity for toys and tenders, and there are special sundecks for loungers with ladders into the sea. The yacht is described as a sumptuous retreat at sea, with a unique layout that includes an enclosed observation deck, cinema, beach club, sauna, scuba diving pool, gymnasium, and ample space for 12 guests.
Ed Miliband, Labour leader, announced plans to cap rents despite warnings from experts that they will backfire, leading to more tenants being evicted and investment in new housing being slashed.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hoped Arsenal would win in a video was removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was offered the chance to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to astronomers seeking to understand what is causing this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may even contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, with a temperature difference of about 70 nano-Kelvins, which is enough to stand out when the entire cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB) of the universe is measured.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair where he was shot in 1865 as part of its observance of the 150th anniversary of the assassination. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back, is part of the museum's collection and has been housed in various locations since its founding.

A 19-year-old vlogger named Jake Boys surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking tickets to see One Direction perform in Cardiff. However, he mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead of Wales, where the concert was actually taking place. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has developed a mobile X-ray scanner, the Roboscan 2M Aeria, that can scan entire planes for contraband, bombs, and weapons. The device, which costs €3 million, is already being used to check trucks at borders in Eastern Europe and has helped seize 76,000 packs of illegal cigarettes. The company claims it can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes. The device can detect weapons and other contraband in small or medium-sized jets that land at low-security airports.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. Munden, described as having a 'fanatical obsession' with young girls, was last seen leaving a hospital in Hampshire. He was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. Munden, formerly of Southampton, is autistic and suffers from mild learning difficulties. He is believed to have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital. A court heard he admitted ten unrelated offences of possessing or attempting to possess indecent images of children. Officers are launching a manhunt to find Munden, who is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, of a heavy build, and has dark hair.

Middlesbrough are top of the Championship, with just four weeks remaining. They have a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth and are favored to win the title. The match against Watford on Monday is a lunchtime kick-off, which could give Middlesbrough an advantage. Watford's Odion Ighalo is excited to play in the English top flight, while Bournemouth's Steve McClaren is confident they will win their game against Birmingham. The promotion race is so tight that a win for Watford and Norwich could change the top two. Jonathan Woodgate, Middlesbrough's captain, is hoping to play through a broken toe.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women sharing images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with users posting beauty shots featuring professional models and selfies. The trend has been embraced by both men and women, with some using it as a statement of defiance and others as a fashion statement. The trend can be traced back to designer Jean Paul Gaultier's catwalk show at Paris Fashion Week earlier this month, which featured silver-haired models.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and financial difficulties, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after living without gas, water, and electricity for months. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had created online fundraisers but failed to draw any donations. Their suicide pact was discovered when firefighters found a pair of charcoal grills filled with smoldering coals in their bedroom. The couple left behind two daughters, Randa and Kira, who called them "the hardest-working people I know."

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications he would quit if the party is left out of power. Clegg emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the risks of losing the center ground and undoing past sacrifices. Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope to be made Chancellor if the Lib Dems form another coalition with the Conservatives.
