Clegg also appeared to lean towards another deal with the Tories, saying he deserved 'credit' for forming the Coalition while enduring 'five years of constant bile from the Labour Party.'

A pensioner in Somerset was attacked by a badger that was the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth while enjoying the sunshine with his Jack Russell. The badger, which had two cubs, burst through a hedge and attacked the pensioner's dog, which pulled him back indoors. The pensioner was left badly shaken and fears he could have been attacked if his dog had not been there. The National Farmers' Union has issued advice for residents on protecting their property from invading badgers.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg on Wednesday. Mourinho visited Fulham's Motspur Park training ground with his son Jose Junior. Fulham's Liam Donnelly was sent off, but Mourinho seemed in good spirits. Porto won 3-0, with Leandro Silva scoring a hat-trick. Mourinho's side, Chelsea, are closing in on the Premier League title with six games to play.

Andreas Christopheros, a 29-year-old property developer, was severely injured in a December 2014 acid attack on his home in Truro, Cornwall. Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, was charged with perverting the course of justice and is due to appear at Bodmin Magistrates Court on April 30. Her husband, David Phillips, 48, was already charged with grievous bodily harm with intent. Mr Christopheros, a father-of-one, suffered life-changing injuries, including a loss of vision and facial scars, after the attack.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route has erected signs warning pilgrims not to defecate along the famous path, as angry residents complain about the practice. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have become an attraction for pilgrims. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there are few places to relieve themselves. The signs are posted next to warnings that urge people not to litter. The mayor of the town says it is a "huge failure" that needs to be remedied.

A massive fire destroyed a building that once housed a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. Flames engulfed the structure, which was located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. The fire affected only the building itself and a few nearby power lines. Local resident Terry Rauh reported that a fire had occurred there before. The investigation into the cause of the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give Shoshana Hebshi $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search, and held her for hours.

A plane crash landed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people and causing the airport to close. The Airbus A320, bound from Incheon International Airport in South Korea, reportedly missed the runway and skidded off, spinning 180 degrees. Local media described it as a crash landing, with no sign of the landing gear. The incident occurred after the plane had set off from Seoul, South Korea, and is believed to have overran the runway at 8pm local time.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality TV star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000 and has a sun or moon that moves depending on the hour of the day.

Veteran actor Robert Hardy is selling his extensive collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The 89-year-old, known for his roles in "All Creatures Great and Small" and "Winston Churchill," is auctioning off more than 200 items he has collected over his career. The most unusual item is a hand-painted limewood diorama depicting the Battle of Agincourt in 3D, estimated to fetch £4,000 to £6,000. The sale includes paintings, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and a fine collection of crystal chandeliers.

A Brazilian commuter, Nelson Felippe, took a photo of a woman hugging another woman on a train platform and shared it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the scene. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. Felippe's post, which cleverly mocks conservative attitudes, warns against public displays of affection and challenges social conventions. He believes such behavior can be dangerous and should be avoided. Felippe, who works at the Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, is actually observing a public transport safety regulation, which the man in the photo is breaking. The post has received thousands of comments, with users praising Felippe's witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan, Jonathan Stevenson, wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket great, asking for tips on left-handed leg spin almost 20 years ago. Benaud's detailed response, dated September 27, 1996, was shared on Twitter as a tribute to the "great man." The letter included notes on spin bowling for left-hand bowlers, explaining the difference in coaching between right-handed and left-handed bowlers. Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler, also provided advice on different deliveries and how to deliver them.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will revolutionize travel, allowing users to experience destinations from multiple viewpoints and even change their perspectives. The company purchased Oculus, a virtual reality headset maker, and promised virtual reality gaming would be available "this year." Zuckerberg mentioned that users will be able to see the world from multiple viewpoints using the Oculus Rift headset, which is expected to be used in videos filmed with multiple cameras. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, preventing her from getting married on her birthday. Her boyfriend, Guo Kai, arranged for professional photographers to take wedding photos for her, despite her condition requiring frequent medical attention. Despite the challenges, the couple's love and commitment were evident, and they planned to celebrate their love with a photo shoot on her birthday.

Blaine Boudreaux, 34, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death after three separate DUI collisions in Houston that killed a 6-year-old boy and injured his mother. Boudreaux, who has a history of DUIs in Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic, killing the boy and injuring his mother. The suspect was arrested at the scene after failing a field sobriety test.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company, with positions based at its Redmond campus in Washington and run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers, with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella apologizing for comments suggesting women don't need to ask for raises.

Two deputies involved in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned due to threats against them and their families. The shooting occurred when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot Harris, who was trying to arrest him. The deputies are not charged with a crime but have faced criticism for their actions. The sheriff's office has suspended operations of the drug unit pending a review of the April 2 shooting. The FBI has cleared the agency of any civil rights violations. The shooting has led to allegations of forgery and unqualified training, with the sheriff denying these claims. The family of Eric Harris has demanded justice and changes in policy.

A couple, Katie Prager and Dalton Prager, are in a race against time as Katie Prager, a 24-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis, waits for a life-saving lung transplant. Katie was diagnosed with Burkholderia Cepacia in 2009 and is in critical condition, with doctors predicting she would not live a year without new lungs. Her husband, Dalton, has already received new lungs, but Katie is waiting for a transplant at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. Katie's insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs, leaving the couple in a desperate situation. Dalton is pleading for help, saying that his wife is being turned into a number and a statistic by her insurance company. The couple is running out of options and needs help to save Katie's life.

The Sleep Cycle app data reveals that the world's earliest wake-up time is on a Monday in South Africa, while Americans wake up at 7am and are in the worst mood all week. Slovakia tops the list for national average sleep quality, with the UK in 45th place and the US in 49th. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on a Wednesday night, with over half of countries surveyed saying they have the most restful sleep on this day. The data also shows that people in Finland get the most hours of sleep on a Saturday, while in Japan, people get an average of just six hours and nine minutes sleep. The best sleep quality in the world is recorded in China on Thursdays, and Americans typically don't rise until 8:24am on Fridays, reporting the best wake-up mood.

Mexican artist Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to her lover Jose Bartoli, written during their secret three-year romance, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, written in Spanish between August 1946 and November 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. Frida signed her letters to Jose 'Mara', which biographer Hayden Herrera explained is probably short for 'Maravillosa', a name Jose would call her.

Red Len McCluskey, the fiery leader of the trade union Unite, is highly popular with Labour activists during his two-day tour in Wales. However, his union's influence on Labour candidates is a potent, sinister force seeking to drag Britain back to the dark days of the 1970s. McCluskey, a former dock worker and socialist revolutionary, openly yearns for the 1970s when unions held the government to ransom. His union, Unite, has a claimed membership of 1.42 million and remains addicted to failed socialist policies, including a major expansion in the public sector, higher taxation, and ever more state spending.

Zoologist Elad Hershkowitz captured footage of various animals drinking water in their enclosures using a GoPro camera. The footage shows a range of drinking behaviors, from a rhino almost kissing the surface to a lemur delicately licking it. Some animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence. The zookeeper anticipated a range of reactions from the animals and ensured the camera was secure before the experiment.
Just a quarter of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, a poll reveals today as the Prime Minister tries to step up his campaign passion.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev, accused of being involved in the shooting of the politician in Moscow on February 27, told the court he had been abducted, beaten, and pressured into confessing to Nemstov's murder. Dadaev had previously confessed to the killing but now says he was beaten and pressured into making that statement. Dadaev is one of five Chechen men accused of killing the opposition leader. Nemstov was shot in the back four times on a bridge close to the Kremlin in February, sparking a huge protest march in Moscow.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed over 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before soldiers found him at 10 a.m. on Sunday. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue but was uninjured. His unlikely rescue provides hope to a country devastated by the disaster.

A Church of Scientology-affiliated drug rehabilitation center, Narcocon, is attempting to convert a historic property near Camp David into a drug rehab center, despite opposition from local residents and environmentalists. The property, Trout Run, is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical use, making it a potential loophole for Narcocon to build their center. The proposed program, which uses sauna sessions and the teachings of L. Ron Hubbard, has been sued in the past for wrongful deaths. Narcocon officials deny that the program tries to convert addicts to Scientology, but their website prominently features Hubbard's quote. The historic designation could allow Narcocon to conduct their program, potentially leading to controversy and legal challenges.

The article describes the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English due to NATO's reliance on their language skills have been fired and blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. They sleep in market stalls and avoid traveling to see their families. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and new residents reclaiming streets. The U.S. Embassy and NATO declined to comment.

One US Navy SEAL died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, a Navy spokesman said. The two members of the Navy's elite sea, air, land teams were found at the bottom of the pool by another service member around 3pm local time at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, is set to show live Premier League matches in the United States for the first time this weekend, with more than one in ten Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live. NBC has doubled US interest in the Premier League in the past two years, with 32 million people watching at least one match in 2013-14, compared to 13 million in 2012-13. The move comes as NBC hosts Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Kyle Martino, along with pitchside analysts Lee Dixon and Robbie Mustoe, prepare to cover the Manchester derby at Old Trafford and the Liverpool-Newcastle match at Anfield. Lowe, a Crystal Palace fan, is helping to influence young American football choices, with replica Premier League shirts now being seen more frequently.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said on the Andrew Marr Show, accusing him of "stabbing the country in the back" by forming a deal with the SNP to get into power. Johnson, who appeared alongside Miliband, launched a personal attack, with their exchange descending into a shouting match. Miliband responded by saying, "Come on Boris, you're better than that." The rivals' heated exchange ended with presenter Andrew Marr injecting humor, and the men trying to laugh about it.

A 26-year-old prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The judge sentenced him to an additional 30 days for contempt of court. The incident occurred when Dustin Irons, who was appearing via video-link, became disgruntled with the proceedings and exposed himself despite being in handcuffs. Sheriff's officers quickly covered him up and bundled him back to his cell. Captain Stewart Harp, who witnessed the incident, expressed admiration for Irons' creativity. Irons, who had been arrested for trashing a hotel room and assaulting people inside, was already in prison since December. He faces another disciplinary investigation and could be placed in a segregation unit for his misdemeanor.

Jenson Button believes McLaren has improved significantly since the Australian Grand Prix, with both he and Fernando Alonso discovering the car was competitive alongside other midfield runners. Although Button and Alonso retired during the race, the team's progress was noted, and they are now hoping to race against other cars. McLaren acknowledges that they still have a long way to go, but they are moving in the right direction.

A hospital in Western Australia, Fiona Stanley, was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitized medical instruments, leading to its medical service provider being stripped of its contract and fined. The hospital has been found to continue operating with poorly sanitized instruments, raising concerns about patient safety. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated morale issues among its workforce.

Becca Litchfield and her partner Dale, who chose to forgo their dream wedding to pay for IVF, have welcomed twins and found a way to say their "I do's" after winning a wedding competition. The couple, who had attempted two rounds of IVF, were overjoyed when they discovered the fertility treatment had worked, and Becca gave birth to twins, Darci-Mai and Stanley.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for 24 hours, with the page being replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other brands. The company issued an apology and removed the content, but it was not until a day later that Facebook was contacted to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the US caused confusion and laughter with its vocalizations after meeting a young husky dog. The Shibu Inu squeaked and squawked, attempting to bark at its new companion, which caused the husky to whine. The video shows the two dogs engaging in intense barking, whining, and yapping at one another, with people in the background laughing and mimicking their actions. The video concludes with the husky losing interest and the Shibu Inu settling down.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English seamer, is preparing to lead England in the upcoming Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to challenge the opposition and has trained hard to become the fastest bowler on the pitch. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the West Indies' conditions. He is determined to earn his spot and perform well in the first Test against the West Indies on April 13.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. Smith, who has lost two previous challenges to Ward, is seen as a potential warm-up opponent for a rematch with Carl Froch. The WBA has ordered Ward and Froch to meet in a unification fight, with Froch willing to travel to the UK if Ward returns the compliment by coming to the UK. Smith is expected to face Andre Ward in Oakland's Oracle Arena, with the fight being seen as a chance for him to shake off the ring rust.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but faced a crisis when five of her six police officers and several other top officials resigned after her election. The resignations were attributed to "safety concerns," and the outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, has no idea why the employees quit. The town, with 713 residents, is 57% white and 41% black, and has experienced a surge in crime, despite a large police force. The new mayor's father, Simon Wofford, says his daughter has a good relationship with the police department.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club but is set to become available this summer. The Ivorian, who has played a major role in City's recent trophy-winning period, is content with his life at the Etihad Stadium and is not in a rush to leave. However, his wages are a stumbling block towards a potential move. Inter Milan, managed by Roberto Mancini, are interested but given his huge wages, there are some doubts. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24 million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants do not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder, which is also known as clinical depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 38% of those taking antidepressants did not meet the criteria for obsessive compulsive disorder, panic disorder, social phobia, or generalised anxiety disorder. The researchers concluded that many individuals prescribed antidepressants may not have met the criteria for mental disorders. The study was conducted by U.S. investigators who looked at those taking selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), the most commonly prescribed type of antidepressant. SSRIs are usually the first choice medication for depression and other psychiatric conditions because they generally have fewer side effects than most other types of antidepressant. The study was published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry. Doris Fuller, the mother of a mentally ill daughter who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller wrote about how her daughter's illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that. The article also mentions that despite proper treatment, her daughter eventually decided to stop taking her meds, which brought her troubles back, even more acute than before.

A 10-year-old boy named Koby Hodder nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. He collapsed while playing British Bulldog, a game where children run from one side of a field to another without being caught. Koby's heart stopped for 12 minutes, leading to a cardiac arrest. He was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, who had a similar cardiac arrest in 2012. Teachers performed CPR until paramedics arrived, who used a defibrillator to save Koby's life.

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, advocates for changes to divorce laws in England and Wales to remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in matrimonial disputes. She proposes a one-year cooling-off period after declaring that a marriage has permanently broken down, encouraging couples to resolve arrangements for children and money before obtaining a divorce. This overhaul aims to make the divorce process more equitable and less reliant on fault-based claims.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering building a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise, potentially becoming their home. The stadium, set to open in 2018-19, would feature a synthetic surface beneath a retractable grass pitch, allowing for NFL-style games. The NFL is expected to have a permanent franchise in London within five years, and teams are testing logistics for their three games at Wembley this autumn. Tottenham's new stadium, with a capacity of 65,000, is seen as more suitable for NFL requirements than Wembley's 90,000 seats. The NFL sees the new stadium as advantageous, despite concerns about the national stadium's status and seating capacity.

U.S. senators have written to FIFA, calling for Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup due to its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The senators, including John McCain, urge FIFA to move the global competition.

Universal announced the release date for the sequel to "Fifty Shades of Grey" on February 10, 2017, and February 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, married to the author of the trilogy, will write the script for the second film. James, who has been credited with keeping creative control, is no longer directing the sequel.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and his overall record is one of the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and he is the only manager in the Premier League with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but West Brom's home defeats against QPR and Leicester City have left them stuck on 33 points, with four of their final five fixtures coming against Liverpool, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Arsenal, leaving little wriggle-room. Pulis has a good reputation as an organiser, tactician, and player-bender, but he has never finished higher

Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the championship following a gun attack on their team bus during a match. The bus was attacked as it drove to the airport after a match against Caykur Rizespor. The injured driver, who was taken to hospital, seeks medical help. Fenerbahce considers the attack unacceptable and demands justice for the driver. The club has posted pictures of the damaged bus, including shattered windows and bullet holes. The incident occurred after Fenerbahce won a match against Rizespor.

A massive snow avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The avalanche, which occurred during the Nepal earthquake, left climbers and local workers dazed and shocked. Helicopters rescued 8,000 injured people and 17 dead climbers from the mountain. The avalanche struck Base Camp, but climbers at higher camps, estimated to be in the hundreds, could not descend on their own due to the dangerous Khumbu Icefall.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Donetsk, Ukraine. In 2014, he found himself again in the middle of a war in Eastern Ukraine, where a stray missile hit his house, killing his daughter. Margolin and his family fled to Israel, where he arrived in March 2014. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews has brought 600 Jews to Israel since December, including Margolin.

John Carver, Newcastle United's assistant manager, is eager to take charge of the team against Sunderland on Sunday, knowing the outcome could impact his chances of winning the head coach position. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players in 1999, which led to a 2-1 defeat, serves as a cautionary tale for Carver. The match is expected to be crucial, with Carver hoping a win could boost his chances of securing the job beyond the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning in North Charleston, South Carolina, where a black driver was fatally shot by a white police officer. Sharpton called for reform in national policing legislation and urged the community to use this opportunity to change policing practices. He also attended a vigil near the scene of the Scott shooting on Sunday afternoon.

Brendan Rodgers will remind Raheem Sterling of his responsibilities after the Liverpool youngster hit the headlines for the wrong reasons before scoring the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide, also known as 'hippy crack', and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. The 20-year-old faces a club investigation and potential disciplinary action over his behaviour, and Liverpool manager Rodgers now says he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails.

Labour received more than £1 million in union donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservative party, in a boost to Ed Miliband's election campaign. Unions gave more than £700,000 to Labour, with Dave Prentis and Len McCluskey contributing £400,000 each. The union donations equate to £105,420.80 a day, or £1.22 a second.

Police were called to Manchester Airport after passengers on a Qatar Airways flight became disruptive and kicked off during a delay at Birmingham Airport. The flight was diverted due to strong winds, causing a 24-hour delay and resulting in passengers being stranded at the airport. The airline apologized for the delay, which occurred after the operating crew exceeded their legal flying hours.

Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300 million mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. The 21-year-old performer has been close friends with Mayweather for years and has accompanied him into the ring on numerous occasions. Bieber is set to lead Mayweather's entourage at the MGM Grand.

The U.S. Department of Education announced that Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit career college, will shut down all of its remaining 28 campuses. This is a positive development in the long struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable, as Corinthian once enrolled more than 70,000 students. The article highlights the predatory nature of for-profit colleges, which enroll only 13% of college students but account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. The closure of Corinthian marks a new chapter in the for-profit college crisis, with graduates of the now-defunct college joining a "debt strike" and the Department of Education signaling a willingness to forgive loans of Corinthian graduates.

Pep Guardiola denies a dispute with former Bayern Munich doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit after claiming the bond of trust was damaged. Muller-Wohlfahrt blamed the medical staff for the defeat by Porto, but Guardiola says it was his decision and injuries are part of football. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, is set to make his return to Madison Square Garden for a world title defence against Bryant Jennings. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in 1996, recalls how it changed his life and the power of sport to change one's life. Despite being just a year short of his 40th birthday, Klitschko believes age has no bearing on how long he can go on for.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear, has admitted he will miss fronting the show. Former presenter Angela Rippon said she would be keen to return to the motoring show if invited back. Lord Hall, the director-general of the BBC, announced that the corporation would not be renewing Clarkson's contract.

In a La Liga match, Fabian Orellana of Celta Vigo threw a lump of grass at Sergio Busquets during a heated argument, leading to Orellana being shown a red card. Busquets, who was also involved in the incident, grabbed his eye despite the grass hitting him. Barcelona's Luis Enrique's side earned a crucial three points after Real Madrid's 9-1 victory against Granada earlier in the day.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when bombs went off at the Boston Marathon finish line. This year, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, the man convicted of the bombings, faces sentencing. Judge George A. O'Toole warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the race, stressing the importance of avoiding prejudicial information. The sentencing phase is expected to last four weeks, with the maximum penalty for several charges being death.

Tens of millions of Chinese people marked the Qingming Festival, a three-day holiday, by travelling home to their ancestral villages to clean tombs, burn fake paper money, and leave food and drink to ensure their loved ones are not poor or hungry in the afterlife. The festival, which celebrates the coming spring and the beauty of nature, is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms and falls in the first week of April every year.

Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. His album outsold those by more youthful musicians like Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping him reach the top of the charts. The album includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits like 50 Ways to Leave Your Lover. It marks Simon's first top-charting album since The Rhythm of the Saints in 1990.

Iker Casillas insists he will stay at Real Madrid even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper. The 33-year-old Spanish goalkeeper claims he is willing to fight for the jersey he went on to make his own after breaking in to the side as a 16-year-old in 1996. Real Madrid has repeatedly linked to a move for Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas hopes to fulfil his contract and earn the starting position, stating that things are decided by details and that Real Madrid is a team of fight, struggle, and effort.

Britain's employment hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, with the International Monetary Fund praising Chancellor George Osborne's economic strategy. The Conservative government has created more jobs in the last five years than the rest of the EU combined, with Rolls-Royce announcing its biggest-ever order for passenger jets. IMF chief Christine Lagarde and German finance minister Wolfgang Schaeuble praised Osborne's handling of the economy, while Labour's opposition to austerity measures has been weakened. The Chancellor, speaking at the IMF and World Bank meetings, said the UK economy is on course to return to the black in 2018-19. However, Greece poses a threat to the global economy, and the deepening crisis could hit Britain.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called the Tivoli, priced under £13,000, targeting thrifty motorists. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden, and features a European name. It offers a range of engines, transmissions, and safety features, including a five-year unlimited mileage warranty. The Tivoli aims to double SsangYong's annual UK sales from 2,000 to 4,000 vehicles.

A chef, Sam Longhurst, created a 10-inch, half-kilogram burger at the Whole Damn Farm restaurant in Manchester, containing six forms of three different meats and 2,000 calories. The burger features two beef patties, homemade bacon jam, ham chunks, a whole fried chicken thigh, barbequed pulled pork, and bacon rashers. The creation was inspired by a customer's request for a burger with three kinds of meat. The restaurant owner, Mike Edge, said the burger is a "supersized version" of a homemade burger stuffed with cheese and cold meats.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, known for its high-quality meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef, has opened to the public at a higher price. The canteen, praised as the world's best staff canteen, offers meals like organic sourdough with Yeo Valley salted butter and a dessert of apple and rhubarb crumble with ice cream or creme fraiche. The canteen's menu changes daily based on the available produce. The canteen has been open to the public since earlier this week, with prices higher than the subsidised prices for the workers.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is "much better" and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987 and has 30 Grammy nominations. King, who suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago last year, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille.

On Easter Sunday, Manhattan's Fifth Avenue was filled with bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday. The parade featured a variety of headwear, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets. Some participants wore more conservative attire, while others opted for more colorful and whimsical options. The event attracted a diverse crowd, including Christians, Jews, Hindus, agnostics, and atheists. The parade, which has been held since the 1880s, was a departure from its earlier strolling display and featured a mix of traditional and modern headwear.

Emergency crews in East of England received 1,248 inappropriate calls in two years, including one where a squirrel was mistaken for a human victim, and one where a woman reported feeling ill after eating too much takeaway food. The service prioritizes life-threatening calls but warns that inappropriate calls can affect their response times.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake, along with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian, participated in a football challenge with Audi. Hazard and Ake won the first round by scoring 5-3, while Remy and Willian won the second round. In the final round, Hazard and Ake won the challenge by sinking footballs into the boot of an Audi from long range. Willian and Remy were involved in a misfortune when Willian smashed the wing mirror off an Audi with a long-range effort.

Brendan Rodgers criticizes Raheem Sterling's advisor, Aidy Ward, for allegedly being manipulated by outside forces, suggesting Sterling would stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Rodgers sat down with Sterling to advise him to stay at the club, despite the player rejecting a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and having just two years left on his deal. Sterling has also rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up the eight-letter word "erection" as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as the blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word. The incident is not the first time Hewer has struggled to contain himself when a rude word has popped up on the show.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who attempted to buy deadly poison online and later pleaded guilty to trying to commit suicide, was spared jail after the court heard he was unaware his online requests were being tracked by counter-terrorism officers. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was arrested in February and later sentenced to a 12-month referral order. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web and the importance of vigilance in law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at North Manchester General Hospital in December. The incident occurred just months after three babies and one mother died at the same hospital. The deaths prompted an investigation, and Hindle's partner, Chris Barnes, has called for action to prevent further tragedies at the maternity unit.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman, a two-time world champion hurdler, gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of her training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, 32, plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, incorporating training into her pregnancy until the final trimester. Her coach, Mike Hurst, praised her careful training and monitoring of her core temperature. Emily was born at a healthy 3.1 kilograms on Monday.

At least one person died and at least four people were missing after a powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Alabama, with the Coast Guard searching for survivors late into the night. The storm, which rolled through the area around 4 p.m., was reported to have caused significant damage and loss of life. The Dauphin Island Regatta, which had more than 100 sailboats and 200 participants, was canceled due to the storm.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has been diagnosed with macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that are getting progressively worse over time and can steal vision. Her doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. Barr said in an interview that she helps relieve the pressure by using marijuana. Macular degeneration is a breakdown of the part of the retina that allows us to see fine details in the center of vision, while glaucoma damages the nerve that connects the retina to the brain. The risk for both diseases goes up for everyone after age 60, with some people, especially African Americans, at higher risk in their 40s. There is no cure for either disease, but treatments can delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

An Oklahoma jury convicted 17-year-old Chancey Luna of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of Australian college baseball player Christopher Lane, who was killed while jogging in Duncan. Luna was found guilty of the fatal shooting from a passing car, and the jury recommended life in prison without parole. Luna's defense attorney argued that he meant to scare Lane, but the judge denied a second-degree murder conviction. Luna did not testify, and the defense called only his mother as a witness.

Arsene Wenger insists his record against Jose Mourinho will not affect Arsenal's match against Chelsea, as the two teams face off in the Premier League. Wenger has lost seven and drawn five of their 12 meetings. Chelsea's strengths include efficient counter-attacks and set-pieces, while Arsenal has a good run of form and desire to win. Wenger expects a good game at the Emirates, and Chelsea has a strong chance of securing the title.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become a global superstar after a series of mega-fights, including a fight against Floyd Mayweather on Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before being given his chance on the big stage in 2001. He has made a remarkable rise through the weight divisions from being an incredibly slight light-flyweight when he made his debut. Pacquiao left home aged 14 to move to the Philippines capital Manila to pursue his career in the sport. He is now one of the biggest stars in the world.

Jack Grealish, a talented young footballer, has been photographed inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can be used recreationally but is also illegal. Grealish, who starred for Aston Villa in their FA Cup semi-final win over Liverpool, has been caught on camera using the drug. Grealish's actions have been described as a way to keep him grounded and focused on his career. Wenger, the manager of Arsenal, has stated that professional athletes have a duty to look after their bodies and that alcohol is a poison that slows down the body. Grealish's confidence and future as a top footballer have been questioned, with some suggesting that he may have made the wrong choices.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 in cosmetic surgery to resemble reality TV star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men with eggs on Easter Monday after being targeted online for his appearance. The attack occurred at a pub in Sutton Coldfield, West Midlands, where Barton had checked in on Facebook minutes before. The assailants reportedly tracked Barton down using his social media posts and then pelted him with eggs, leaving him with yolk and shell on the pavement. Barton believes he was targeted because he had "checked in" at the pub and spent £55,000 on his appearance. The incident highlights the challenges faced by individuals pursuing a celebrity lifestyle, including financial strain and online harassment.

Manchester University in Indiana was in lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. Police said they received a phone call from someone saying that they had stabbed their roommate at the university, was armed with a shotgun and threatening to blow up the administration building. Manchester University had issued a statement advising students at its North Manchester campus, some 36 miles west of Fort Wayne, to shelter in place. Barricade yourself in a room, stay away from windows. Be quiet, silence cell. Wait for police or All-Clear. The person was possibly armed with explosives, according to the university. North Manchester Police, a bomb squad from Fort Wayne and Indiana State Police were all at the scene. No injuries have been confirmed.

Edinson Cavani, known as "El Matador," will face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals, with the spotlight on him as PSG struggle to progress beyond the last eight. Despite having a reputation for class, Cavani has endured a goal drought and has faced challenges in recent matches.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds and was awarded a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull, after a derby defeat, won a surprise 28-20 match against St Helens, which shocked the home side. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, and Jordan Rankin added the extras. The game was tense, with Hull's Tom Makinson bringing Saints level after Shaul's early try. Hull's Jordan Pryce scored a try, and Hull's Tom Rankin added the goal. Saints' Alex Walmsley nearly scored a try, but the in-goal touch judge ruled a knock on. Hull's Adam Swift lost the ball, and Hull forced an error, which Hull's Jordan Hohaia drove towards the posts.

The United States' undocumented and documented immigrant population is projected to reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the population by 2060. This growth is expected to continue, with immigration population growing almost four times faster than the native-born population. The Center for Immigration Studies predicts that by 2060, immigrants could make up 82% of the population. This trend has significant implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment.

Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury for Arsenal Under 21s, but the team lost 1-0 to Reading's U21s. Wilshere was joined by other injured players including Serge Gnabry and Abou Diaby. Martin Keown's son, Niall, scored the winning goal for Reading in the opening minutes.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has fallen outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing, but he has been working hard on the practice ground. Rose's return to the sixties score of 69 at the Shell Houston Open is a welcome sign, and he is optimistic about his future at the Masters. Phil Mickelson, who enjoyed his best round in months with a 66, is proud of his position in the world rankings and is focused on his game.

A £25 million mansion built on the site of a former milking parlour in Mayfair, London, has gone on the market. The property, which features modern amenities like an indoor swimming pool and a cinema room, was once a milking parlour and a depot before being demolished in the 19th century. The mansion, which has four bedrooms, is decorated with modern furnishings and has a private lift and guest cloakroom. It was constructed in 2011 after developers demolished the original structure. The property is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank for £25 million.

Bayern Munich's squad is weakened by injuries, but Thomas Muller believes the team's unity is stronger. The Bavarians, chasing three titles, are without key players Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League quarter-final against Porto. Muller says the team's recent games with a decimated squad helped build unity. Bayern coach Pep Guardiola is eyeing a Treble of Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and Champions League.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited their team's base in Brackley to discuss strategies for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. After being beaten by Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel at the Malaysian Grand Prix, the Mercedes drivers were determined to win in Shanghai. The visit was part of their efforts to find a winning formula for the race. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that he was surprised by Vettel's victory, which was attributed to Ferrari's tactics and the cooler temperatures in China. The race results showed that Vettel won by 8. 5 seconds, with Hamilton a further 12. 5 seconds behind. Mercedes now faces the challenge of adapting to Ferrari's tactics in the upcoming race.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to use nitrogen gas for executions if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or unavailable. The bill, signed on Friday, states that the person will become unconscious within 8-10 seconds and die a few minutes later. This follows a review by the U.S. Supreme Court of Oklahoma's use of lethal injections, which has been put on hold. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, saying Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A Russian freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and sinking in just 15 minutes. More than 1,300 people are involved in the massive rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking was reportedly caused by an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast, and the trawler hit an object in the sea, possibly drifting ice. The incident occurred at around 4am local time, and temperatures in the water can drop to as low as -2 degrees Celsius.

Men with advanced prostate cancer could benefit from a pioneering drug originally meant for women, according to new clinical trials. Olaparib, already used to treat women with breast cancer, showed promise in delaying the progression of prostate cancer in men with genetic defects within their tumours. The drug, known as Lynparza, extended the length of time that patients with advanced prostate cancer lived without their disease getting worse. The London trial, led by researchers at the Institute of Cancer Research and the Royal Marsden hospital, found that 16 out of 49 men responded to the drug, with lower tumour cell counts in the blood and improved responses in medical scans. Olaparib is the first cancer drug to target inherited genetic mutations and is one of the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors. The drug became the first of a new class of drugs called PARP inhibitors to be granted approval last month for use in ovarian cancer by the European Commission and the US Food and

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12, 000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies to feature their properties on her site. Taylor has stayed at exclusive resorts with private plunge pools, idyllic spas, and sumptuous rooms, and has photographed them for her website.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The two male hippos had been fighting for some time and the mother of the calf stayed with her herd, possibly believing it safer to stay out of harm's way herself. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve. The mother tried to get the baby back but with the young calf in the sub-adult's mouth there wasn't much she could do. The hippopotamus died of its injured hours later.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident where Branislav Ivanovic was struck on the head by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters at Loftus Road. Chelsea players were targeted by objects thrown from the crowd during their victory celebration. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses to come forward. The club is banning those involved and appealing to the Metropolitan Police to identify the perpetrators.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect was found dead hours later, and while police did not say how he died, it was not a homicide. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is raising money for funeral services and has started a GoFundMe page.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, has three homes, including a £1 million property she bought from a housing association eight years ago. She opposed extending the right to buy policy to housing association tenants but now owns a £3 million property. This hypocrisy has been criticized by Conservative MPs and housing association chiefs, who are accused of drawing huge salaries while wishing to deny tenants a foot on the property ladder.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was beaten by protesters armed with iron bars during an attack on his hounds in Everleigh, Wiltshire, three months after the incident. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, police have dropped the investigation. Lane condemned the decision as "pathetic" and expressed anger at the lack of effort from the police. The attack occurred despite the hounds chasing an artificial scent rather than a fox. The incident has angered hunt supporters across the country, with Wiltshire Police confirming they have stopped the investigation pending further information.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer, stating he prefers to stay at the Mestalla. He has been linked with Premier League teams Manchester United and Chelsea, but Gomes says he is happy to stay in Spain, particularly Valencia, where he has been scoring and helping the team to fourth place in La Liga.

An Australian teenager, Audrey Pekin, was raped twice in Bali while on holiday with her family. The 19-year-old claims she was lured to a remote home by a man named Henry Alafu, who then attacked her twice. Alafu allegedly lured her to a villa and raped her in a taxi. The teenager, who has type 1 diabetes, was unable to escape and sought help from passing motorists and workers in a nearby service station. CCTV footage showed Alafu waiting in the lobby for her. The Indonesian police have let Alafu escape, and the teenager has accused them of failing to protect her.

Animal rights activist Ashley James has teamed up with PETA to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously abandoned its fur-free policy. James, who is known for her vegan lifestyle, has posed with a fake fox image on Harvey Nichols' billboards, highlighting the cruelty of the fur industry. Harvey Nichols has denied the allegations, stating that they only source products from reputable brands and that they are committed to sustainable and responsible practices.

Chile has joined several South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex, with President Michelle Bachelet's new law taking effect in six months. The law will give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman, benefiting around 2 million people. The change is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples, such as not being allowed to visit partners in hospital or make medical decisions on their behalf.

Chelsea are on track to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history, leading the table for 230 days as of April 10, 2023. They could surpass Manchester United's record of 262 days if they remain top of the league. Chelsea's 2005/06 title-winning side under Mourinho led the table for 257 days.

Cape Verde, a small Portuguese former colony with a population of 500,000, is known for having more musicians per square kilometer than any other country in the world. The country's diverse cultural heritage, shaped by the transatlantic slave trade, piracy, and Jewish exiles, has given rise to unique musical styles like batuque, morna, and funana. Cape Verde is now seeking to tap into the economic potential of its rich cultural heritage, particularly through the music and arts sectors. The country's prime minister and culture ministry have recognized the importance of music for economic growth, and the Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been celebrating its seventh edition, has become a significant event in the country.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney Opera House went viral again after heavy storms hit Sydney, with some users linking the phenomenon to the weather. The video, originally posted by Darren Johnson in June 2012, was quickly debunked by wave experts and YouTube commenters, who pointed out inaccuracies and the impossibility of the surfers breaking waves inside the harbor.

Reading, the FA Cup semi-finalists, were defeated 1-0 by Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who made a fumble against Arsenal, was retained for the match.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, will miss the Champions League match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury. The Brazilian defender, who had a run that led to his injury, will be out for at least four weeks, potentially affecting PSG's title defense.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy, with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. The show's illegal downloads increased by 45% year-on-year, jumping from 4.9 million in 2014 to 7 million in the two-month period from February to April. Brazil was the top country for illegal downloads, followed by France, the US, Canada, and the UK. HBO announced in March that the forthcoming season will air across 170 countries at the same time, and launched a new internet streaming service, HBO Now, in an attempt to curb piracy and recapture revenue.

Leicester City host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. Leicester has won just one of their last 10 home matches, while West Ham has won their last seven away games against the Foxes.

For six years, a statue of Lucille Ball in Celoron, New York, has been a source of controversy. The statue, based on a moment from her show "I Love Lucy," depicts her as drunk and pitchy for a health tonic, which locals find unflattering. A Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has attracted over 600 likes, with the anonymous creator calling for the statue's removal. Artist Dave Poulin, who created the statue, has declined to comment, and the town estimates it would cost $8,000 to $10,000 to recast it. The statue depicts Ball during her most loved moment on the show, but locals find it unflattering and frightening at night.

A woman who was forced to stand during an 11-hour flight to lose weight, fearing she was crushing the woman next to her, has shed nearly half her body weight. Sharon Smith, 43, from Halesowen, West Midlands, went from a size 26 to a healthy 9st 9lb after joining a slimming club and taking up running. She lost 4st through joining Weight Watchers Online but then shed another 4. 5 stone after taking up running.

One new mother, Nicola Bonn, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences of raising her 14-month-old daughter Poppy and the challenges of being a first-time mother. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shared a post titled "Why We Need to Stop Justifying Ourselves" that detailed the overwhelming amount of opinions and judgments she received from others.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, are feared to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS. Hassan is believed to be related to Hammaad Munshi, who was arrested at 15 for planning to murder non-Muslims. The families are in shock and worry about their safety. The boys, who were on a school trip, used the Easter holidays to flee Britain.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described the grief as especially painful because Stephanie had so much to look forward to. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but now the family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral instead. The venue turned into a memorial site after her murder.

Southampton is interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who wants to leave the club this summer. Koeman, the manager of Southampton, is keen to bring Vilhena to the south coast to bolster his squad ahead of possible European qualification. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment that has angered heritage experts. The move was designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere' but was branded 'misguided' by critics. The Trust said the beanbag experiment was 'short-term' and would not continue for the whole year. The experiment will be replicated at nine other venues around the country.

Former Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the footpath outside the Sydney Conservatorium of Music with a flat tyre, while his driver changed it. Felicity Waterford, who was waiting for her daughter at the Conservatorium, offered assistance and took a selfie with Howard. This incident came weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis acknowledges that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 lead against Queens Park Rangers, leading to a 3-2 loss. Pulis recalls his own experience of being 2-0 up but losing in a play-off final in 1999, emphasizing that teams can still struggle with late goals. Pulis also praises the team's recent performances, hoping to continue their good results.

A Bouvier's red colobus monkey, thought to be extinct for over 50 years, has been rediscovered in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Researchers captured the first-ever photograph of the monkey, which was previously known only from three specimens. The discovery proves the species is not extinct and is now being studied to learn more about it. The monkey, which was first discovered in 1887, is now officially named Piliocolobus bouvieri.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for an eight-day trip, including a stay at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan. The visit is their first to the country, where they are exploring landmarks and attending cultural events. The Kardashian-West crew is staying in the capital's finest digs, with bodyguards and police in tow. The city is known for its cultural and economic significance, with a mix of Soviet-era architecture and Neo-Classical official buildings. The trip is well-connected to major European centers, with cheaper flights available from London.

British expats Patrick and Valerie Jubb are trapped in southern Spain over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated, facing the potential loss of their property due to illegal additions made by a previous owner. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are unable to do so due to the town hall's ruling that the alterations are illegal. The Jubbs claim they obtained a certificate stating there were no infractions when they bought the estate, but the town hall disagrees. The case is unique because the property is located inside Los Alcornocales Natural Park, where the usual rule that local authorities lose the right to demolish a house that has been illegally altered if they fail to detect the alterations within four years does not apply.

Despite expectations, Apple's iPhone sales in the first quarter of 2015 surpassed analysts' forecasts, with more than 61 million iPhones sold, accounting for two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone's strong performance, driven by a 40% increase in sales compared to the previous quarter, has driven Apple's best quarter results ever, with a 72% growth in sales in China.

A 3-year-old girl, Elisa Tyler, has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a mysterious white van that she believes may have caused her mother's death in a car crash. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, says she has been having these visions since the crash, which occurred two months ago. The incident involved a 2002 Ford Explorer that crashed into a tree on a rain-soaked road in Chesterfield County, Virginia. The crash was ruled a one-car collision caused by poor road conditions. The girl's father believes the visions may be related to the white van, which he thinks may have caused her to be injured. The incident has led to a series of hit-and-run accidents involving a white box truck in the area.

Researchers have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. The study, conducted by psychologists at New York University, focused on how the brain stores memories for 'emotionally neutral events' that gain significance through subsequent experience. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing, such as the amygdala and striatum, and also the regions involved in encoding new experiences, like the hippocampus.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening brain tumour, has raised over $80,000 for his life-saving surgery. The 18-year-old has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her boyfriend, who is paralysed and unable to dress himself. The surgery is scheduled for Wednesday by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. The community has shown overwhelming support, raising $80,000 on a GoFundMe page. Jackson, who completed school at the end of last year, has put off university to help his boyfriend.

Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs, as the club considers streamlining its squad. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, played in QPR's crucial 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion at the Hawthorns. QPR have also shown interest in West Bromwich Albion's striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have discovered regional variations in English sentence structure across the United States, with some states using phrases like "I'm so totally over this" or "I ain't never had no trouble with none of 'em." The study, which analyzed 1,000 sentences from 50 states, found that people in the South are more likely to use presentative sentences, while those in the North are less likely to do so. The findings challenge the idea that English has a single grammatical system and highlight the diversity of the language in different regions.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a 9-day journey across Canada, from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia, to enjoy the scenery. He used an online advertisement site to find a free rocking chair and attached it to his trailer. The video shows him sitting in the chair, enjoying the Canadian landscape, and even mimicking planes. He traveled with a friend and his dad, sharing laughs and stories. The journey was described as a "creature comfort" experience.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a Twix multi-pack as a win bonus to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate, and thanked him for sending him the Twix.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed a night out at the darts in his hometown of Sheffield. Dave Chisnall, a darts player, won two matches in a row, moving up to second place in the Premier League table. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and was pleased with his performance.

Marco Verratti of Paris Saint-Germain praises Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role off the pitch, despite the striker's suspension for the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona.

The Ministry of Defence accidentally published a secret RAF aerodrome manual containing vital details on the Falklands Islands' defenses, including GPS coordinates and runway depth, on their website, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The information was accessible to Argentine intelligence agents, who could use it to plan an attack. The MoD acknowledged the leak but denied it was particularly sensitive. The Falklands Islands are defended by modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the UK is considering purchasing new anti-aircraft missiles.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to improve the team's offensive performance to match their defensive efficiency as they aim to climb back up the Super League ladder. The Giants have fallen from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter period. Anderson attributes the team's poor start to the fast-paced nature of the season and acknowledges the need to fix issues with the offense. If Huddersfield wins their next game, they could leapfrog Catalans Dragons, who have the best defensive record in the league.

Planners in Windsor have allowed two Costa coffee shops to open less than 500 yards apart, sparking controversy among residents who fear it will lead to an overabundance of fast food and coffee shops in the area. The new Costa will open on the site of the former Dedworth Road HSBC branch, while a Costa that replaced a cycle shop opened earlier this year, leaving only a Costa Express at a petrol station between them. One resident, Samantha Taylor, expressed concern about the situation, while another resident, Matt Gordon-Smith, argued that the new Costa is a positive development for the area. Costa's planning application states that the new shop would be a "significant driver to local trade," and planners said there was no legal reason to refuse.

The British Veterinary Association (BVA) has withdrawn its support for the controversial pilot culls of free-running badgers, stating that the first two years of culling have not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary has promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election, with critics accusing the culls of being a 'party political issue'.

Geoff Barrow, founder of Portishead, accused streaming services of giving his band's music away for free, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite 34 million plays. Barrow wants musicians to be paid more and says streaming is hurting young talent, stopping them from establishing themselves.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. Fans of the show, which follows the ambitions and betrayals of competing noble factions and families in the fantasy world of Westeros, now face the daunting task of avoiding spoilers online as the first four episodes are released over the course of the month.

A best man composed an emotional song at his brother's wedding to use as his speech, touching guests and going viral online. Daniel Buccheri, 25, performed "Stay With Me" to his brother Adrian's new wife Sarah at their March 29 wedding in Melbourne. The unique speech, viewed over 100,000 times online, included tributes to his brother and his bride, as well as a touching account of their love story.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after giving birth to her daughter Mia. She started exercising every morning, hitting the exercise bike at Gatcombe Park before her daughter wakes up. Zara, who is vying for a place on Team GB at the Rio Olympics, is committed to a strict exercise and diet regime to get back in shape.

Raheem Sterling's interview, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. Some fans hope he will leave the club, while others believe he has the potential to be worth more than the £100,000-a-week contract he turned down. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and many fans are now of the belief that if he wants to go, he's welcome to.

Barcelona's 1996 Spanish Super Cup-winning team, led by Bobby Robson and Pep Guardiola, is now breeding managers. Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui are among the current coaches of the Champions League winners, who were all part of the same team that won the 1996 Super Cup.

Eric Cantona, a former Manchester United legend, has declared Javier Pastore, a Paris Saint-Germain forward, as the best player in the world. Cantona's assessment is based on his observation of Pastore's passing skills and creativity, which he believes surpasses that of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Cantona's comments come at the Laureus World Sports Awards in Shanghai, where he was third in the Ballon d'Or in 1993 behind Roberto Baggio and Dennis Bergkamp.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder for killing his tenant Michael Spalding, 39, by dismembering his body and throwing the parts into a canal. The trial took 15 hours and was decided by an unanimous verdict at Birmingham Crown Court. Simon, with the help of his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, dumped the suitcases containing the body parts and tools into the canal. Bird was cleared of murder and manslaughter but admitted assisting an offender. The case involved dismembering the body, hacking it up, and stuffing the parts into suitcases, which were then dumped in the canal.

Local councils are using 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where elderly people and others are most at risk of social isolation, which can lead to health problems such as dementia and high blood pressure. Essex and Gloucestershire councils have already implemented the maps, and a new report recommends using them across the country. The maps are based on statistics on public health factors and surveys of residents, and are used to identify vulnerable areas and target help where it is needed most. The Campaign to End Loneliness has called on other councils to copy the maps and draw up their own versions for their local area.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she's ever had or ever wanted. She remembers when French fries and a classic Coca-Cola cost just 65 cents, and her first day on the job when she spilled a shake all over a woman's fur coat. Eddingfield has been providing top-notch service for 60 years, and her favorite memory was when Jerry Mathers and Tony Dow of the television series 'Leave It to Beaver' came to eat there in the late 1970s.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting, who had just penned a congratulation message to James Anderson, England's leading Test wicket-taker, as part of Slazenger's celebratory flag tour, believes that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell, and Joe Root play well, there might not be a place for Pietersen in the team. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014, and Gatting admits that more questions will be asked of the England captain if he fails to find runs against West Indies.

A 17-year-old college student, Caleb Benn, developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos directly from their computer to the popular photo-sharing platform. The app, which is priced at $4.99, has been generating $1,000 a day in revenue. However, Instagram has filed a lawsuit against Benn, claiming that his app violates the company's terms of service. Benn has denied the allegations, stating that he was aware of the legal gray area and that he would have fixed the app had he been given more time. The controversy highlights the tension between social media platforms and developers who want to expand their reach beyond mobile devices.

Most companies in South Korea have hoesik at least once a month and sometimes every week. For foreign business travelers, drinking etiquette is intense, with drinking considered a way to get to know someone. Koreans always identify the "higher" person in the relationship and defer to them. Avoid empty glasses, chug after everyone has poured, and turn your body away from senior figures.

The Duke of Kent, 79, has been discharged from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after being treated for a dislocated hip following an injury sustained during a trip to Balmoral Estate.
