Buckingham Palace confirmed he was successfully treated. The Duke, who became the Duke of Kent at age six, is the son of Prince George, the younger brother of King George VI and King Edward VIII. He is the country's top Freemason and has been President of the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been called into question by local business owners who believe the outdated and controversial practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer serving a public service. The practice, started in 1965 by Gold Coast developer Bernie Elsey, was introduced to stave off bad publicity associated with newly installed parking meters. However, local business owners argue that advancements in parking meter technology have made expiry times not always displayed, and the group is now violating anti-touting laws by promoting branded merchandise. Gold Coast Chamber of Commerce president Peter Yared claims the group is a business now, and he believes it is time for them to move on. The Meter Maids, led by general manager Michael Yarwood, defend their practice, stating that tourists love and embrace the group as a quintessentially part of their Gold Coast and Surfers Paradise experience.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330 million to the International Monetary Fund, claiming it will make the payment on time. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said Greece will in fact make the payment on April 9. Greece has drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay domestic bills, but the country is due to repay a £330 million loan to the International Monetary Fund on April 9.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week, citing the images as "deeply upset" the hostage's family. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US.

A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a letter to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, saying that forming emotional attachments is a value in marriage and that Jedi should avoid the dark side. Lucasfilm sent Colin a letter granting his request, and he was elated to receive a reply.
Wisconsin defeated Kentucky 71-64 in the NCAA Tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak. Wisconsin advances to the Final Four, while Kentucky finishes the season at 38-1.

Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe, and other performers have been criticized for their renditions of the national anthem, with some likened to "butchers" for their poor performances. The article highlights several notable instances where famous individuals have been called out for their singing of the anthem, including Whitney Houston, Roseanne Barr, Jimi Hendrix, and Michael Bolton.

CCTV footage of a violent altercation between Irish brothers Patrick and Barry Lyttle, resulting in Patrick's near-death, has been released. Barry, charged with grievous bodily harm, faces a potential jail term of up to two years. Patrick, who called for the charges to be dropped, comforted his brother as they watched the footage.

The family of conjoined twin sisters Faith and Hope Howie, who died 19 days after birth, were devastated to find their gravesite cleared of mementos and thrown in the rubbish by cemetery staff. The Howies had built a small shrine at the site, but when they returned to retrieve their daughters' belongings, everything had been removed apart from a bunch of flowers. The staff had not been notified that they would be cleaned, and the Howies were only able to retrieve about 25 percent of their memorabilia.

Lord Neuberger, Britain's most senior judge, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, arguing that judges and courtrooms should allow women to wear the traditional dress as a sign of respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges to be sensitive to the cultural and social habits of those facing them, noting that they often come from a more privileged sector of society. This suggestion comes amid uncertainty over the place of Muslim traditional dress in the legal system following a controversial trial in 2003.

Andre Cole, a 52-year-old Missouri inmate, was executed for the 1998 murder of his ex-wife and her friend, Anthony Curtis, in a fit of rage over child support payments. Cole was the third convicted killer executed in Missouri this year. The execution was carried out by lethal injection at the Eastern Reception, Diagnostic and Correctional Center in Bonne Terre, Missouri, at 10:15 pm on Tuesday. The execution was carried out despite appeals from the U.S. Supreme Court, which had previously denied Cole's request for clemency.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. The Duchess is several days overdue, forcing Harry to return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army and a week-long tour of New Zealand. The new baby's arrival will be announced on Twitter and Instagram, with details posted on an easel outside Buckingham Palace.

An alleged fraudster named Justin Jackson has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, former Obama aide Reggie Love, and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food, and jewelry worth $2.4 million. Jackson is being sued by Oprah's TV network and Love, and has been convicted for grand theft over a ruse in which he tricked a jeweler into lending him items worth $2.4 million. He is accused of sending letters purporting to be from Oprah and her representatives, as well as from former Obama aide Reggie Love, to recommend him for jobs and get free goods.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has set a €50 million price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the "new Messi." A bidding war is set to break out over Dybala, who is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus, and PSG. Inter Milan manager Roberto Mancini was spotted at the Stadio Ennio Tardini watching the Serie A match between Parma and Palermo on Sunday.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is facing an economic downturn and a bribery scandal at Petrobras. Rousseff's supporters are holding rallies in her support, while her opponents are calling for her impeachment. The Petrobras scandal involves a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme at the state-run oil company, with many politicians and executives accused. The protests have grown in size and breadth, with some demonstrators initially voting for Rousseff.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, "You and the Night", includes a scene with Cantona on his hands and knees in just his underwear. Cantona, 48, says it is not pornography but a work of art, praising its beauty. The film has been both praised and criticized, with some calling it an "orgy" and others an "artistic failure".

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100, 000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Manager Brendan Rodgers described the offer as "incredible." Sterling, who has two years left on his contract, has postponed contract talks until the end of the season. PFA Chief Executive Gordon Taylor defends Sterling, saying he is not a "money grabber" and believes waiting until the season is over could be a wise move. Sterling has been linked with moves to Arsenal and leading clubs in Spain. Taylor believes Sterling is aware of what he owes to Liverpool and Rodgers has put his faith in him. Sterling scored for England in their Euro 2016 qualifier with Lithuania.

An Ohio woman, La-Sonya Mitchell-Clark, discovered her biological mother, Francine Simmons, works at the same call-center operation company as her. After connecting the dots, she found out her mother is closer than she could imagine, living just six minutes away in Youngstown. Simmons, who was 'still in shock' from finding out about her daughter, reached out to Mitchell-Clark through social media, and they eventually decided to meet after a phone call. Mitchell-Clark also found out she has three younger sisters, two of whom, Kamala and Maisha Cummings, said the reunion was 'a relief' and 'amazing' for their family.

Oscar "Papoo" Hernandez Jr., a convicted gun trafficker for Aaron Hernandez, was "awed" by the New England Patriots star and "grateful to be noticed" when he sent Hernandez a rifle and two handguns a month before Odin Lloyd's murder. Hernandez pleaded guilty to weapons charges in connection to his namesake's murder case.

A 33-year-old man named Joel Parker was arrested in Florida for throwing a Snickers bar at a bus driver's head after threatening him and being disruptive during the ride. The driver was not injured, but Parker was charged with battery and issued a trespass warning.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has discussed pre-season plans with Saido Berahino, indicating the striker will remain at the club beyond the summer transfer window. Berahino, who has expressed a desire to play in the Champions League, is likely to be included in England's under-21 squad for the upcoming European Championships. Pulis praised Berahino's performance and commitment, suggesting he would not be influenced by agents.

Giovanni Lo Porto, a Sicilian man who worked on reconstruction projects in Pakistan after deadly flooding, was abducted by four armed men in 2012 and later killed by a U.S. drone strike. He was a project manager for the German aid organization Welthungerlife, working on clean water and sanitation projects in Pakistan. Lo Porto was a popular student and passionate humanitarian who dedicated his life to helping others, particularly in Asia and Pakistan.

A photographer captured an image of hundreds of sharks near a beach in south Florida, prompting speculation that the sharks were Blacktips or Spinners migrating to breed. The incident has been shared more than 2,000 times on social media.

An 11-year-old retired K-9 officer named Zeus, a German Shepherd who worked with the Ridgefield Police Department for eight years as a K-9 officer, was honored in a grand procession before he was put down due to a severe degenerative hip disorder and declining health. The tribute was held on Wednesday, and Zeus took his last ride in a cop patrol car during the procession. The police department wrote an emotional message about Zeus, expressing their deep love and respect for him. Zeus was being taken to Ridgefield Veterinary Clinic where he was to be euthanized. The vehicles traveled from the police headquarters and ended at the veterinary hospital. The grand procession was held in Ridgefield, Connecticut, and residents lined the streets to watch.

Since Operation Yewtree, the number of child sex abuse reports has surged by more than 60%, with thousands of new cases filed in 2014. Despite a 9% drop in arrests, critics accuse the Government of failing to protect victims. The South Yorkshire force saw a 577% increase in reported cases, with 501 investigations in 2014. The NSPCC helpline has seen a 81% increase in calls about sexual abuse since the operation's launch.

Iceland has become a popular filming location for TV series and Hollywood blockbusters, with Thingvellir National Park and Svartalfheim providing stunning settings for Game of Thrones and Thor: The Dark World, respectively. The country's dramatic landscapes, including the Svinafellsjokull glacier and Dettifoss waterfall, have been used in Interstellar and Prometheus, respectively. The article highlights the unique filming locations in Iceland, including Thingvellir National Park, Svartalfheim, Reykjanes Peninsula, Skaftafell National Park, and Vatnajokull glacier, which have been featured in various blockbuster films.

A 100-year-old mechanic’s garage in Sydney has sold for $1.2 million, with the proceeds expected to be used to convert the building into a home. The grey-fronted structure, built as a fire station in 1917, was used as a mechanic’s garage for three generations before being converted into a three-bedroom, four-storey house. The property is located in Paddington, Sydney's inner city, offering a five-star location with easy access to Oxford Street and Bondi Beach.

Samantha Rawcliffe, a 40-year-old mother-of-two from Morecambe, was diagnosed with functional neurological disorder (FND) after losing control of her body and crashing her car. The rare condition, an umbrella term for a range of neurological symptoms that doctors cannot explain, has left her confined to her house, unable to walk, and reliant on a mobility scooter. She is now taking 32 different drugs each day to manage her symptoms, including choking fits and tremors.

The sculptor of a controversial statue of Lucille Ball, dubbed "Scary Lucy," has admitted to being "disappointed" with the work and offered to fix it for free. The statue, based on a moment from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," has been called "monstrous" and "frightening" by some residents of Celoron, New York. The sculptor, Dave Poulin, pledged to create a new statue that would be "beautiful and charming" and cost an estimated $8,000 to $10,000 to recast.

Bayern Munich's versatile left-back David Alaba will miss the rest of the season after being ruled out for around seven weeks with a torn knee ligament. Alaba, who was out for three months earlier this season, was injured while playing for Austria against Bosnia. He is set to start rehabilitation work in about a month and will miss the closing stages of the season. Bayern Munich is top of the Bundesliga and through to the Champions League quarter-finals.

Beatrice Nokes, the daughter of two solicitors and a detective, appeared in court on charges of running an upmarket prostitution ring with her father and a police officer. Nokes faces three charges of inciting prostitution and seven more related to controlling prostitution and misconduct. The case involves grooming young women and operating the ring from properties in London.

Diana Doyle, a whistleblower, revealed that a firm linked to the sale of NHS patient data is offering details of eating disorder sufferers, stress, hair loss, dandruff, impotence, snoring, dieters, and those with plastic surgery for just 12p a head. The firm, Sequester, is also offering to supply names of those who have had plastic surgery, smoke, wear glasses or contact lenses, have sensitive teeth, and have wills or health insurance. The revelations prompted probes by the Information Commissioner's Office and the Direct Marketing Commission, and a third investigation by the General Pharmaceutical Council into Pharmacy2U, the UK's biggest online pharmacy.

Jordan Spieth, 21, won the 2017 Masters golf tournament, becoming the second-youngest champion behind Tiger Woods. He equaled Tiger's record of 18 under par and led from start to finish. Spieth's 14-year-old sister, Ellie, who is autistic, provided him with perspective and support. Spieth described the reality of winning as "even better" than his dreams. He wore the green jacket for the first time and said he hoped to be finishing his final Masters appearance in 50 years.

Dick Advocaat, 67, will not underestimate the significance of the Old Firm derby against Newcastle, unlike his 1998 mistake with Celtic. Advocaat takes charge of Sunderland for the first time on home soil, with North-East rivals Newcastle as the visitors. Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe trains with his team-mates ahead of the game. Advocaat admits he did not realise the significance of the Old Firm fixture in 1998, leading to a humiliating loss. He recalls: 'To be honest, I did not realise at that moment it was so huge. 'We lost that game and I remember saying in the press conference when they were really upset, 'It is no problem for me because it is just one of 38 games and we will not lose any more.' 'I would not say that anymore! But we became champions that year, six points ahead of Celtic, and won the treble.' Advocaat, though, does

A young woman, Belinda Bartholomew, claims she was racially abused and called a "f***ing c***" by a butcher at a Bondi shop when she tried to change her chicken selection for a Game of Thrones-themed dinner. The butcher denies the claims, saying she was the one being rude.

Freddo Frog, a popular children's chocolate, has been reduced in size by 20% from 15g to 12g, despite keeping the price the same. This change was spotted by a shop owner who stocks the treats. Cadbury's spokesman explains the decision is due to manufacturing cost increases they can no longer absorb. The company recommends the Freddo Frogs be sold for $4.99, which won't increase or decrease. Thousands of chocolate fans expressed anger and disappointment, with some accusing Cadbury of being greedy and unaffordable.

Hillary Clinton's campaign-in-waiting met in Brooklyn on Saturday, a day before officially announcing her presidential bid. Robby Mook, her soon-to-be campaign manager, distributed a "values statement" outlining the campaign's goals and strategies. The document mentions issues that plagued Clinton's 2008 campaign, emphasizing humility, discipline, and unity. The campaign aims to avoid mistakes and focus on winning in states, with a goal of giving every family and business a path to prosperity. Clinton plans to launch her campaign through a video message on social media shortly after her announcement.

A 29-year-old woman, Kyli Wilfson, revealed her 18-month-long battle with chronic pancreatitis, a rare condition that left her unable to eat anything for a year and a half despite feeling extremely hungry. Initially misdiagnosed as acute pancreatitis, she was eventually diagnosed with chronic pancreatitis, which only worsened over time. Kyli lost 30 pounds and had to rely on a feeding tube due to the disease's permanent damage. Her fiancé, Dustin Wood, felt bad eating in front of her.

Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon poses with a sceptical face in this meme, referencing Labour leader Ed Miliband's direct message to Prime Minister David Cameron. The images show Labour leader Ed Miliband superimposed over London rapper Plan B, and Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg superimposed over Christopher Steed and Stephen Webb from Channel 4 series Gogglebox. The images were inspired by a debate where Labour leader Ed Miliband appeared with the Scottish National Party leader Nicola Sturgeon, Ukip's Nigel Farage, Green leader Natalie Bennett, and Plaid Cymru's Leanne Wood, but Prime Minister David Cameron and his deputy Nick Clegg stayed away.

Amir Khan, the British boxer, is set to face Manny Pacquiao in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, after Mayweather declined the fight. Khan, who has been waiting for Mayweather for two years, is now set to fight Pacquiao, who is preparing to face Mayweather on May 2. The fight could take place in November or December in Abu Dhabi, and Khan hopes to fight in the Middle East.

A tiny two-bedroom home in Islington, London, priced at £750,000, has sold for £750,000, despite being only 5ft wide in some areas and 8ft 8in wide at its widest. The narrow house, with a 'galley kitchen' and a garden, has attracted a lot of interest and is now under offer. The home, which was put on the market with Foxtons for £750,000, is described as a 'stylish two bedroom period house' with characterful touches and a pretty rear garden. The buyer will have to pay £27,000 in stamp duty, the same as a second-hand narrow boat which is 50ft long.

Nicola Sturgeon, the leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP), is launching an extraordinary bid to lead the UK, unveiling a manifesto that includes policies tailored for a power-sharing deal with Labour. Several of her election pledges overlap with Labour policy, such as slashing tuition fees in England and rolling back competition in the English NHS. The SNP aims to build a 'progressive alliance' for people 'right across the UK' and is positioning itself as a major force in the upcoming election, with the party on course for a landslide victory, potentially triggering constitutional turmoil.

Celtic won the Glasgow Cup for the fourth time in eight seasons, defeating Rangers 2-0, with Josh Kerr scoring twice. The match was played behind closed doors due to fan trouble, and Rangers struggled to create chances.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis, who previously played for Crystal Palace, insisted he will never change his traditional attire of cap, track suit, and white trainers, even though his side won 2-0 against his former club. Pulis, who has led West Brom to 36 points and virtually guaranteed their Premier League safety, will continue to wear his customary attire at every match.

Jameela Jamil, a 29-year-old television presenter and former model, spent £3,000 on having all her amalgam fillings removed and replaced with white fillings after experiencing health problems for nearly seven years. She thought she had lupus, but tests revealed high levels of mercury, which she believed was caused by the amalgam fillings. After removing the fillings, her mercury levels returned to normal, and she was diagnosed with mercury poisoning. The dental association and EU Commission's Scientific Committee concluded there was no risk from amalgam fillings.

Suge Knight, the co-creator of Death Row Records, is awaiting trial for murder and attempted murder in Los Angeles Superior Court. Despite being refused an appeal to have his bail reduced from $10 million to $5 million, Knight believes his close friend, the undefeated professional boxer Floyd Mayweather, will bail him out when he wins on Saturday. Mayweather, worth $420 million, is set to land a record pay check after going head-to-head with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday. Knight's attorney, Matthew Fletcher, is confident that Mayweather will come to his aid and bail him out.

In an interview with Puss Puss magazine, stylish chef Gizzi Erskine reveals that her feline, Kimchi, has a discerning palate and loves crunchy human food, such as poppadoms and tortilla chips. The cat, described as a British shorthair, is known for stealing food from her plate and prefers crunchy treats over soft ones. Kimchi is also a fan of taramasalata, which Erskine considers her "death row dish." The article highlights the luxurious cat treats Kimchi enjoys, including caviar, salmon roe, and a two-tiered cake covered in cat treats.

Martin Springall, the father of a little girl who appeared in a photograph of a mysterious pair of boots, has no idea what the boots could be. The photograph, taken in Japan in 2014, sparked debate online about the boots' origin and meaning. Springall insists the boots were not Photoshopped and that he and his daughter were the only ones in the area.

The UK government plans to introduce new immigration policies that will force foreign workers to pay an average of £22,000 in tax before they can claim benefits, including those from the EU. The Home Secretary Theresa May announced the plans, which include banning EU migrants from receiving state support for four years and deporting those who do not find employment within six months. The crackdown is aimed at limiting the appeal of coming to Britain from poorer parts of the EU and is part of the government's effort to negotiate a new deal with Europe, including curbing access to benefits.

A severely disabled boy, Cody Neatis, has been sleeping on a mattress on the floor in a hospital since last Thursday due to a lack of a suitable bed for him. Cody, who has Down's syndrome, epilepsy, autism, and is fed by a tube, has been without a hospital bed because staff do not have the special cot needed to keep him safe in his sleep. His mother, Lynne Neatis, 48, has had to sleep with Cody for the past week, fearing he will injure himself or pull out his oxygen. The hospital does not have the specialist high-sided cot needed for Cody and other disabled children. Lynne Neatis is demanding answers from the local health trust as she claims she has waited two years for the bed.

Ahead of the Masters golf tournament, Derek Lawrenson reports on the excitement and challenges faced by players, including Rory McIlroy's quest for a career Grand Slam and Tiger Woods' return to the tournament with his children. Henrik Stenson, recovering from flu, is expected to impress, while Tiger Woods' return to the traditional par-three tournament is met with skepticism. The 16th hole practice round tradition is highlighted, with no player matching Vijay Singh and Martin Kaymer's feats of skipping their balls across the water.

Juventus have ruled out a move for Manchester United loan star Radamel Falcao after claiming the Colombia striker's wages are 'beyond their means'. Falcao has endured a difficult period at Old Trafford after arriving in an expensive loan deal from Monaco last summer. Juventus general manager Beppe Marotta has claimed that Falcao wanted to come to Turin last summer but the Serie A champions have now taken themselves out of the race to sign him.

David Cameron plans to sell Lloyds Bank shares worth £4 billion if he wins the election, offering them at a discount and encouraging long-term shareholders to hold onto their shares. This is the largest privatisation since the Thatcher era, with a £20 billion bailout by Gordon Brown's government. The sale is part of a Conservative policy to hark back to the 1980s, with a loyalty bonus of one free share for every ten held for at least a year. The sale of Lloyds shares would be the biggest privatisation since the 1980s when Mrs Thatcher's government sold £3.9 billion of BT shares and £5.6 billion of British Gas shares.

Scientists have warned that living near congested roads with high levels of air pollution can cause 'silent strokes' that increase the risk of dementia. The microscopic particles, mostly from traffic fumes and factory emissions, alter the structure of the brain and are linked to 29,000 deaths in Britain annually. Researchers found evidence that living near congested roads or polluted areas can lead to 'silent strokes' causing brain shrinkage and other damage.

Jessica Ainscough, a 30-year-old wellness warrior who died from a rare and aggressive form of cancer, wrote an emotional letter to her followers revealing she was undergoing radiation treatment in her final weeks. She had previously rejected chemotherapy and radiation, opting for controversial Gerson Therapy, which lacks scientific support. After discussions with experts, Ainscough began a course of targeted radiation in her final weeks, which was among the toughest for her partner, Tallon Pamenter. The radiation successfully shrunk the tumour but complications arose, leading to her death. Ainscough's partner expressed her courage and grace, and the couple's love was deeply affected by her passing.

Ten people, including four children, were involved in a multi-vehicle crash on the Brisbane Valley Highway in Brisbane's west on Wednesday afternoon. Three vehicles collided, resulting in chest and shoulder injuries for a 40-year-old man and a 5-year-old boy, and arm and abdominal pain for a 27-year-old woman and a 6-year-old girl. The affected stretch of the highway was closed off with diversions in place.

Jason McDonald, a 34-year-old volunteer at the Colorado Gator Farm, walked a thin slackline rope over a pool containing more than 50 hungry alligators, including some measuring up to ten feet in length. McDonald, who has been involved with alligators for over ten years and has taken handling classes, thought this would be an interesting new way of interacting with the fearsome creatures. The gators were surprisingly ok with the slackline, and McDonald plans to take his hobby further by walking over Elvis or Morris, his two biggest gators on the farm.

The son of a Syrian imam who was shot dead on a London street may have met his father's killer just days before the murder. Abdul Hadi Arwani, an opponent of Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad, had visited the area where he was killed with his son days before his death. Arwani, 48, was shot and killed in his car on a quiet street in North West London after being called there last Tuesday, apparently to provide a quote for building work. The man, who has not been otherwise identified, also told the imam that there was no need for his son to accompany him again when he did come back. The counter-terrorism unit is looking into whether the man was a hired killer who postponed the hit because Arwani was not alone.

Hong Kong's Jenny's cookies, a tin of butter cookies priced at $9, have become a popular item, with tourists and locals lining up for hours to purchase them. The cookies have sparked a black market, with bakeries making and selling knockoffs, and the original store warning against buying "fake" cookies. The frenzy has spread to other parts of the world, with similar food manias occurring in other countries.

A mother-of-one, Kira Hollis, who was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder and battled depression and anorexia, has revealed how bodybuilding gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. At just 6st, she was deemed clinically underweight and was ordered by doctors to go to the gym to gain some weight. There, she turned her life around and is now a healthy 9. 5st personal trainer. Ms Hollis says bodybuilding changed her life and gave her the confidence to overcome her depression. She was also helped by the Cherry Orchard Clinic in Tamworth and medication from her doctor. Her story went viral after she uploaded a video online, which has now been more than two million times.

Lewis Ferguson, 18, survived a spectacular fall from Merrion Square during a race at Wincanton on Wednesday, causing him to hit the fence and perform a mid-air somersault. The incident, which was captured on video and has been viewed millions of times online, has made Ferguson an internet sensation. Despite the fall, Ferguson said he was undeterred from getting back in the saddle and expressed his desire to ride at the Cheltenham Festival and Aintree every year. The incident was described as the worst fall the race course clerk of the course Barry Johnson had ever seen.

Hillary Clinton launched her campaign in a unique and unconventional way, using a video, new logo, and a road trip to "rebrand" herself and reframe her message. Critics dismissed her efforts as "relentlessly, insultingly vapid" and "boring as s---," but marketing experts argue that her launch may have been more successful than initially thought. The campaign aims to flip Clinton's message from self-absorbed to empathetic, projecting a more confident, fresher, and forward-looking image. The campaign's success will be crucial in determining whether Clinton can reframe herself in voters' eyes.

More than 1,700 Chinese high school students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took an exam in their school's playground on Saturday, the first time the school allowed students to sit exams outdoors due to insufficient indoor space. The students organized the outdoor exam themselves, with a regular radio announcement instructing them to turn their chairs and desks to avoid being dazzled by the sun. The school reported that the outdoor exam could be a test of the students' organizing capacity and that many students believe it is a novel way to broaden their horizons and feel more relaxed.

Sportsmail has partnered with Gillette to offer a unique chance for one lucky reader to win a pair of Nike Magista Obra boots signed by Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart. The prize includes a new Gillette Fusion ProGlide razor with Flexball technology and a shave gel. The competition closes on April 19.

Kecil, a baby orangutan, was rejected by his natural mother and a surrogate mother, but was adopted by Maggie, an experienced surrogate mother at Chicago's Brookfield Zoo. Maggie proved her parenting skills by raising Kecil for the past 10 months, and the two now have an inseparable bond. Kecil, who had to be moved from his birthplace at Toledo zoo 14 months ago after his natural mother failed to bond with him properly, will have his first public outing this weekend in two hours slots between 10am and midday, allowing him to nap in the afternoons.

A 61-year-old woman died suddenly and was eaten by her pet dogs after lying undiscovered for days. The dogs, initially thought to have tried to wake her before becoming desperate for food, ate parts of her vital organs. The most likely cause of death was an accidental overdose of medication, but the exact cause was not determined due to the dogs' consumption of her organs. The incident occurred after the woman collapsed and died following an accidental overdose of medication.

France's handball star Nikola Karabatic, along with his brother Luka, faces fraud charges over their alleged involvement in an illegal betting case. Karabatic, a multiple world and Olympic gold medalist, was banned by the French league for betting on a match in which his Montpellier club lost to a struggling team. He is currently playing for Barcelona in the Spanish league. The trial is expected to take place within months, with Karabatic facing up to five years in prison and a fine.

A gang of six men, including Ahmed Hassan-Sule, 21, and Mohamed Saleh, 22, were convicted of a string of sexual offenses against teenage girls in Banbury, Oxfordshire, from 2009 to 2014. The offenses ranged from inciting sexual activity with a child to rape. Hassan-Sule and Saleh were sentenced to nine and four years in jail, respectively. The girls, aged between 13 and 16, were targeted at under-18s parties organized by Hassan-Sule. The judge criticized the men for using their football club's charity events to gain popularity among young people and exploiting their emotional immaturity. The case highlights the importance of reporting sexual offenses and the bravery of the victims in coming forward.

Former New England Patriots star Aaron Hernandez faces three more trials, including a murder trial in which he is accused of killing two men and wounding another person near a Boston nightclub in July 2012. Hernandez pleaded not guilty at his arraignment.

The Emirates Airline has signed a £30 million three-year deal to sponsor the FA Cup, rebranding it as the Emirates FA Cup. This deal, along with existing sponsorship deals with Arsenal, AC Milan, and Hamburg, adds to Emirates' portfolio of sporting sponsorships.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic champion, is set to compete in his fifth Olympics in Rio next year, but he won't be swimming at the world championships in Russia this summer. He has been banned from the last major international meet before the Rio Olympics due to a second drunken driving arrest. Phelps, who is 29 years old, has been through a difficult time, including a six-month suspension and treatment for alcohol addiction.

Gareth Bale is a huge doubt for Real Madrid's Champions League quarter-final second leg match against Atletico Madrid with a calf injury. Bale limped off during Real's 3-1 home victory over Malaga on Saturday. Los Blancos are also without Croatian midfielder Luka Modric, who suffered a knee ligament strain and is expected to be unavailable for six weeks. Real coach Carlo Ancelotti hopes to have striker Karim Benzema fit for the match after the Frenchman missed Saturday's encounter with a knee injury.

Scientists warn that older people are more susceptible to emotions when making decisions over their retirement, particularly during financial crises. A study found that more than 50% of pensioners panicked and sold investments during the 2007-2008 global financial crisis, resulting in a significant loss of wealth. The study, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, analyzed 1,204 retired people with investments between 2006 and 2008. It revealed that retirees with better-than-average ability to solve logic problems were less likely to make misjudgments in the investment market based on their emotions. The study also found that lower cognitive ability in old age can reduce an investor's ability to control emotional responses to a loss. Under reforms announced by Chancellor George Osborne, anyone turning 55 who isn't in a final salary scheme will soon be allowed to dip into their pension and take the income they need, under the biggest shake-up of pensions for almost a

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini should be given more time to turn around the club's fortunes, according to Stuart Pearce, who believes the team is at a level where they need to be in the Champions League and win the Premier League. Pearce, who has experience managing the club, suggests Pellegrini should stay in place despite the team's recent poor form, which he attributes to the fading influence of Yaya Toure.

Manchester United's stars, including Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera, and Robin van Persie, are training in the sunshine ahead of their Premier League derby against Manchester City on Sunday. Manchester United, currently in fourth place, hopes to win the match to move four points clear of City in the league standings.

Fiorentina lost 1-0 to Verona, leaving them nine points behind third-placed AS Roma. Fiorentina's coach, Vincenzo Montella, said his team paid dearly for failing to turn their domination into goals. Fiorentina is now in sixth place on 49 points, one place and a point behind Sampdoria who occupy the final Europa League qualifying spot.

Miley Cyrus, 22, attended the 30th Annual Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame Induction Ceremony in Cleveland, Ohio, where she posed for a social media snap with somewhat bushy underarm hair. This sparked controversy, with some users advising her to shave, while others defended her choice. Cyrus is known for her controversial sartorial choices, and her armpit hair caused a stir on social media.

Barcelona's Lionel Messi, Neymar, and Luis Suarez have scored 102 goals in all competitions this season, taking them five points clear in La Liga. Messi has 49 goals, Neymar has 32, and Suarez has 21. The trio's dominance is highlighted by their 6-0 victory over Getafe, with Messi scoring twice and Suarez claiming two goals. Barcelona's emphatic win boosts their Liga goal difference to +78, putting pressure on Real Madrid ahead of their match with Almeria.

Andrea McVeigh, 44, was left scarred for life after being knocked down by a cyclist who fled the scene. The incident occurred in Bermondsey, south London, on April 14. McVeigh suffered two three-inch gashes to her forehead and other facial and hand injuries. CCTV footage of the cyclist was issued by the Met Police, who are now appealing for his arrest. McVeigh is currently off work sick and has two black eyes, a swollen nose, stitches, and a feeling of being scared to go out onto the street.

Paul Gregory, 51, of Bedford, was fined £795 for having a blue badge, claiming he could only walk 200 metres, when in fact he was a keen walker. He was exposed when Bedford Borough Council staff noticed a newspaper report about his exploits on a 191-mile hike. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by misrepresenting his physical abilities and was ordered to carry out 150 hours of unpaid work and pay a £60 victim surcharge.

Apple has filed a patent for a new way to unlock its devices using a user's face. The patent details a system that would automatically unlock the device if the scanned face matches a previously taken photo. The system would track the movement of the phone to determine whether it is being used or placed flat on a table. The patent was filed by Apple in March 2011 and awarded earlier this week.

Elizabeth Sedway, 51, a cancer patient from California, was ejected from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to California because she lacked a doctor's note clearing her to fly. Her husband and two sons were also removed from the plane. The incident sparked outrage and led to a video of the family being kicked off the flight being shared nearly 10,000 times.

Three people were taken to hospital after a head-on collision between a vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a modern Toyota Kluger on Easter Sunday night in Frenchs Forest, Sydney. The Jaguar, worth over $120,000, was completely written off. No one was injured, but all three adults involved were hospitalized for precaution. Police are investigating the incident. The Jaguar is considered a rare and valuable classic car. The crash occurred on Warringah Road.

Google has set up a team to boost the lifespan of phones, tablets, and electric cars, with sources claiming the team is working on flexible and wearable batteries. The team, led by Dr. Ramesh Bhardwaj, has been working on solid-state, thin-film batteries since 2012. Google has been collaborating with experts at AllCell Technologies to develop batteries that function at subfreezing temperatures, which is vital for its Project Loon balloons. The company has been working on similar projects since 2012.

The 223ft Explorer is a luxury superyacht designed by British yacht designer Tony Castro, featuring a helipad, infinity pool, and space for 12 guests. It can carry a helicopter, twin limousines, a submarine, jetskis, paddleboards, and inflatables. The yacht costs approximately 40 million euros to build, making it expensive to purchase. The layout includes a large carrying capacity for toys and tenders, and ample space for 15 crew. The yacht is described as a sumptuous retreat at sea, with special sundecks and amenities for guests.
Ed Miliband, Labour leader, announced plans to cap rents despite expert warnings that they will backfire, leading to more tenants being evicted and investment in new housing being slashed.

A 10-year-old Huddersfield Town fan who said he hopes Arsenal wins has been removed from his role as a mascot for Reading in the FA Cup semi-final against Arsenal. The young supporter was offered the chance to be a mascot for England instead.

A giant supervoid 1.8 billion light-years across may be responsible for a mysterious 'Cold Spot' in the universe, according to astronomers seeking to understand the cause of this larger-than-expected cold area. If confirmed, the supervoid would be the largest single structure ever found by humanity. The supervoid appears to be 'roughly spherical' and may contain a 'significant substructure' at its centre. The supervoid is thought to be causing a 'less-dense' region of the universe, with the Cold Spot region containing about 20% less matter than other regions of the universe. The supervoid is 1.8 billion light-years across and would be the biggest object ever found. Some 'exotic physics' is also needed to explain what's happening.

The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, will display Abraham Lincoln's chair shot in Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C. on April 15 as part of its observance of the assassination's 150th anniversary. The chair, which has a dark stain on the back believed to be blood from the shooting, will be removed from its enclosure to be displayed in an open plaza. The chair has been part of the museum since its founding 85 years ago and was originally housed in the Logan County Courthouse.

Jake Boys, a 19-year-old vlogger from Hailsham, England, surprised his girlfriend Emily Canham by booking tickets for One Direction to perform in Cardiff. However, he mistakenly booked plane tickets to the Republic of Ireland instead of Wales, where the concert was actually taking place. The couple is now planning to buy new train tickets to Cardiff for the band's show in June.

A Romanian company has unveiled the Roboscan 2M Aeria, a mobile X-ray scanner that can detect contraband, bombs, and weapons on airplanes. The device, which is the world's first "airplane scanner," uses a cone of radiation to scan planes and can detect objects inside. While the radiation emitted is not safe for humans, the company believes it could become a vital tool in aircraft safety. The Roboscan 2M Aeria is being developed by MB Telecom and costs €3 million. It can scan planes from small private jets to medium-sized commercial airplanes and can be used to detect weapons and other contraband in low-security airports. The device can scan an entire plane in about 20 minutes.

A 54-year-old convicted paedophile, Stephen Munden, has gone on the run after vanishing from a psychiatric unit. He was last seen leaving a hospital in Hampshire and is described as about 5ft 8ins tall, heavy, and with dark hair. Munden, who suffers from learning difficulties, may have shaved off his beard before leaving the hospital. He was detained under the Mental Health Act after sexually touching a three-year-old girl. A court heard he had admitted ten unrelated offences of possessing or attempting to possess indecent images of children. Munden is described as having a fanatical obsession with young girls. A manhunt is underway to find him.

Middlesbrough are top of the Championship with just four weeks remaining, holding a 7-point lead over second-placed Bournemouth. The league is highly competitive, with teams separated by just one point. Watford and Bournemouth are struggling, while Norwich is in contention. Jonathan Woodgate, Middlesbrough's captain, is expected to play through a toe injury. The promotion race is tight, with a win for Watford and Bournemouth could change the top two.

The latest hair trend is grey hair, with women sharing images on social media under the hashtag #grannyhair. The trend has gained popularity on platforms like Instagram, with beauty models and self-proclaimed grey-haired Instagrammers posting images of their silver locks. The trend has been embraced by both men and women, with some viewing it as a feminist statement and others as a quirky fashion fad. The trend can be traced back to fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier's catwalk show at Paris Fashion Week earlier this month, which featured silver-haired models.

A couple from Bellefontaine, Ohio, who were struggling with chronic conditions and had no running water or electricity, died from self-inflicted carbon monoxide poisoning after their online fundraisers for help went ignored. The couple, Randy and Jodi Speidel, had been living without gas all winter and had limited food and scraps for their two cats. Their online campaign for $1,000 to help them was unsuccessful, and they were found dead in their bedroom with a pair of charcoal grills filled with smoldering coals. The couple had removed their cats to spare their lives, and their daughters, Randa and Kira, called them "the hardest-working people I know."

Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg vowed to continue as leader even if the party is reduced to fewer than 30 MPs, despite previous indications he would quit if the party is left out of power. He emphasized his commitment to serving the country and his party, despite the risks of losing the center ground and undoing past sacrifices. His comments came as Business Secretary Vince Cable expressed hope for a deal with the Conservatives.

A pensioner was saved from a badger by his Jack Russell dog, which dragged him back indoors. The badger was described as the size of a large pig with six-inch teeth. The National Farmers' Union advises residents to protect their property from badgers by using badger-proof fencing and keeping bins covered.

Jose Mourinho watched Fulham Under 21s lose to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, while Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho chose Fulham's Motspur Park training ground to watch the match. Mourinho joked with Fulham goalkeeping coach Vic Bettinelli, whose son plays for the first team at Craven Cottage. Chelsea crashed out of the Champions League, but Mourinho's son is on student terms with Fulham. Chelsea are closing in on their first Premier League title since 2010, with six games to play and a win would bring the trophy back to Stamford Bridge.

A businessman was attacked with corrosive liquid in a doorstep acid attack in Cornwall, leaving him with life-changing injuries and a loss of vision. The attacker, Nicole Phillips, 45, from Hastings, has been charged with perverting the course of justice. The victim, Andreas Christopheros, 29, a property developer, is recovering at a hospital.

A Spanish town on the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route is warning pilgrims and other visitors to stop defecating along the famous path. The signs, which show a squatting figure defecating within a red circle with a diagonal line across it, have been erected in the municipality of Lastres. The signs are posted next to warnings that urge people not to litter. The pilgrimage attracts thousands of pilgrims every year, but there can be very few places to go when nature calls. The signs are found to be so amusing they have become an attraction, with pilgrims stopping to pose for photos with them.

A massive fire consumed a building that was once home to a strip club in Flint, Michigan, on Wednesday afternoon. The blaze took place at a building located on a Flint intersection, and started at about 1pm. Only the building itself and a few nearby power lines were affected. Local resident Terry Rauh told MLive a fire took place at the building once before. An investigation into what was behind the blaze continues.

A woman of Arab and Jewish descent who was strip-searched at a Detroit-area airport has reached a settlement in a lawsuit filed on her behalf. The federal government will give Shoshana Hebshi $40,000 as compensation for being humiliated on the 10th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks after armed agents forced her from a plane at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, made her undress during a search and held her for hours.

A plane crash landed at Hiroshima Airport in Japan, injuring 20 people. The plane, an Airbus A320, had crashed after missing the runway and skidded off the runway. The plane had set off from Incheon International Airport in Seoul, South Korea. Local media reported that the plane had overran the runway at 8pm local time. The plane had deployed evacuation slides and appeared to have a hard landing. The crash occurred two years after an Asiana Airlines flight crashed in San Francisco, leaving three teenagers dead and nearly 200 passengers injured.

Mark-Francis Vandelli, a wealthy reality TV star, has opened up his watch collection to the Evening Standard, showcasing 16 expensive timepieces. He revealed his favorite items and the history behind them, including a Bulgari Bulgari Chrono 42, a Cartier Tortue Collection Privée, and a Rolex yellow gold Oyster Perpetual. His most expensive watch is a Cartier white gold Moonphase, which he bought for £32,000 and has a sun or moon that moves depending on the hour of the day.

Actor Robert Hardy, 89, is selling his collection of antiques in a £100,000 auction after deciding to downsize his home. The collection includes a diorama of the Battle of Agincourt, a longbow made from yew with a mother-of-pearl handle, and a portrait of Hardy holding the bow. The auction, held by Dominic Winter in South Cerney, Gloucestershire, includes dozens of books, furniture, swords, flintlock rifles, silverware, and crystal chandeliers.

A Brazilian man took a photo of a man standing on a yellow safety line on a train platform and posted it on Facebook, expressing his disapproval of the man's behavior. The image quickly went viral, with over 100, 000 views in 24 hours. The man, Nelson Felippe, works at the Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro and is a Catholic. He believes that people should be protected from seeing such behavior in public, and that children will think it's normal to wait on the yellow line. Felippe's post has received thousands of comments, with users praising his witty way of exposing homophobia.

A young English cricket fan who wrote a letter to Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricket player, almost 20 years ago, has shared the Australian cricket great's response in the wake of his death. The letter, written by Jonathan Stevenson, a director at LiveWire Sport, was dated September 27, 1996, and included a full sheet of notes about spin bowling for left-hand bowlers. Richie Benaud, who enjoyed a remarkable Test career as a wily leg-spin bowler and middle-order batsman, responded to Stevenson's letter, offering advice on left-handed leg spin. The letter, signed by Benaud, included tips on different deliveries and gave pointers as to how they should be delivered.

Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg predicts that virtual reality will play a key role in the future of travel, allowing users to experience new environments and locations without the need for physical travel. Zuckerberg's views are supported by Facebook's recent purchase of virtual reality headset maker Oculus and the company's promise to support virtual reality on its newsfeed. Marriott hotels have also trialled Oculus Rift on a tour of hotels across America, allowing guests to sample different holiday destinations.

A 22-year-old woman in China was diagnosed with bone cancer and admitted to the hospital, but her boyfriend arranged for her to have wedding photographs taken. The couple met a year ago and fell in love, with the photographer taking the photos even though the woman is bedridden due to her condition.

A 34-year-old man, Blaine Boudreaux, was charged with intoxication manslaughter, intoxicated assault, and failure to stop and render aid involving death in connection to three separate DUI collisions that took place within three hours in Houston. Boudreaux, who also has an extensive DUI record in his native Louisiana, was allegedly drunk when he ran a red light on Lockwood Drive at around 6:30pm and slammed his Dodge pickup truck into a Honda Civic. The boy's mother, Cynthia, was hospitalized with a punctured lung and broken bones.

Microsoft has launched a pilot program to hire people with autism for full-time positions within the company. The positions will be based at its Redmond campus in Washington and will be run in partnership with Specialisterne, a Danish nonprofit that helps train people with autism for careers in IT. The program aims to expand opportunity and represent customers. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was forced to apologize for saying that women don't need to ask for a raise and should just trust the system to pay them well.

Two deputies involved in the fatal attempt to arrest Eric Harris in Tulsa, Oklahoma, have been reassigned because of threats against them and their families, Sheriff Stanley Glanz said Monday in a news conference. The deputies were trying to arrest Harris when Reserve Deputy Robert Bates shot him.

A couple who married in their teens and suffer from cystic fibrosis are in a race against time as the young wife waits for a life-saving lung transplant. Katie Prager, 24, was diagnosed with an infection in her lungs called Burkholderia Cepacia and is desperately in need of a transplant as doctors predicted she would not live a year without new lungs. Her husband Dalton, 23, pleaded for help, saying that his insurance company, Kentucky Medicaid, will not pay for the out-of-state treatment she needs at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.

The Sleep Cycle app has gathered data from over two million users aged 18 to 55 in 47 countries, revealing that the world sleeps the least on Mondays in South Africa, with Americans waking up at 7am and being in the worst mood all week. The best sleep quality occurs on Wednesdays, with China recording the highest sleep quality in the world that night. The data also shows that people in Finland get the most hours of sleep on Saturdays, with an average of eight hours and two minutes, while people in Japan get an average of just six hours and nine minutes sleep. The best sleep quality worldwide occurs on a Wednesday night, with China recording the highest sleep quality in the world that night.

Frida Kahlo's unpublished love letters to Jose Bartoli, a Catalan artist, are expected to fetch upwards of $120,000 when they go up for auction at Doyle New York on April 15. The letters, written between 1946 and 1949, were saved by Jose until his death in 1995 and comprise more than 100 pages. The letters, which Frida signed as 'Sonja', shed light on her important paintings, an unknown pregnancy, and her relationship with Diego Rivera.

Trade union leader Len McCluskey, known for his militant stance, is popular with Labour activists but is a potent, sinister force in British politics seeking to use his financial and organizational muscle to drag Britain back to the dark days of the 1970s. His influence on Labour candidates is chilling, and his socialist revolution is potentially disastrous for the governance of this country.

A zookeeper placed a GoPro camera at the bottom of water troughs to capture the different perspectives of animals drinking. The footage shows a variety of unique drinking methods, from a rhino almost kissing the surface of the water to a lemur delicately licking it. The zookeeper filmed the animals for a total of 30 hours and cut the final footage down to four minutes. The animals were initially skeptical about the foreign object in their troughs, but eventually got used to the camera's presence and drank freely. The zookeeper anticipated a range of reactions from the animals and ensured that the camera was secure before the experiment.
A YouGov poll found that only 25% of voters think David Cameron is hungriest to win the election, compared to 43% who believe Ed Miliband is most up for the fight.

A man charged with assassinating Russian opposition leader Boris Nemstov has told a court he was beaten and pressured into confessing to the murder. Zaur Dadaev is accused of being involved in the shooting of the politician in Moscow on February 27, along with four other Chechen men. Now Russian news agencies have quoted him as telling the court that he had been abducted, beaten and pressured into confessing to Nemstov's murder. Dadaev is one of five Chechen men who have been accused of killing the opposition leader. Nemstov was shot in the back four times on a bridge close to the Kremlin in February, sparking a huge protest march in Moscow.

A 4-month-old baby boy named Sonit Awal was pulled from the rubble of a Nepal earthquake that killed more than 5,000 people. His father, Shyam Awal, frantically searched for him amid the debris for 22 hours before the soldiers found him. Sonit's face was exposed during the rescue, but he was uninjured. The rescue provides hope to a country that has experienced so much loss.

A Church of Scientology-backed organization is facing a land use battle over its plans to turn a patch of secluded land near the presidential retreat Camp David into a drug rehab center. Narcocon, a drug rehab network affiliated with the Church of Scientology, is trying to prove that the property has historic significance so that they can build a center for twelve patients. The organization's website prominently features the religion's founder L. Ron Hubbard, and its methods include spending up to five hours a day in a sauna for 30 days straight and mega doses of the vitamin Niacin. The property is currently classified for resource conservation and does not permit any medical purpose, according to the zoning laws.

The article discusses the aftermath of the U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan, focusing on the challenges faced by expatriates and locals in Kabul. Five men who once spoke English fluently due to their work with NATO have been fired and blacklisted, leading to isolation and fear of retaliation. They sleep in market stalls and avoid traveling to see their families. The city has transformed, with neighborhoods emptying out and new residents reclaiming streets. The article highlights the ongoing impact of the U.S. war on Afghanistan and the challenges faced by those who have adapted to the new reality.

Two US Navy SEALs died and another was critically injured while training in a pool at a Virginia military base, a Navy spokesman said. The incident occurred on Friday at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek-Fort Story. The names of the SEALS were withheld pending notification of next of kin. Both were assigned to Naval Special Warfare Group Two, which contains SEAL teams. The sailors were swimming in lap lanes and were not wearing gear at the time. One was pronounced dead, and the second is listed in critical condition. Capt Pete Vasely, Commander, Naval Special Warfare Group TWO, said the incident is ongoing and the families and friends of the fallen SEALs are being supported.

NBC, the broadcasting giant, has transported their entire Premier League production from their HQ in Stamford, Connecticut, to England for this weekend's round of matches. This move is expected to increase US interest in the English Premier League, with some 13 million Americans watching at least one top-flight English game live in 2012-13 and 32 million in 2013-14. The move comes as NBC hosts Rebecca Lowe, Robbie Earle, and Kyle Martino, along with pitchside analysts Lee Dixon and Robbie Mustoe, prepare to cover the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on Sunday and the Liverpool-Newcastle match on Monday.

Ed Miliband will do "more damage to the country than he did to his brother," Boris Johnson said on the Andrew Marr Show, launching a furious personal assault on his rival. The London Mayor accused Miliband of "stabbing the country in the back" by doing a deal with the SNP to get into power.

A prisoner in Oregon was slapped with an extra 30 days behind bars for dropping his trousers and flashing a judge during a court hearing. The judge sentenced him to an extra 30 days in jail for contempt of court.

McLaren's Formula One team has improved their performance significantly since their last race in Malaysia, according to team driver Jenson Button. Button believes the team is now in a position to challenge for the championship, with the team's new Honda power unit showing promising results. Despite the team's progress, Button acknowledges that there is still a long way to go and that the team needs to improve their downforce and power unit performance.

A hospital in Western Australia was found to have blood and bone fragments on supposedly sanitised medical instruments, leading to the hospital being stripped of its medical service provider Serco and fined $60,000. The incident has damaged the hospital's public image and generated a loss of morale within its workforce.

Becca Litchfield and her partner Dale, who had given up their dream wedding to pay for fertility treatment, have welcomed twins after winning a wedding competition. The couple, who had attempted two rounds of in vitro fertilization, were overjoyed when they discovered they were pregnant.

A family-friendly coffee shop in Omaha, Nebraska, had its Facebook page hacked and flooded with pornography after an employee clicked on a malicious link in an email. The hack lasted for almost 24 hours, and the page was replaced with adult cartoons similar to those posted on other major brands. The company offered an apology and removed the inappropriate content, but it was not until a day later that the company was able to regain control of the account.

A young Shibu Inu puppy at an American Kennel Club center in the US caused a commotion by barking at a young husky dog. The video shows the two dogs engaging in a playful conversation, with the Shibu Inu attempting to bark at the husky. People in the video laugh and mimic the dogs' actions, while a staff member attempts to calm the puppy. The video concludes with the husky losing interest and the Shibu Inu settling down.

Liam Plunkett, an experienced English fast bowler, is eager to prove himself in the West Indies Test series against the West Indies. He aims to use his pace to lead England to victory and has recovered from a minor ankle injury. Plunkett is competing for a place in the England Test side with Chris Jordan and Mark Wood, who are both familiar with the West Indies' conditions. He relishes the challenge of roughing up the batsmen and feels confident in his ability to bowl well in practice and warm-up games to earn his place in the team.

Paul Smith, a boxer from Liverpool, is set to face Andre Ward in a unification fight for the WBA super-middleweight title. The bout is seen as a warm-up for a potential rematch with Carl Froch. Ward, ranked among the top five pound-for-pound boxers, is the ideal opponent for Smith, who is not fighting for a title. The WBA has ordered their two super-middleweight champions, Ward and Froch, to meet in a unification fight. Froch is turning his attention to his other ambition, a first appearance on the Las Vegas Strip, against the namesake son of Mexican legend Julio Cesar Chavez.

Tyrus Byrd, the first African American mayor of Parma, Missouri, was sworn in last week but the majority of the city's police officers, city attorney, clerk, and water treatment supervisor resigned after her election. The outgoing mayor, Randall Ramsey, has no idea why the employees quit, citing 'safety concerns'. The town has suffered a surge in crime, and residents believe the departure of city employees is not related to the election.

Manchester City midfielder Yaya Toure will not be forced out of the club, but the team is set to make him available this summer. The Ivorian has played a major role during City's recent trophy-laden period and remains fully committed to the cause. Inter Milan is interested in the 31-year-old, but given his huge wages, there are some doubts over whether they would be able to afford it. City will resist any attempt by Valencia to pull out of a £24million deal for Alvaro Negredo to fund a move for Radamel Falcao.

A new study claims that more than two-thirds of people taking antidepressants may not actually have depression. The study, published in the Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, found that 69% of people taking SSRIs did not meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. The researchers concluded that antidepressants are commonly used in the absence of clear evidence-based indications. Dr Howard Forman, medical director of the Addiction Consultation Service at Montefiore Medical Center, stated that clinical depression is distinct from temporary feelings of sadness and that these do not make people mentally ill. The study also found that prescriptions for antidepressants have more than trebled since 1998 in the world's richest countries.

Doris Fuller, the mother of a 28-year-old woman who killed herself, has revealed how her daughter's mental illness, which went undiagnosed until her early 20s, eventually drove her to suicide. Fuller wrote about her daughter's life in a Washington Post article, describing how her daughter's bipolar disorder and psychosis led to her death. Fuller said her daughter was the bravest person she had ever known and that her suicide doesn't change that. The article also discusses how Fuller's daughter's condition worsened over years and eventually drove her to suicide.

A 10-year-old boy nearly died after suffering a cardiac arrest in the school playground. Koby Hodder's heart stopped for a staggering 12 minutes after he collapsed while running around with friends during the morning break. He was playing British Bulldog, a game in which children run from one side of a playing field to another without being caught by one of the 'bulldogs', who often employ forceful tactics to trap runners, including rugby tackling opponents to the ground. Koby suffered a cardiac arrest, where the electrical activity of the heart becomes so chaotic that it stops pumping and quivers or 'fibrillates' instead. His heart suddenly stopped beating blood around his body and he collapsed and lost consciousness. The 10-year-old was later diagnosed with the same heart condition as footballer Fabrice Muamba, a former Bolton Wanderers player who collapsed after suffering a cardiac arrest during the first half of Bolton's FA Cup quarter-final against Tottenham in 201

Baroness Hale of Richmond, Britain's most senior female judge, has proposed that divorce laws in England and Wales should remove the need for allegations of adultery and blame, aiming to reduce bitterness in most matrimonial disputes. She wants to see a one-year cooling off period after declaring that a marriage has permanently broken down, during which couples can sort out arrangements for children and money. Lady Hale, who is deputy president to the Supreme Court and the only woman among the 12 Supreme Court justices, is behind the move for 'no fault' divorce in England and Wales 20 years ago.

Tottenham Hotspur is considering a state-of-the-art stadium with a retractable pitch that could accommodate an NFL franchise. The stadium, set to be completed for the 2018-19 season, would feature a 'slide-out' grass pitch with an NFL-style synthetic surface. The NFL is said to be within five years of having a permanent franchise in London, and logistics for NFL games at Wembley are being tested. The new stadium could be more suitable for NFL games than Wembley, which has a capacity of 90,000 seats. The NFL is keeping their options open, but a new London stadium designed with American football requirements would be advantageous.

U.S. lawmakers have written to FIFA President Sepp Blatter, calling for Russia to be removed as host of the 2018 World Cup because of its role in the Ukraine crisis and occupation of Crimea. The 13 lawmakers, including Republican John McCain, urge FIFA to move the global competition.

Universal announced that the sequel to the box office blockbuster "Fifty Shades of Grey" will hit theaters on Feb. 10, 2017, and the third film in the series will debut Feb. 9, 2018. Niall Leonard, author's husband and screenwriter, will write the script for the second film. The second film is titled "Fifty Shades Darker." The first film earned a massive $568.8 million worldwide.

West Brom manager Tony Pulis will receive a hero's welcome when he returns to Crystal Palace on Saturday, but he must wonder if he'll ever be successful at the right end of the Premier League. Pulis has never finished in the top half of the Premier League, and his overall record is one of the worst of any long-serving Premier League manager. Pulis has never managed to guide a team into the top half of the Premier League, and he is currently the only manager in the Premier League with more than 12 months experience who has never finished higher than 11th. Pulis has a proud record of never being relegated, but he must wonder if he will be successful at the right end of the Premier League.

Fenerbahce, the Turkish football club, has called for the suspension of the Turkish championship following a gun attack on their team bus. The attack occurred on Saturday night as the bus drove to the airport after an away match. The injured driver was taken to hospital, but no other injuries were reported. Fenerbahce believes the attack is not being solved and is calling for a championship suspension. The club has posted pictures of the damaged bus on their website.

A massive avalanche struck Everest Base Camp on Saturday, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens. The avalanche, which struck at the height of the climbing season, left many climbers stranded and injured. Helicopters rescued hundreds of climbers from higher camps, but the situation remains dire, with many still missing and buried under the snow and ice. The disaster has claimed the lives of at least 4,300 people in Nepal, with thousands more injured and hundreds still trapped in the mountains.

Gregory Margolin, a 16-year-old Jewish recruit in the Soviet Red Army during World War II, survived the war and later settled in Donetsk, Ukraine. In 2014, he found himself again in the middle of a war in Eastern Ukraine, where he was attacked by a stray missile. His granddaughter, Liora, and his daughter, Ira, were killed in the attack. Margolin, who had survived one war, arrived in Israel on March 24, 2014, as part of a wave of Ukrainian Jewish immigration to Israel. The International Fellowship of Christians and Jews, founded by Rabbi Yechiel Eckstein, set up a refugee center to support the Jewish community in Eastern Ukraine.

John Carver, a former assistant to Ruud Gullit, is relishing the chance to take charge of Newcastle United against Sunderland on Sunday. Gullit's controversial decision to leave out star players Alan Shearer and Duncan Ferguson in 1999, which led to Newcastle's defeat, serves as a cautionary tale for Carver. The match is crucial for Carver's chances of winning the head coach position beyond the end of the season.

The Reverend Al Sharpton delivered a sermon and addressed the Walter Scott situation on Sunday morning. He preached at the Charity Missionary Baptist Church and addressed the Scott case and the need for reform around national policing legislation during his sermon. Mayor Keith Summey, Sheriff Al Cannon, Senator Marlon Kimpson, SCLC Leader Michael Steele, North Charleston Police Chief Eddie Driggers, and Assistant Police Chief Reggie Burgess were in attendance. Sharpton wrote on Facebook that he joined them to discuss the Scott shooting and to change what's going on in North Charleston. He also said that North Charleston, known as a place of intolerance, could be the place that could set a new tone in policing all over the United States.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers will speak to Raheem Sterling about his recent controversies, including his alleged use of nitrous oxide and shisha pipe, after the forward scored the opener in a 2-0 win over Newcastle United. Sterling, who is unwilling to sign a new contract at Anfield, has been videoed passing out after allegedly inhaling nitrous oxide and on Sunday was pictured puffing on a shisha pipe. Rodgers said he will take time to talk to his rising star about what being a professional entails. Sterling's lack of a second goal would have left him disappointed at Anfield.

Union barons gave more than £1 million to Labour in the second week of the election campaign, swelling the party's war chest for the final 14 days of the campaign. Labour received £1. 1 million in donations between April 6 and April 12, more than twice as much as the Conservative party, which received just £492, 512. Unison, USDAW, and Len McCluskey's Unite gave more than £400, 000 to Labour, while the Conservatives received £460, 000 from wealthy individuals. The Liberal Democrats received £50, 000 and Ukip £8, 000.

Passengers on a Qatar Airways flight were stranded at Manchester Airport for five hours after their plane was diverted to Birmingham due to severe winds. Passengers became frustrated with airport staff and police were called twice to the tarmac. The flight was eventually allowed to depart for Doha.
Canadian pop sensation Justin Bieber will carry Floyd Mayweather's championship belts into the ring ahead of his $300million Las Vegas mega-fight with Manny Pacquiao on Saturday.

The article discusses the closure of Corinthian Colleges Inc., a for-profit college that has been struggling to hold accountable. Corinthian, which once enrolled more than 70,000 students, is one of the worst of the "predator colleges" that offer dubious degrees, saddle students with high amounts of debt, and gobble up tens of billions of dollars in federal money every year. The closure of Corinthian is a positive development in a long struggle to hold for-profit colleges accountable. The article also mentions that for-profit colleges enroll only 13% of the nation's college students, but they account for nearly half of all student loan defaults. The article concludes that the remaining for-profit colleges should be closed, and any student not gainfully employed or transferred to a reputable college within three years should be considered a victim, and their debts should be forgiven.

Pep Guardiola has denied claims of a dispute with former Bayern Munich club doctor Hans-Wilhelm Muller-Wohlfahrt, who quit the club after being blamed for the defeat by Porto. Muller-Wohlfahrt claimed the bond of trust was damaged, but Guardiola played down the feud. Muller-Wohlfahrt had worked at Bayern for almost 40 years and was 72 years old at the time of his resignation. Bayern lost 3-1 to Porto in the Champions League quarter-final on Wednesday. Guardiola appeared to publicly humiliate Muller-Wohlfahrt eight days before his exit from the club. Muller-Wohlfahrt is a world leader in his field and has been at Bayern for almost 40 years.

Wladimir Klitschko, the reigning heavyweight champion, has recalled his dramatic rise to the top on the eve of his world title defence against Bryant Jennings. The Ukrainian superstar will make his return to US soil for the first time in seven years when he takes on the slick Philadelphian at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. Klitschko, who won Olympic gold in Atlanta in 1996, has been reminiscing about how it all started for him when he won gold at the Olympics, instantly catapulting him into a hero in his home country.

Jeremy Clarkson, who was fired from Top Gear, has admitted he will "miss" fronting the BBC2 show. Former presenter Angela Rippon, who first presented the show 38 years ago, said it would be "great" if she were invited back. The BBC has not announced whether it will renew Clarkson's contract.

Celta Vigo striker Fabian Orellana was shown a red card for throwing a lump of grass at Barcelona midfielder Sergio Busquets during a La Liga match. The incident led to Busquets grabbing his eye, and referee Inaki Vicandi Garrido gave Orellana his marching orders. Despite the incident, Barcelona earned a crucial three points against Celta Vigo.

In 2013, three people died and over 200 were injured when a pair of bombs went off within 12 seconds of each other at the finish line of the Boston Marathon. In 2015, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was convicted of using weapons of mass destruction, bombing a place of public use, conspiracy, and aiding and abetting. The sentencing phase of his trial began on April 21, and the judge warned jurors not to attend the Boston Marathon or any events related to the anniversary or the current running of the Boston Marathon. The maximum penalty for several of the charges is death.

Millions of Chinese people travelled home to their ancestral villages for the annual Qingming Festival, marking the start of spring and honouring their loved ones. The festival involves cleaning tombs, burning fake paper money, and leaving food and drink to ensure the deceased are not poor or hungry in the afterlife. The festival is celebrated in the first week of April and is one of the 24 Chinese solar terms.
