Paul Simon, 73, has topped the UK album chart for the first time in 25 years with his latest release, The Ultimate Collection. The album, which includes 19 tracks from his 50-year career, including hits from his days with Simon & Garfunkel, has outsold more youthful musicians such as Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. Simon's recent tour with Sting is believed to have been the catalyst in helping to propel him to the top of the charts.
Iker Casillas insists he will stay at Real Madrid even if David de Gea arrives to displace him as first choice keeper at the Bernabeu.

Britain's employment hit a record high of 31 million in the three months to February, according to official figures. The Conservatives' economic strategy was praised by the International Monetary Fund, with Chancellor George Osborne receiving a "wonderful job" from Christine Lagarde. Rolls-Royce announced its biggest-ever order, worth more than £6 billion, to power passenger jets for the Middle Eastern airline Emirates. The UK's fiscal deficit has been significantly reduced over the last few years, and the Chancellor has delivered a "highly unusual endorsement" of the Tories. The UK economy is "firmly on course" with strong growth and record high employment. However, Greece poses the biggest threat to the global economy, and fears are mounting that the recession-battered country will default on its debts and be forced to leave the eurozone.

SsangYong, a Korean automaker, is launching a new sports utility vehicle (SUV) called Tivoli in the UK, priced under £13,000. The SUV is named after the Italian town of Tivoli, known for its Renaissance architecture and garden. It is powered by 1.6-liter Euro 6 petrol and diesel engines with six-speed manual and automatic transmissions. The Tivoli SUV arrives in the UK this summer in three trim levels, with a choice of front-wheel drive or 'intelligent' 4x4 and seven airbags across the range. The entry-level SE, from £12,950, is finished in grey cloth trim and includes 16-inch alloys, cruise control, a petrol stop/go system, seven airbags, and 'smart' steering with normal, comfort, and sport modes. The top-of-the-range ELX, from £16,000 to £19

A chef has created a 10in-tall, half-kilogram burger piled with six forms of three different meats and containing a whopping 2,000 calories. The Whole Damn Farm burger features two beef patties and a whole fried chicken thigh, along with barbequed pulled pork and bacon. The burger was created after a customer challenged the chef to create a burger containing three kinds of meat. The head chef, Sam Longhurst, from the Splendid Kitchen restaurant in Manchester, devised the mega meal after experimenting with cooking at home. The burger is described as a "monster of a burger" and is considered a supersized version of a homemade burger stuffed with cheese and cold meats.

The Yeo Valley staff canteen, which serves high-quality meals prepared by a Michelin-starred chef, has opened to the public. The canteen, which offers meals for £2, has been hailed as the world's best staff canteen. The canteen's menu changes daily and includes organic and locally sourced produce. The canteen has been praised for its high-quality food and the staff's love for it.

Blues legend B.B. King was hospitalized for dehydration, but he is "much better" and is back home resting with his grandchildren. King, 89, has used various models of Gibson guitars over the years, and named each one of them Lucille. He has 30 Grammy nominations and has been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987. King, who has suffered from dehydration and exhaustion after a show in Chicago, has canceled the remainder of his tour.

On Easter Sunday, New York's Fifth Avenue was transformed into a sea of bizarre hats as people celebrated the holiday in outlandish headgear. The parade featured a variety of headpieces, including ship-shaped hats, elaborate dioramas, and floral bonnets. The event attracted people of different faiths and backgrounds, with some wearing more conservative attire and others opting for more colorful and whimsical headwear. The parade was organized by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation and was held in the heart of Manhattan.

Emergency crews in East of England received 1,248 inappropriate calls in the last two years, including one where a squirrel was reported to have been run over by a car. The service said it receives around 2,500 calls per day and that half of the phoney calls were attended by front-line crews, potentially putting lives at risk.

Chelsea players Eden Hazard and Nathan Ake took part in a football challenge with their teammates Loic Remy and Willian. The challenge involved shooting balls into the boot of a car from close range and from long range. Hazard and Ake won the first round, while Remy and Willian won the second round. In the final round, Hazard and Ake won again, while Remy and Willian were involved in a misfortune when Willian smashed the wing mirror of one of the Audi's with a long-range effort.

Brendan Rodgers has criticised Raheem Sterling's advisor, suggesting that the player is being manipulated by outside forces and that he would be inclined to stay at Liverpool if left to make a decision alone. Sterling has rejected a contract extension worth £100,000 a week and has just two years left on his deal at the end of this season, but Rodgers said he has sat down with Sterling since that TV interview and to tell him that his best interest would be served by staying at the club for now, even though there may come a time when he does leave.

Rachel Riley, Countdown's co-presenter, was embarrassed on a recent episode when contestants offered up a rude eight-letter word as their answer to the word game. Host Nick Hewer struggled to stifle his laughter as the blushing Ms Riley spelled out the word 'erection'. The word game, which has been running since 1982, recently picked up a Guinness world record when it reached its 6,000th episode.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, who was arrested after attempting to buy deadly poison online, was spared jail after pleading guilty to the charge. The teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, expressed an interest in buying the poison and suggested making future purchases in larger quantities. The case highlights the dangers of the dark web and the need for vigilance in law enforcement.

Three hours after giving birth to her long-awaited baby girl, Lianne Hindle, a 37-year-old mother-of-four, died at the scandal-hit North Manchester General Hospital in December. The incident occurred just months after three babies and one mother died at the maternity unit. The deaths prompted an investigation, and the family of Lianne Hindle, whose partner Chris Barnes and his sister Karen have called for action to prevent further tragedies, has expressed concerns about the care she received.

Australian Olympian Jana Pittman gave birth to her second child, a daughter named Emily, just days after a video surfaced of the athlete training while eight months pregnant. Pittman, who plans to compete in both the Beijing World Championships and the 2016 Rio Olympics, continued to train while pregnant with her son Cornelis, who was born seven months after he was born in 2006. The athlete's coach, Mike Hurst, said that Pittman trained every second day and was careful to monitor her core temperature throughout her training program. The 32-year-old was filmed training for the 2016 Rio Olympics the day before she went into labour.

A powerful storm capsized several sailboats during a regatta in Alabama, resulting in at least one death and multiple missing people. The storm rolled through the area around 4 p.m. and a man was plucked from the waters by the Coast Guard around 9 p.m. The storm caused significant damage to the boats and resulted in scattered boats across Mobile Bay. The storm was described as a gale, and the boats sank quickly, leaving the crews exhausted but unharmed.

Roseanne Barr, 62, has been diagnosed with macular degeneration and glaucoma, two eye diseases that are getting progressively worse over time and can steal vision. The diseases are caused by fluid build-up and pressure in the eyes. Barr's doctors haven't provided a timeline, but her symptoms are worsening. The combination of the two is terrible. Macular degeneration takes away her central vision, and glaucoma is taking away her peripheral vision. There is no cure for either disease, but there are treatments that may delay the progression of early-stage glaucoma and therapies that might halt further vision loss in advanced cases of macular degeneration.

A 17-year-old Oklahoma teenager was convicted of first-degree murder in the 2013 shooting death of an Australian college baseball player who was killed while out for a jog. The Stephens County jury found Chancey Allen Luna guilty in the August 16, 2013, death of Christopher Lane, who was shot in the back while running along a city street in Duncan. The jury recommended that Luna be sentenced to life in prison without parole.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger insists his team's poor record against Jose Mourinho will not affect their chances of beating Chelsea on Sunday. Wenger has lost 12 of their 12 meetings with Mourinho, drawing five and losing seven. The match is expected to be a high-stakes contest, with Chelsea boasting efficiency in counter-attacks and set-pieces. Wenger emphasizes the importance of focusing on Sunday's performance rather than their past encounters.

Manny Pacquiao, a Filipino boxer, has become one of the most recognizable figures in sports after a series of major fights, including a bout against Floyd Mayweather, which is scheduled for Saturday night at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Pacquiao, who was born into poverty in the Philippines, spent his early career boxing in the Far East before gaining recognition in 2001 when he fought against Lehlo Ledwaba in an IBF world super-bantamweight title fight in Las Vegas. His rise to fame has been marked by a series of successful fights, including a victory over Floyd Mayweather, who is set to face Pacquiao in the Fight of the Century on Saturday night.

A young footballer, Jack Grealish, has been caught on camera inhaling nitrous oxide, a drug that can be used recreationally but is also illegal. The incident has sparked debate about the role of drugs in professional sports and the need for athletes to prioritize their health. Grealish, who has become a top-flight starlet, has not yet achieved the level of success he has shown in his games. Wenger, the manager of Arsenal, has emphasized the importance of professional athletes taking care of their bodies and avoiding drugs that can slow down their performance.

Sam Barton, a 22-year-old man who underwent £55,000 of cosmetic surgery to look like reality star Joey Essex, was attacked by a group of men who pelted him with eggs on Easter Monday. The attack was believed to be targeted because he had checked in at a pub on Facebook minutes earlier. Sam had spent £20,000 on treatment for his teeth, around £5,000 on Botox, £2,000 on waxing, and £2,500 on tanning treatment. He had also undergone two nose jobs, one of which was free on the NHS. Sam had spent £100,000 on debts to finance his plastic surgery and a champagne lifestyle to match his TOWIE heroes Joey Essex and Harry Derbidge.

A university in Indiana was on lockdown late on Friday night after a 'likely prank call' about an armed person near the main administration building. The university issued a shelter in place warning and continued to repost the message for hours after the original message. No injuries have been confirmed, and the university's peace studies program is located on the campus.

Edinson Cavani, a player known as El Matador, prepares for Paris Saint-Germain's quarter-final clash with Barcelona. If PSG are to progress beyond the Champions League's last eight, Cavani must torment the stars from Catalonia.

Derry Mathews has won the interim WBA lightweight title after defeating Tony Luis in a close fight. Mathews, who was drafted in at the last minute, outperformed Luis in the closing rounds and was given a 114-112, 114-112, 115-112 decision.

Hull, the injured champions, defeated St Helens 28-20 in a surprise victory at Langtree Park. Hull's Jamie Shaul scored the winning try, and the win was a significant comeback from a previous defeat. The game was notable for its tactical changes and the return of former Saint Alex Walmsley. Hull's Jordan Rankin added the extras, and the win was crucial for Hull, who had lost to rivals Wigan in the previous week.

The U.S. Census figures predict that the undocumented and documented immigrant population in the United States could reach a record high of 51 million by 2023, with immigrants accounting for 14.8% of the population. By 2060, the immigrant population could reach 78 million, making up 82% of the population. The growth in immigrant population has important implications for workers, schools, infrastructure, congestion, and the environment. The surge in immigrant population has led Republican presidential candidates to figure out their stance on the subject as potential new policies could be established.

Arsenal Under 21s lost 1-0 to Reading U21s in a match that showcased the club's next generation of talent. Martin Keown's son, Niall, scored the only goal for Reading, while Jack Wilshere made his long-awaited return from injury but could not prevent the defeat.

Justin Rose, the English golfer, has been struggling with his form, falling outside the world's top 10 after a bruising Florida swing. However, he has been working hard on the practice ground and has shown improvement in his game. Rose has been hitting 17 out of 18 greens in regulation and signed for a 69 at the Shell Houston Open. He is optimistic that he will be able to finish well at the Masters. Phil Mickelson, another golfer, has enjoyed his best round in months with a 66 on Thursday. Rose is proud of his recent improvement and hopes to maintain his position in the world rankings.

A Mayfair mansion that was once a milking parlour has gone on the market for £25 million. The property, which is decorated with modern furnishings and features a private lift, indoor swimming pool, and cinema room, was built in 2011 after the original structure was demolished. The mansion is being sold by estate agents Wetherell and Knight Frank.

Bayern Munich's squad is stronger for their recent injury troubles, according to Thomas Muller. The Bavarians, chasing three titles this season, are without Arjen Robben, Franck Ribery, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and David Alaba for the Champions League game against Porto. Muller believes the team will be able to score goals despite the injuries. Bayern Munich will rely heavily on the scoring prowess of Muller and Robert Lewandowski in the absence of Robben and Ribery.

Mercedes team-mates Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton visited the team's Brackley base in an attempt to devise a winning strategy for the upcoming Chinese Grand Prix. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admitted that he was surprised by Sebastian Vettel's Malaysian Grand Prix victory, which was won by 8.5 seconds. The team's tactics were criticized for being too aggressive, which pushed them into a three-stop strategy that was not as effective as Ferrari's two-stop strategy. The visit to the base was seen as a sign of the team's determination to regain their dominance in the championship.

Oklahoma Governor Mary Fallin signed a bill allowing the state to perform executions with nitrogen gas if lethal injection is ruled unconstitutional or becomes unavailable. The bill was signed on Friday, and the state's executions have been put on hold while the U.S. Supreme Court reviews its use of lethal injections. Fallin reaffirmed her support for the death penalty, stating that Oklahoma executes murderers whose crimes are especially heinous.

Bafetimbi Gomis scored twice in Swansea's 3-1 win over Hull on Saturday and tops this week's EA Sports' Performance Index after another thrilling installment of Premier League action. Gomis has scored four goals in his last six Premier League games and earned a Game Index score of 52.9 this weekend.

A massive freezer trawler sank in the Sea of Okhotsk, killing at least 56 crew members and leaving 13 missing. The ship, carrying 132 crew members, sank in just 15 minutes after an empty fuel tank and lack of ballast caused it to tip over. More than 1,300 people are involved in the rescue operation, with 63 survivors rescued so far. The sinking is believed to have been caused by hitting an object in the sea, possibly drifting ice. The incident occurred at around 4am local time, and temperatures in the water can drop to as low as -2 degrees Celsius, making rescue efforts challenging.

A new study suggests that a drug originally developed for women with breast cancer could also help men with advanced prostate cancer. The drug, called olaparib, works by blocking the cancer cell's ability to repair damage, targeting cells with genetic defects. The study found that 16 out of 49 men with advanced prostate cancer responded to the drug, stopping prostate cancer growth and improving responses in medical scans. The drug could extend the length of time that a prostate cancer patient lives with the disease without it getting worse.

Travel photographer Rhiannon Taylor, 29, from Australia, has turned her passion for photography and globetrotting into a business by launching the website "In Bed With" to review and photograph the best hotels, beds, pools, and room service around the world. With more than 12,000 followers on Instagram, she has built relationships with hotels and PR companies over the past seven years, allowing her to stay at exclusive resorts and feature their properties on her site. The website's name, "In Bed With," is a play on her Instagram handle, and the concept is unique as it focuses on luxurious accommodations. Taylor has photographed properties in countries like Indonesia, the US, and Mexico, and has received payments from hotels and companies for featuring their products on her site.

A five-day-old baby hippopotamus was mauled to death by two adult hippos in the iSimangaliso Wetland Park in eastern South Africa. The calf's mother watched in horror as the hippo was flung into the air before being dragged along the surface of the water. The baby stood no chance against the two adults as they brawled in the muddy waters of the nature reserve. The mother tried to get the baby back but with the young calf in the sub-adult's mouth there wasn't much she could do. The hippopotamus died of its injuries hours later.

The Football Association will contact QPR and Chelsea after an incident at Loftus Road where Branislav Ivanovic was struck by a cigarette lighter thrown from a section of home supporters. Chelsea players celebrated the winning goal, and objects were thrown onto the pitch. QPR is reviewing CCTV footage and appealing to witnesses. The club is banning those involved and will liaise with the Metropolitan Police. Chelsea duo Nemanja Matic and Branislav Ivanovic were struck.

A young mother and her three children were found murdered in their home in Tisdale, Saskatchewan. The suspect in the case was found dead hours later, and while police would not say how he died, they did say that it was not a homicide. The victim's sister, Laura Gross, described the discovery as "very, very devastating." The family is now trying to raise money for their funeral services.

Emily Thornberry, a senior Labour politician, was forced to resign from the shadow cabinet after tweeting a picture of a house she owned, which was later revealed to be worth almost £3 million. The incident highlighted Thornberry's hypocrisy in opposing right to buy while renting out a property she bought from a housing association.

Mike Lane, a huntsman, was attacked by protesters armed with iron bars during a hunt in Wiltshire, England. Despite evidence pointing to the identity of the attacker, police dropped the investigation three months later, angering the victim and supporters of the hunt. The attack occurred when protesters sprayed hounds with citronella to distract them from an artificial scent, and the suspect was identified in a video. The incident has sparked outrage and calls for the police to do more to protect hunters.

Valencia midfielder Andre Gomes insists he has no intention of leaving the club this summer. He says remaining at the Mestalla is his preferred option. Gomes has netted four times in 25 La Liga appearances since leaving Benfica last summer, helping Valencia to fourth place in the table. Chelsea has reportedly shown interest in him, but Gomes denies being contacted by the Premier League leaders.

An Australian teenager was raped twice by a man she met in Bali, according to a Channel 9 investigation. Audrey Pekin, 19, says she was lured to a remote home by Henry Alafu, who then attacked her in a taxi. Alafu allegedly told her a party was taking place at a nearby villa, and the pair agreed to go together. During the ride, Pekin felt unwell due to her diabetes, and Alafu locked the door and raped her. She escaped the cab but was forced again, and Alafu allegedly molested her in the back of the vehicle. Pekin's family believed Alafu attacked her, but the Indonesian police let him escape.

PETA has teamed up with Ashley James, a former Made in Chelsea star, to launch an anti-fur campaign against Harvey Nichols, a department store that previously had a ten-year anti-fur policy. The campaign features a fake skinned fox and aims to educate people about the cruelty of the fur industry. Harvey Nichols has since re-introduced its fur-free policy, but PETA is still in talks with billboard companies to mount posters outside the store.

Chile has joined several of its South American neighbors in allowing civil unions between people of the same sex. President Michelle Bachelet enacted a new law on Monday, which will take effect in six months and give legal weight to cohabiting relationships between two people of the same sex and between a man and a woman. The law is intended to end discrimination faced by common-law couples and gives them greater rights in the realms of property, health care, pensions and inheritance.

Chelsea are on course to become the most dominant title-winners in Premier League history as they prepare to break the record of most days at the summit of the table in a single season. Mourinho's side have led the way since beating Everton 6-3 at Goodison Park on August 30, after Tottenham had led the table following the first two rounds of games. Chelsea players celebrate as they beat Stoke City 2-1 in the Premier League last Saturday.

Cape Verde, a small country off the coast of Africa, is tapping into its rich musical heritage to boost its economy. The country, which has few natural resources, is promoting music and culture as a way to attract visitors and create jobs. The Kriol Jazz Festival, which has been held in Cape Verde for seven years, has become a major event, bringing artists from around the world to share their music. The festival has helped to showcase Cape Verde's unique musical styles, such as batuque and morna, and has attracted visitors from all over the world. The success of the festival has encouraged the government to invest in the creative economy and to promote Cape Verde's cultural heritage.

An old hoax video showing a wave rider surfing in front of the Sydney's Opera House has gone viral for the second time. The video was originally posted by Sydney radio duo Fitzy and Wippa on Tuesday morning, quickly being reposted by other sources. Some users have referenced the weather as the trigger of the strange phenomenon, with musician Fortafy uploading the video with the caption 'storm brings out surfers in Sydney Harbour.' YouTube commenters pointed out inaccuracies in the video, such as the appearance of rocks around the Opera House and the cardboard-esque appearance of the man in the final shot. Wave experts vowed it was a sham, and Ben Macartney, a swell forecaster, told News.com that it was theoretically impossible for ocean swells to break that far inside the Harbour.

Reading, the FA Cup semi-finalists, were defeated 1-0 by Birmingham in a Sky Bet Championship game at the Madejski Stadium. Clayton Donaldson scored the winning goal in the 78th minute. Reading's Adam Federici, who had fumbled a crucial clearance against Arsenal in the last four of the Cup, was retained for the match.

David Luiz, a key player for Paris Saint-Germain, will miss the Champions League clash with Barcelona due to a hamstring injury. The Brazilian defender, who has been a mainstay for the team, will be out of action for at least four weeks, potentially affecting PSG's chances of securing the Ligue One title.

The return of Game of Thrones has sparked a surge in internet piracy with fans making more than 100,000 illegal downloads per day. Figures by anti-piracy and security firm Irdeto revealed overall illegal downloading of show is up 45 per cent year-on-year, jumping from 4.9 million for the same two-month period in 2014.

Leicester City host West Ham United in a Premier League match on Saturday. Leicester's Matt Upson is out with an Achilles injury, while West Ham's Winston Reid is back after a hamstring problem. The match is scheduled for 3pm and will be refereed by Mark Clattenburg.

A statue of Lucille Ball, the beloved comedian from the TV show "I Love Lucy," has become a source of controversy in Celoron, New York. The statue, which depicts Ball in a drunken state pitching a health tonic, has attracted criticism from locals who say it is unflattering and monstrous. The statue, which was created by artist Dave Poulin, has been estimated to cost between $8,000 and $10,000 to recast. The town has tried to honor its most famous resident, but the statue has sparked a debate about the accuracy of historical depictions.

A woman who tipped the scales at almost 20st lost nearly half her body weight after she was forced to stand during an 11-hour flight because she feared she was crushing the woman in the seat next to her.

Nicola Bonn, a 34-year-old mother of a 14-month-old daughter, started a blog called Upfront Mama to share her experiences and advice on raising a baby for the first time. Her candid account of bringing up a baby for the first time went viral, and she shares one of her blog posts with FEMAIL. She believes that one of the main hurdles for new mothers is that everyone has an opinion and they're often not afraid to air it, which can be quite overwhelming for a new mother who is less experienced.

Two teenage boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, who are believed to have traveled to Syria to join ISIS, have been reported missing by their families. The boys, who are from Dewsbury, West Yorkshire, have not been in contact with their families for several days and cannot be reached on their mobile phones. The families are in a state of profound shock and deeply worried about the safety of their loved ones. The two families have released a statement expressing their concern and implore anyone who may have any information to get in contact with the police.

Stephanie Scott, a beloved school teacher from Leeton, was brutally murdered just days before her much-anticipated wedding. Her father, Robert, described her as bubbly and thoughtful, and her aim was to make her wedding day as perfect as hers. The wedding was to be held at the picturesque Eat Your Greens venue, decorated with yellow balloons and flowers, but instead of a wedding, the Scott family must prepare for Stephanie's funeral. The wedding guest list of 120 people was sent out, but the ceremony was due to go ahead on Saturday, April 11, before her remains were discovered by police.

Southampton are interested in signing Tonny Vilhena, a 20-year-old winger from Feyenoord, who is eager to leave the club this summer. Koeman, the manager of Southampton, is also considering bringing Jordy Clasie, a £10m-rated midfielder, to the south coast. Koeman is also looking to make Eljero Elia's loan move from Werder Bremen permanent.

The National Trust replaced antique furniture with beanbags in the library of Ickworth House, Suffolk, in an experiment that has angered heritage experts. The move was designed to encourage visitors to 'dwell and take in the atmosphere' but was branded 'misguided' by art historian Bendor Grosvenor. The Trust said the beanbag experiment was 'short-term' and that it presents each house in context. The experiment will be repeated at nine other Trust venues around the country.

Former Australian Prime Minister John Howard was photographed standing on the side of the road with a flat tyre, but was helped by a woman who was waiting for her daughter at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. The incident came just weeks after Liberal MP Christopher Pyne was challenged to change a tyre on national television after boasting he was a 'fixer'.

West Bromwich Albion manager Tony Pulis has admitted that Joey Barton "probably had a point" about the team's performance during a 2-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers earlier this season. Pulis believes that Barton's comments about the team's inability to finish the game were justified, as the team had been leading 2-0 and lost 3-2. Pulis also recalled his own experience of leading a team to a 2-0 lead but losing in a play-off final in 1999. Pulis praised the team's performances and hopes to continue that success in their upcoming match against QPR.

A new species of monkey has been discovered after scientists learned to distinguish it by the appearance of its penis. The white-cheeked macaque was discovered in the remote highland forests of south-east Tibet after researchers set up camera traps.

Kim Kardashian and her family are visiting Armenia for eight days, including a rock star welcome and exploring the country's landmarks. The visit is their first to Armenia, where they are staying at the Armenia Marriott Hotel Yerevan. The Kardashian-West crew are staying in the capital's finest digs, with the burliest of bodyguards and police in tow. The visit is well connected to major centres throughout Europe, with cheaper flights from London requiring a transfer.

A British couple, Patrick and Valerie Jubb, are facing legal battles with the local town hall over a luxury bed and breakfast they once operated in southern Spain. The couple, who purchased the property in 2008, are attempting to sell it but are now facing the possibility of losing it over illegal additions made by a previous owner. The Jubbs claim they have done nothing wrong and are trapped in the property due to the ongoing legal dispute.

Apple reported a 40% increase in iPhone sales in the first quarter of 2015, with more than 61 million units sold, accounting for two-thirds of its $58 billion in revenue and $13.6 billion in profit. The company's iPad revenue fell 29% to $5.4 billion, while Mac computer revenue rose 2% to $5.6 billion. The iPhone has become the engine behind Apple's success, with a 72% increase in sales in China.

A 3-year-old girl who survived a 2017 SUV crash with her mother has been plagued by disturbing nightmares and daytime visions about a white van, which her father believes may have something to do with the crash. The girl's father, Craig Tyler, told CBS6 that the little girl has been having nightmares and daytime visions about the accident. The white van has been linked to no fewer than three hit-and-run incidents in which two cars and a school bus were side-swiped.

Researchers have discovered that the brain can remember 'neutral' or boring events more easily when they are tied to an emotion. This finding suggests that the brain has the remarkable ability to store information that seems inconsequential at the time in case it becomes useful later on. Emotion increases our ability to remember by affecting activity in brain regions involved in emotional processing and also the regions involved in encoding new experiences.

Jahnae Jackson, the girlfriend of a teenager with a life-threatening tumour, has put her psychology studies on hold to care for her long-term boyfriend, Jackson Byrnes, who was diagnosed with a stage four brain tumour four weeks ago. The 18-year-olds from northern NSW have raised over $80,000 from community generosity for his life-saving surgery to be performed by renowned neurosurgeon Dr. Charlie Teo. Jackson is paralysed and needs help dressing himself, and Jahnae and her girlfriend have been desperately raising the sum needed to pay the hospital. The community support from the small town of Casino in northern NSW has been overwhelming, and they are overwhelmed by the community support from the small town of Casino in northern NSW. Jackson's surgery is likely to save his life, but he still has a long road of rehabilitation in front of him as he will be left paralysed for some time.

Nedum Onuoha, a QPR centre-back, is being targeted by Hull City, Everton, and West Ham United, among other clubs. Onuoha, who has 15 months left on his contract, has played regularly under Chris Ramsey and was in the starting eleven for QPR's 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion. Stoke manager Mark Hughes is also interested in Onuoha, and Everton and West Ham are also showing interest in the player. Onuoha is also being considered for a move to Stoke, while Hull City are interested in West Bromwich Albion's striker Victor Anichebe, who is likely to be sold this summer.

Researchers at Yale University have created an interactive map that shows the subtle differences in sentence structure across the US. The map reveals that every state has its own set of phrases that can seem bizarre to the rest of the English-speaking world. The project was conducted using an online crowdsourcing platform and the researchers were not interested in what is considered to be correct grammar, but in what people do naturally. The overall pattern was clear; In the South people found that sentence to be completely normal, while in the North, it was almost unheard of.

A Canadian man named Kalman Kallai took a rocking chair on a nine-day journey across Canada from Borden, Ontario to Comox, British Columbia. He used the chair to enjoy the scenery and took photos of the planes flying by. The video shows him sitting on the chair, posing, and dancing with his dad.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood revealed a Twix multi-pack as a 'win bonus' to six-year-old fan Charlie Pye, who applied for the club's hotseat after Paul Lambert was sacked. Sherwood joked that Pye's win bonus would be sweets and chocolate.

Kell Brook, a world boxing champion, enjoyed an evening at the darts as he watched the Premier League road show come to his home town of Sheffield on Thursday. Dave Chisnall, a darts player, won both of his games in week 10 to move onto 17 points in second place. Chisnall said he felt comfortable throughout the night and got a great start by defeating Gary Anderson.

Marco Verratti of Paris Saint-Germain has praised Zlatan Ibrahimovic for his essential role in the club's Ligue 1 goals, saying he is always on hand to help his team-mates and exerts confidence in the team. Ibrahimovic, who was suspended for the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Barcelona, will be available for selection ahead of the return fixture.

The RAF's main base on the Falklands Islands was accidentally published on the MoD's website, containing vital details such as GPS coordinates and runway depth, which could be used by Argentina to prepare an invasion. The information was accidentally uploaded to a public section of the MoD's website and could have been downloaded by Argentine intelligence agents. The MoD denied the information was particularly sensitive and admitted the manual had been available on the internet. The RAF is defending the islands with modern Eurofighter Typhoon aircraft, and the UK is considering leasing 12 Sukhoi SU-24 bombers from Russia.

Paul Anderson, Huddersfield Giants coach, hopes to kick-start his side's misfiring attack to climb up Super League. The Giants have plummeted from third to ninth after losing all three games over the Easter holiday period. Anderson says they need to find their offensive groove more than their defensive one. Huddersfield can climb to a season-high fourth if they make it three wins in a row against Catalans Dragons.

Two Costa Coffee shops have been allowed to open less than 500 yards apart in Windsor, England, sparking controversy among residents who believe it will lead to an overabundance of coffee shops in the area. The new Costa will open at the site of the former Dedworth Road HSBC branch, while the other Costa replaced a cycle shop earlier this year. The Costa Express is also located between the two shops.

The British Veterinary Association has withdrawn its support for the controversial shooting of free-running badgers in two four-year pilot culls in Somerset and Gloucestershire. The BVA concluded that the first two years of culling had not demonstrated conclusively that 'controlled shooting' of badgers could be effective and humane. The BVA still supports badger culling to tackle tuberculosis in cattle. The Environment Secretary promised to roll out more culls across the country if the Tories win the election.

Portishead founder Geoff Barrow has accused streaming services of giving music away, saying his band received just £1,700 in royalties despite their songs being played 34million times. Barrow, who also runs the Invada record label, told The Times that he wants musicians to be paid more and says it is hurting young talent, stopping people from establishing themselves on the scene.

Game of Thrones fans who did not want to wait and legally watch HBO's hit series premiere its fifth season tonight have leaked the first four episodes online. The episodes began appearing on torrent download sites on Saturday night, and are thought to have leaked from review copies given to the press. The first four episodes of the show's next season are titled The Wars to Come, The House of Black and White, High Sparrow and The Sons of the Harpy. They had been downloaded more than 550,000 times as of early Sunday morning.

A best man left guests at his brother's wedding in tears after composing an emotional song to use as his best man's speech. Daniel Buccheri, a 25-year-old singer, composed the song "Stay With Me" to use as his speech at his brother Adrian's wedding. The unique speech performed by Daniel at Poet's Lane in Sherbrooke, east of Melbourne, has been viewed over 100,000 times online and included tributes to his brother and his bride and also delves into his childhood and says he always looked up to his older sibling.

Zara Phillips, the Queen's granddaughter, has revealed how she regained her fitness after the birth of her daughter Mia. She started exercising every morning, hitting the exercise bike at her home before her daughter wakes up. She also spends time with horses at her mother's stables and squeezes in extra exercise like swimming or cycling. Zara hopes to qualify for the 2016 Olympics and is eager for her daughter Mia to grow up around horses.

Raheem Sterling's interview on Wednesday, in which he said he was not ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, has angered fans and potentially changed their opinion of him. The interview was ill-timed and did not go well, and it has fueled the fire among some fans who want him to leave. Sterling has been linked with a move to Arsenal, and while he has the potential to be worth more than the £100,000-a-week contract he has turned down, he is also prone to bouts of inconsistency and prolonged poor form. Liverpool fans have a popular mantra that no player is bigger than the club, but Sterling is nowhere near.

The article discusses a series of images from Barcelona's training sessions featuring former and current coaches, including Jose Mourinho, Pep Guardiola, Luis Enrique, Laurent Blanc, and Julen Lopetegui. The images reveal a pattern of coaches from the same club and era working together, suggesting a connection between the teams. The article also mentions the breeding of managers from that team, with players from the 1996 Spanish Super Cup team going on to manage other clubs.

Eric Cantona, a former Manchester United striker, has declared Javier Pastore, a Paris Saint-Germain forward, as the best player in the world. Cantona's assessment is based on Pastore's ability to pass and create opportunities for his teammates, which he believes is a key aspect of the game. Despite Messi and Ronaldo's impressive statistics, Cantona argues that Pastore's creativity and ability to surprise opponents make him the most creative player in the world.

Lorenzo Simon, 34, was found guilty of murder after killing his tenant then hacking his body into pieces. Simon forced victim Michael Spalding, 39, to decorate his flat before attacking him when he refused to work any longer. He then dismembered the handyman using a hacksaw and put Mr Spalding's body parts and tools into two suitcases. Simon, with the help of his girlfriend Michelle Bird, 35, then threw the suitcases into a canal which they weighed down using broken concrete slabs.

Two county councils, Essex and Gloucestershire, have implemented 'loneliness maps' to identify areas where residents are most likely to suffer from social isolation. The maps are based on statistics on public health factors and surveys of residents to identify those who rarely speak to their neighbors, are unsatisfied with their social life, and say they don't have someone to talk to. The most vulnerable areas are marked in red. The Campaign to End Loneliness recommends the maps as a way of treating the problem across the country. The report identifies a number of other risk factors that might make people more likely to suffer from chronic loneliness.

Dedicated waitress Judy Eddingfield, 65, celebrated her 50th anniversary working at Winstead's restaurant in Kansas City, the only job she's ever had or ever wanted. She started working there in 1965, when she was 15, and has been providing top-notch service for half a century. Eddingfield's mother had been working at the restaurant for 13 years when she started, and she has been married to her first husband, Jerry Mathers, for 18 months after meeting him at the restaurant.

Former England captain Mike Gatting believes Kevin Pietersen should not walk straight back into the international set-up, even if he piles on the runs for Surrey this season. Pietersen has returned to the LV= County Championship in a bid to stake a claim for an England recall, although the 34-year-old only managed 19 runs against Glamorgan on Sunday. Gatting believes that if Gary Ballance, Ian Bell and Joe Root play well, there might not be a place for Pietersen in the team. Pietersen is keen to play for England again after being sacked in 2014.

A 17-year-old college student named Caleb Benn developed an app called 'Uploader for Instagram' that allows users to upload photos to the popular photo-sharing app directly from their computer rather than using only their smartphone. The app is currently making $1,000 a day, and Instagram is unhappy with the hackings its API. Benn is currently making $1,000 a day from the app, and Instagram is asking him to 'fix' the app by Monday. The app allows users to combine their photos into a single image before uploading it to the app.

South Korean business culture emphasizes drinking as a way to get to know colleagues. Foreigners may feel pressured to participate, but understanding the context can help. Koreans defer to senior figures and pour alcohol first, while turning one's back to them during drinking. Gunbae! is a common phrase to chug the entire glass.

The Duke of Kent, 79, was admitted to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary after suffering a dislocated hip during an Easter trip to the Royal Family's Balmoral estate. He was successfully treated and is expected to leave hospital later today.

Meter Maids, a 50-year-old tradition of Surfers Paradise, Queensland, have been criticized by local business owners who believe the outdated and outdated practice of young women dressed in gold bikinis walking the main tourist strip and placing money into expired meters is no longer relevant due to advancements in parking meter technology. The controversy has split the Gold Coast community, with business leaders calling for the end of an era, while local business owners label the group as outdated and no longer providing a service.

Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills. Deputy finance minister Dimitris Mardas said that Greece will in fact make the payment on time. Greece has denied it will miss a repayment of £330million to the International Monetary Fund after reports it had drawn up plans to introduce a parallel drachma currency to pay its bills.

Turkey has blocked access to Twitter and YouTube after refusing to remove pictures of a prosecutor held during an armed siege last week. The prosecutor, Mehmet Selim Kiraz, died in hospital after being taken hostage by the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union, and the US. The government blocked access to social media platforms after images of the hostage-taking were shared, and the prosecutor's wife and children were deeply upset.

A young Star Wars fan, Colin Gilpatric, wrote a letter to George Lucas asking if Jedi Knights could marry. Lucasfilm responded positively, stating that marriage is a value in the Jedi order and can be a path to the light side. Lucasfilm sent Colin a letter and a package of Star Wars merchandise, including books and toys, to ease his mind.

Wisconsin defeated Kentucky in the NCAA basketball tournament semi-finals, ending Kentucky's unbeaten streak. The Badgers will face Duke in the final. Kentucky's unbeaten season ends, and the team finishes the season at 38-1.
Vince Neil, Mötley Crüe's lead singer, was criticized for his rendition of the national anthem at a football game, prompting a comparison to the dangers of tackling the song.

A video of a violent altercation between brothers Patrick and Barry Lyttle, who were reunited for a holiday in Australia, has been released for the first time. The video shows Patrick pushing his brother Barry, who retaliates with a single punch that causes his brother to fall to the ground. Barry is charged with grievous bodily harm and has pleaded guilty. Magistrate Graeme Curran said a jail sentence was likely, and Barry could spend up to two years in a Sydney jail. The brothers were reunited for a night out in Kings Cross, and the video shows them exchanging words before the fight escalated. Patrick was treated by paramedics at the scene and was found in a pool of blood and vomit. The matter returns to court for a possible sentencing hearing on Thursday.

The family of conjoined twin sisters who died 19 days after they were born have been left mortified after they arrived at their gravesite to find cemetery staff had cleared the baby section of all mementos and tossed them in the rubbish.

Lord Neuberger, the President of the Supreme Court, suggested that Muslim women should be allowed to wear a full-face veil while appearing in court, as it shows respect towards different customs. He emphasized the need for judges and courtrooms to be sensitive to the fact that they usually come from a more privileged sector of society and have an understanding of the different cultural and social habits.
Andre Cole, 52, was executed in Missouri for killing a man in a fit of rage over child support payments 16 years ago. He was the third convicted killer put to death this year in Missouri.

Prince Harry will fly out of the UK to Australia without seeing his new niece or nephew, as the Duchess of Cambridge is several days overdue for the birth of her second child. Harry, who will be bumped down to fifth in the line of succession, had returned briefly to hand out prizes at the London Marathon after engagements in Turkey. He was forced to return to Australia for a month-long placement with the army and a week-long official tour of New Zealand.

An alleged fraudster has been accused of posing as Oprah Winfrey, executives from her TV network, former Obama aide Reggie Love and Madonna's manager in an attempt to trick people into giving him jobs, clothes, free food and jewelry worth $2.4million. Justin Jackson, a Florida man, has been carrying out the bizarre schemes in the hope of cashing in on the freebies, or winning himself a job in luxurious hotels, according to court documents.

Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini has slapped a €50million (£36m) price tag on Paulo Dybala, telling Paris Saint-Germain they will have to spend big to sign the 'new Lionel Messi'. A bidding war is set to break out over Dybala, who is being tracked by Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal, Inter Milan, Juventus and PSG.

Hundreds of thousands of Brazilians are protesting against President Dilma Rousseff, who is struggling with an economic downturn and a massive bribery scandal. The protests are calling for Rousseff to be impeached. Petrobras, the state-run oil company, is the center of the scandal, with allegations of a multimillion-dollar kickback scheme. Rousseff has defended Brazilians' right to protest and acknowledged the need to clean up corruption at Petrobras, but has denied any prior knowledge of it. The country was already sharply divided during presidential elections, and participation in the protests has not been consistently strong.

Former Manchester United midfielder Eric Cantona has denied claims he starred in a soft porn film, insisting it is a "piece of art". The French film, You and the Night, has a number of racy scenes, including one in which Cantona is on his hands and knees in just his underwear. However, Cantona says it is not pornography and is instead a "piece of art". The film has been both praised and criticized, with some calling it a "superb artistic orgy" while others describe it as "confusing" and "trashy".

Psychologists have found that certain types of music can enhance the enjoyment of a fish and chip supper, according to a study. The intensity of Nessun Dorma, performed by Luciano Pavarotti, is said to be the perfect accompaniment to dark mouse or coffee, while the high-pitched piano in Billie Holiday's Autumn in New York can help emphasise the autumnal flavour of a pumpkin pudding. The so-called digital seasoning also applies to wine, helping drinkers to enjoy their tipple by up to 15 per cent more, if served alongside the right music.

Raheem Sterling, 20, has been offered a £100, 000-a-week contract by Liverpool, but negotiations have ended in stalemate. Sterling has insisted he is not a 'money grabber' and Taylor, chief executive of the Professional Footballers' Association, believes waiting until the season is over before resuming talks could be a wise move.
